tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

schema.name: mcp__visualize__show_widget
schema.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

=== tests/asd/entra/Test.ASD.ISM-1504.ps1
﻿function Test-MtAsdMfaAllUsers {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that an enabled Conditional Access policy requires multi-factor authentication for all users on all cloud apps.

    .DESCRIPTION
    ISM-1504 (Essential Eight, Multi-factor authentication, Maturity Level One) asks that multi-factor
    authentication is used to authenticate users to the organisation's online services that process, store or
    communicate its sensitive data. ISM-0974 (Maturity Level Two) extends it to unprivileged users of systems.

    The check passes when at least one enabled Conditional Access policy targets all users and all cloud apps
    and grants access only with the built-in MFA control or an authentication strength that satisfies MFA.
    Policies that only act on Identity Protection risk do not count.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtAsdMfaAllUsers

    Returns true when a policy requires MFA for all users on all cloud apps.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/ASD.ISM-1504
    #>
    [Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.SuppressMessageAttribute('PSUseSingularNouns', '', Justification = 'All users is the name of the Conditional Access scope.')]
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'ASD.ISM-1504',
        Title = 'Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate users of the organisation''s online services.',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'conditional-access',
        Area = 'authentication',
        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
        Severity = 'High',
        UserImpact = 'Medium',
        ImplementationCost = 'Medium',
        Mitre = ('T1078.004', 'T1110'),
        Control = ('essential-eight:ISM-1504', 'essential-eight:ISM-0974', 'nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(1)', 'nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(2)'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        License = 'AAD_PREMIUM',
        Author = 'jusso-dev'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    $policies = @(Get-MtAsdMfaPolicy -Scope AllUsers)
    $testResult = $policies.Count -gt 0

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. These Conditional Access policies require multi-factor authentication for all users on all cloud apps:`n`n%TestResult%"
    } else {
        $testResultMarkdown = 'No enabled Conditional Access policy requires multi-factor authentication for all users on all cloud apps.'
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown -GraphObjects $policies -GraphObjectType ConditionalAccess
    return $testResult
}

﻿function Test-MtAsdMfaPrivilegedUsers {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that an enabled Conditional Access policy requires multi-factor authentication for every privileged directory role.

    .DESCRIPTION
    ISM-1173 (Essential Eight, Multi-factor authentication, Maturity Level Two) asks that multi-factor
    authentication is used to authenticate privileged users of systems.

    The check passes when at least one enabled Conditional Access policy targets all cloud apps, covers each of
    the fourteen highly privileged directory roles listed in the guide (by including all users, or by including
    each role without excluding it) and grants access only with the built-in MFA control or an authentication
    strength that satisfies MFA. Other roles that Microsoft Entra marks as privileged are not checked.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtAsdMfaPrivilegedUsers

    Returns true when a policy requires MFA for every privileged role on all cloud apps.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/ASD.ISM-1173
    #>
    [Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.SuppressMessageAttribute('PSUseSingularNouns', '', Justification = 'Privileged users is the subject of the ISM control.')]
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'ASD.ISM-1173',
        Title = 'Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate privileged users.',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'conditional-access',
        Area = 'privileged-access',
        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
        Severity = 'High',
        UserImpact = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre = ('T1078.004', 'T1110'),
        Control = ('essential-eight:ISM-1173', 'nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(1)'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        License = 'AAD_PREMIUM',
        Author = 'jusso-dev'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    $policies = @(Get-MtAsdMfaPolicy -Scope PrivilegedRoles)
    $testResult = $policies.Count -gt 0

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. These Conditional Access policies require multi-factor authentication for every privileged directory role on all cloud apps:`n`n%TestResult%"
    } else {
        $testResultMarkdown = 'No enabled Conditional Access policy requires multi-factor authentication for every privileged directory role on all cloud apps.'
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown -GraphObjects $policies -GraphObjectType ConditionalAccess
    return $testResult
}

=== tests/asd/entra/Test.ASD.ISM-1649.ps1
﻿function Test-MtAsdJustInTimeAdministration {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that privileged directory roles have no permanent active assignments, so that administration is just-in-time.

    .DESCRIPTION
    ISM-1649 (Essential Eight, Restrict administrative privileges, Maturity Level Three) asks that just-in-time
    administration is used for the administration of systems and their resources.

    The check reads the active assignments of every directory role that Microsoft Entra marks as privileged.
    An assignment that has no end date and was not made through an activation is permanent, and fails the
    check; eligible assignments and time-bound active assignments made with Privileged Identity Management
    pass. The emergency access accounts named in the Maester configuration (EmergencyAccessAccounts) are
    left out, because a break glass account is meant to hold its role permanently.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtAsdJustInTimeAdministration

    Returns true when no privileged role has a permanent active assignment outside the emergency access accounts.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/ASD.ISM-1649
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'ASD.ISM-1649',
        Title = 'Just-in-time administration is used for the administration of systems and their resources.',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'privileged-identity-management',
        Area = 'privileged-access',
        ResourceType = 'DirectoryRole',
        Severity = 'High',
        UserImpact = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Medium',
        Mitre = ('T1098.003', 'T1078.004'),
        Control = ('essential-eight:ISM-1649', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-2(7)', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-6(5)'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        License = ('AAD_PREMIUM_P2', 'Entra_Identity_Governance'),
        Author = 'jusso-dev'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    $roles = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'roleManagement/directory/roleDefinitions' -Select id, displayName, isPrivileged | Where-Object { $_.isPrivileged -eq $true })
    $roleName = @{}
    foreach ($role in $roles) { $roleName[$role.id] = $role.displayName }

    # Eligible assignments are read too: EligibleChecked tells whether the PIM APIs answered, which is what makes an assignment just-in-time.
    $read = Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment -ExpandPrincipal
    if (-not $read.EligibleChecked) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason 'Privileged Identity Management is not available in this tenant, so every assignment is permanent. Just-in-time administration needs Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance.'
        return $null
    }
    $breakGlass = @(Get-MtEmergencyAccessAccount | ForEach-Object ObjectId)

    $permanent = @($read.Assignments | Where-Object {
            $_.AssignmentType -eq 'Active' -and
            $roleName.ContainsKey($_.roleDefinitionId) -and
            [string]::IsNullOrEmpty($_.endDateTime) -and
            $_.principalId -notin $breakGlass
        })
    $testResult = $permanent.Count -eq 0

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. No privileged directory role has a permanent active assignment. $($roles.Count) privileged roles were checked$(if ($breakGlass.Count -gt 0) { ", leaving out $($breakGlass.Count) emergency access account(s)" })."
    } else {
        $table = "| Role | Principal | Type | Scope |`n| --- | --- | --- | --- |`n"
        foreach ($assignment in ($permanent | Sort-Object { $roleName[$_.roleDefinitionId] }, { $_.principal.displayName })) {
            $principal = $assignment.principal
            $name = if ($principal.userPrincipalName) { $principal.userPrincipalName } elseif ($principal.displayName) { $principal.displayName } else { $assignment.principalId }
            $type = ([string]$principal.'@odata.type') -replace '^#microsoft\.graph\.', ''
            $table += "| $($roleName[$assignment.roleDefinitionId]) | $name | $type | $($assignment.directoryScopeId) |`n"
        }
        $testResultMarkdown = "$($permanent.Count) permanent active assignment(s) to privileged directory roles were found. Make them eligible in Privileged Identity Management so that administrators activate the role when they need it.`n`n$table"
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}
=== tests/asd/entra/Test.ASD.ISM-1403.ps1
﻿function Test-MtAsdSmartLockoutThreshold {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that the Microsoft Entra smart lockout threshold is five failed sign-ins or fewer.

    .DESCRIPTION
    ISM-1403 (Guidelines for system access, User account lockouts) asks that user accounts, except for break
    glass accounts, are protected by fixed or risk-based lockout mechanisms aligned to a maximum of five failed
    logon attempts. This control is not part of the Essential Eight Maturity Model.

    Microsoft Entra smart lockout locks an account for the lockout duration after the configured number of
    failed sign-ins, and tracks familiar and unfamiliar locations separately. The check reads the tenant's
    Password Rule Settings and passes when the lockout threshold is explicitly set to the maximum given
    (5 by default) or fewer. The Microsoft default of 10 fails.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtAsdSmartLockoutThreshold

    Returns true when the smart lockout threshold is 5 or fewer.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/ASD.ISM-1403
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'ASD.ISM-1403',
        Title = 'User accounts are protected by lockout mechanisms aligned to a maximum of five failed logon attempts.',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'password-protection',
        Area = 'authentication',
        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
        Severity = 'Medium',
        UserImpact = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre = 'T1110',
        Control = ('ism:ISM-1403', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-7'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        License = 'AAD_PREMIUM',
        Author = 'jusso-dev'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # The most failed sign-ins allowed before an account is locked.
        [ValidateRange(1, 50)]
        [int] $MaximumFailedAttempts = 5
    )

    $settings = Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'settings' -ApiVersion beta
    $rawValue = $settings.values | Where-Object name -EQ 'LockoutThreshold' | Select-Object -First 1 -ExpandProperty value
    $isSet = -not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace([string]$rawValue)
    $threshold = if ($isSet) { [int]$rawValue } else { 10 }
    $testResult = $isSet -and $threshold -le $MaximumFailedAttempts

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. The smart lockout threshold is **$threshold** failed sign-ins, which is $MaximumFailedAttempts or fewer."
    } elseif (-not $isSet) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "The smart lockout threshold is not set explicitly, so the Microsoft default of **10** failed sign-ins applies. Set it to **$MaximumFailedAttempts** or fewer."
    } else {
        $testResultMarkdown = "The smart lockout threshold is **$threshold** failed sign-ins. Set it to **$MaximumFailedAttempts** or fewer."
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}
=== tests/asd/entra/Test.ASD.ISM-1648.ps1
﻿function Test-MtAsdInactivePrivilegedAccess {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that no enabled account with a privileged directory role has been inactive for 45 days or more.

    .DESCRIPTION
    ISM-1648 (Essential Eight, Restrict administrative privileges, Maturity Level Two) asks that privileged
    access to systems and their resources is disabled after 45 days of inactivity.

    The check lists the users with an active or eligible assignment to a directory role that Microsoft Entra
    marks as privileged, and reads the last sign-in of each. A user fails when the account is enabled and the
    most recent interactive or non-interactive sign-in is older than the number of days given (45 by
    default), or when the account has never signed in and was created before that. The emergency access
    accounts named in the Maester configuration (EmergencyAccessAccounts) are left out, because they are
    meant to stay unused.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtAsdInactivePrivilegedAccess

    Returns true when every enabled privileged user signed in within the last 45 days.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/ASD.ISM-1648
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'ASD.ISM-1648',
        Title = 'Privileged access to systems and their resources is disabled after 45 days of inactivity.',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'roles',
        Area = 'privileged-access',
        ResourceType = 'User',
        Severity = 'High',
        UserImpact = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre = 'T1078.004',
        Control = ('essential-eight:ISM-1648', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-2(3)'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        License = 'AAD_PREMIUM',
        Author = 'jusso-dev'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # Days without a sign-in after which privileged access must be disabled.
        [ValidateRange(1, 365)]
        [int] $InactiveDays = 45
    )

    $rolesOf = Get-MtAsdPrivilegedUser
    if ($rolesOf.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause NotApplicable
        return $null
    }

    $cutoff = [datetime]::UtcNow.AddDays(-$InactiveDays)
    $users = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'users' -UniqueId @($rolesOf.Keys) -Select id, userPrincipalName, displayName, accountEnabled, createdDateTime, signInActivity)
    $inactive = foreach ($user in $users) {
        if ($user.accountEnabled -ne $true) { continue }
        $signIns = @($user.signInActivity.lastSignInDateTime, $user.signInActivity.lastNonInteractiveSignInDateTime | Where-Object { $_ } | ForEach-Object { [datetime]$_ })
        $lastSignIn = if ($signIns.Count -gt 0) { ($signIns | Measure-Object -Maximum).Maximum.ToUniversalTime() } else { $null }
        $isInactive = if ($lastSignIn) { $lastSignIn -lt $cutoff } else { $user.createdDateTime -and ([datetime]$user.createdDateTime).ToUniversalTime() -lt $cutoff }
        if ($isInactive) {
            [pscustomobject]@{
                id                = $user.id
                displayName       = $user.displayName
                userPrincipalName = $user.userPrincipalName
                LastSignIn        = if ($lastSignIn) { $lastSignIn.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd') } else { 'Never' }
                Roles             = $rolesOf[$user.id] -join ', '
            }
        }
    }
    $inactive = @($inactive)
    $testResult = $inactive.Count -eq 0

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. Every enabled user with a privileged directory role signed in within the last $InactiveDays days ($($rolesOf.Count) users checked)."
    } else {
        $table = "| User | Last sign-in | Privileged roles |`n| --- | --- | --- |`n"

=== tests/asd/entra/Test.ASD.ISM-1649.ps1
﻿function Test-MtAsdJustInTimeAdministration {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that privileged directory roles have no permanent active assignments, so that administration is just-in-time.

    .DESCRIPTION
    ISM-1649 (Essential Eight, Restrict administrative privileges, Maturity Level Three) asks that just-in-time
    administration is used for the administration of systems and their resources.

    The check reads the active assignments of every directory role that Microsoft Entra marks as privileged.
    An assignment that has no end date and was not made through an activation is permanent, and fails the
    check; eligible assignments and time-bound active assignments made with Privileged Identity Management
    pass. The emergency access accounts named in the Maester configuration (EmergencyAccessAccounts) are
    left out, because a break glass account is meant to hold its role permanently.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtAsdJustInTimeAdministration

    Returns true when no privileged role has a permanent active assignment outside the emergency access accounts.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/ASD.ISM-1649
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'ASD.ISM-1649',
        Title = 'Just-in-time administration is used for the administration of systems and their resources.',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'privileged-identity-management',
        Area = 'privileged-access',
        ResourceType = 'DirectoryRole',
        Severity = 'High',
        UserImpact = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Medium',
        Mitre = ('T1098.003', 'T1078.004'),
        Control = ('essential-eight:ISM-1649', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-2(7)', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-6(5)'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        License = ('AAD_PREMIUM_P2', 'Entra_Identity_Governance'),
        Author = 'jusso-dev'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    $roles = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'roleManagement/directory/roleDefinitions' -Select id, displayName, isPrivileged | Where-Object { $_.isPrivileged -eq $true })
    $roleName = @{}
    foreach ($role in $roles) { $roleName[$role.id] = $role.displayName }

    # Eligible assignments are read too: EligibleChecked tells whether the PIM APIs answered, which is what makes an assignment just-in-time.
    $read = Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment -ExpandPrincipal
    if (-not $read.EligibleChecked) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason 'Privileged Identity Management is not available in this tenant, so every assignment is permanent. Just-in-time administration needs Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance.'
        return $null
    }
    $breakGlass = @(Get-MtEmergencyAccessAccount | ForEach-Object ObjectId)

    $permanent = @($read.Assignments | Where-Object {
            $_.AssignmentType -eq 'Active' -and
            $roleName.ContainsKey($_.roleDefinitionId) -and
            [string]::IsNullOrEmpty($_.endDateTime) -and
            $_.principalId -notin $breakGlass
        })
    $testResult = $permanent.Count -eq 0

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. No privileged directory role has a permanent active assignment. $($roles.Count) privileged roles were checked$(if ($breakGlass.Count -gt 0) { ", leaving out $($breakGlass.Count) emergency access account(s)" })."
    } else {
        $table = "| Role | Principal | Type | Scope |`n| --- | --- | --- | --- |`n"
        foreach ($assignment in ($permanent | Sort-Object { $roleName[$_.roleDefinitionId] }, { $_.principal.displayName })) {
            $principal = $assignment.principal
            $name = if ($principal.userPrincipalName) { $principal.userPrincipalName } elseif ($principal.displayName) { $principal.displayName } else { $assignment.principalId }
            $type = ([string]$principal.'@odata.type') -replace '^#microsoft\.graph\.', ''
            $table += "| $($roleName[$assignment.roleDefinitionId]) | $name | $type | $($assignment.directoryScopeId) |`n"
        }
        $testResultMarkdown = "$($permanent.Count) permanent active assignment(s) to privileged directory roles were found. Make them eligible in Privileged Identity Management so that administrators activate the role when they need it.`n`n$table"
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}

﻿function Test-MtAsdSmartLockoutThreshold {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that the Microsoft Entra smart lockout threshold is five failed sign-ins or fewer.

    .DESCRIPTION
    ISM-1403 (Guidelines for system access, User account lockouts) asks that user accounts, except for break
    glass accounts, are protected by fixed or risk-based lockout mechanisms aligned to a maximum of five failed
    logon attempts. This control is not part of the Essential Eight Maturity Model.

    Microsoft Entra smart lockout locks an account for the lockout duration after the configured number of
    failed sign-ins, and tracks familiar and unfamiliar locations separately. The check reads the tenant's
    Password Rule Settings and passes when the lockout threshold is explicitly set to the maximum given
    (5 by default) or fewer. The Microsoft default of 10 fails.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtAsdSmartLockoutThreshold

    Returns true when the smart lockout threshold is 5 or fewer.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/ASD.ISM-1403
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'ASD.ISM-1403',
        Title = 'User accounts are protected by lockout mechanisms aligned to a maximum of five failed logon attempts.',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'password-protection',
        Area = 'authentication',
        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
        Severity = 'Medium',
        UserImpact = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre = 'T1110',
        Control = ('ism:ISM-1403', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-7'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        License = 'AAD_PREMIUM',
        Author = 'jusso-dev'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # The most failed sign-ins allowed before an account is locked.
        [ValidateRange(1, 50)]
        [int] $MaximumFailedAttempts = 5
    )

    $settings = Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'settings' -ApiVersion beta
    $rawValue = $settings.values | Where-Object name -EQ 'LockoutThreshold' | Select-Object -First 1 -ExpandProperty value
    $isSet = -not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace([string]$rawValue)
    $threshold = if ($isSet) { [int]$rawValue } else { 10 }
    $testResult = $isSet -and $threshold -le $MaximumFailedAttempts

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. The smart lockout threshold is **$threshold** failed sign-ins, which is $MaximumFailedAttempts or fewer."
    } elseif (-not $isSet) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "The smart lockout threshold is not set explicitly, so the Microsoft default of **10** failed sign-ins applies. Set it to **$MaximumFailedAttempts** or fewer."
    } else {
        $testResultMarkdown = "The smart lockout threshold is **$threshold** failed sign-ins. Set it to **$MaximumFailedAttempts** or fewer."
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}
=== tests/asd/entra/Test.ASD.ISM-1648.ps1
﻿function Test-MtAsdInactivePrivilegedAccess {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that no enabled account with a privileged directory role has been inactive for 45 days or more.

    .DESCRIPTION
    ISM-1648 (Essential Eight, Restrict administrative privileges, Maturity Level Two) asks that privileged
    access to systems and their resources is disabled after 45 days of inactivity.

    The check lists the users with an active or eligible assignment to a directory role that Microsoft Entra
    marks as privileged, and reads the last sign-in of each. A user fails when the account is enabled and the
    most recent interactive or non-interactive sign-in is older than the number of days given (45 by
    default), or when the account has never signed in and was created before that. The emergency access
    accounts named in the Maester configuration (EmergencyAccessAccounts) are left out, because they are
    meant to stay unused.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtAsdInactivePrivilegedAccess

    Returns true when every enabled privileged user signed in within the last 45 days.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/ASD.ISM-1648
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'ASD.ISM-1648',
        Title = 'Privileged access to systems and their resources is disabled after 45 days of inactivity.',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'roles',
        Area = 'privileged-access',
        ResourceType = 'User',
        Severity = 'High',
        UserImpact = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre = 'T1078.004',
        Control = ('essential-eight:ISM-1648', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-2(3)'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        License = 'AAD_PREMIUM',
        Author = 'jusso-dev'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # Days without a sign-in after which privileged access must be disabled.
        [ValidateRange(1, 365)]
        [int] $InactiveDays = 45
    )

    $rolesOf = Get-MtAsdPrivilegedUser
    if ($rolesOf.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause NotApplicable
        return $null
    }

    $cutoff = [datetime]::UtcNow.AddDays(-$InactiveDays)
    $users = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'users' -UniqueId @($rolesOf.Keys) -Select id, userPrincipalName, displayName, accountEnabled, createdDateTime, signInActivity)
    $inactive = foreach ($user in $users) {
        if ($user.accountEnabled -ne $true) { continue }
        $signIns = @($user.signInActivity.lastSignInDateTime, $user.signInActivity.lastNonInteractiveSignInDateTime | Where-Object { $_ } | ForEach-Object { [datetime]$_ })
        $lastSignIn = if ($signIns.Count -gt 0) { ($signIns | Measure-Object -Maximum).Maximum.ToUniversalTime() } else { $null }
        $isInactive = if ($lastSignIn) { $lastSignIn -lt $cutoff } else { $user.createdDateTime -and ([datetime]$user.createdDateTime).ToUniversalTime() -lt $cutoff }
        if ($isInactive) {
            [pscustomobject]@{
                id                = $user.id
                displayName       = $user.displayName
                userPrincipalName = $user.userPrincipalName
                LastSignIn        = if ($lastSignIn) { $lastSignIn.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd') } else { 'Never' }
                Roles             = $rolesOf[$user.id] -join ', '
            }
        }
    }
    $inactive = @($inactive)
    $testResult = $inactive.Count -eq 0

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. Every enabled user with a privileged directory role signed in within the last $InactiveDays days ($($rolesOf.Count) users checked)."
    } else {
        $table = "| User | Last sign-in | Privileged roles |`n| --- | --- | --- |`n"
        foreach ($user in ($inactive | Sort-Object userPrincipalName)) { $table += "| $($user.userPrincipalName) | $($user.LastSignIn) | $($user.Roles) |`n" }
        $testResultMarkdown = "$($inactive.Count) enabled user(s) with a privileged directory role have not signed in for $InactiveDays days or more. Disable the account or remove the role, and let an access review or a PIM alert catch the next one.`n`n$table"
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}

        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. None of the $($rolesOf.Count) users with a privileged directory role has an Exchange Online mailbox."
    } else {
        $table = "| User | Privileged roles |`n| --- | --- |`n"
        foreach ($user in ($withMailbox | Sort-Object userPrincipalName)) { $table += "| $($user.userPrincipalName) | $($user.Roles) |`n" }
        $testResultMarkdown = "$($withMailbox.Count) of $($rolesOf.Count) users with a privileged directory role have an Exchange Online mailbox. Give each administrator a separate, unlicensed account for privileged duties and move the role to it.`n`n$table"
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}

I searched once. The results cover the three controls and how they fit the Essential Eight, but not the system hardening guidelines document itself.

- **ISM-1504** covers MFA for users of their organisation's own online services that handle sensitive data. The cyber.gov.au Essential Eight and ISM mapping lists it as the Essential Eight MFA item for online services. (Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate users to their organisation's online services that process, store or communicate their organisation's sensitive data.)
- **ISM-1173** covers privileged users. It applies MFA to accounts with elevated access to systems. (Multifactor authentication is used to authenticate privileged users of systems.)
- **ISM-1872** requires the MFA used for online services to be phishing-resistant. Its change history says it was amended in December 2023 so that it applies to users rather than customers. Customers have their own control, ISM-1873, which provides a phishing-resistant option. (The existing control relating to phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication being used for online services was amended to reflect that it relates to users (but not customers).)

A Microsoft guide maps these controls to implementation steps, such as a conditional access policy that requires MFA and, for ISM-1872, a phishing-resistant authentication strength. (Create conditional access policy requiring multifactor authentication and requiring a phishing resistant authentication strength.)

The results don't include the cyber.gov.au system hardening guidelines. For those, go to cyber.gov.au and search for the Information Security Manual (ISM) or its hardening guidance directly.

input.description: ISM and Essential Eight text
input.prompt:
Research task (read-only, no code changes). I'm reviewing a Maester PR that adds Microsoft 365 checks for Australia's ASD Essential Eight and ISM controls. I need the authoritative ASD wording for each control so I can tell whether ASD specifies implementation details (e.g. which roles count as privileged, whether a specific authentication strength is required, what counts as "permanent", a numeric threshold, which apps/rules) or stays at the level of a generic outcome.

Controls: ISM-1504, ISM-0974, ISM-1173, ISM-1872, ISM-1649, ISM-1648, ISM-0445, ISM-1175, ISM-1403, ISM-1488, ISM-1672, ISM-1673, ISM-1654, ISM-1667, ISM-1668, ISM-1669, ISM-1695.

Sources, in order of authority:
1. The ISM itself on cyber.gov.au (current release; it's published as "Guidelines for ..." chapters, and also as OSCAL/XML/Excel downloads at https://www.cyber.gov.au/resources-business-and-government/essential-cyber-security/ism and the GitHub repo AustralianCyberSecurityCentre/ism-oscal). The OSCAL JSON on GitHub is the easiest way to get exact control text.
2. The Essential Eight Maturity Model (cyber.gov.au) and the "Essential Eight maturity model and ISM mapping" publication, including which maturity level each control sits at.
3. "Essential Eight assessment process guide" (cyber.gov.au), which tells assessors what evidence to look for and what test methods to use for each control. This is the key source for implementation specifics, e.g. how "privileged" is defined, what "phishing-resistant" means, how lockout is tested.
4. The ISM's own definitions/glossary for terms like "privileged user", "phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication", "just-in-time administration", "online services".

Third-party sites (myctrl.tools, ismcontrol.pages.dev, Microsoft Learn) are fine for finding things but quote ASD's own documents for the answer, and say when you could only find a third-party copy.

For each control return:
- the exact control text (verbatim) and the ISM release/date you read it from;
- its Essential Eight strategy and maturity level (or "not in Essential Eight");
- any ASD-specified detail that goes beyond the control text: definitions, assessment-guide test methods, thresholds, lists. Quote it verbatim with the URL/document and section;
- one line: "Specific" or "Generic", meaning whether ASD tells you how to implement/measure it in a way that would decide between two implementations (examples of what the two implementations disagree on: whether only permanent active role assignments fail vs any active assignment; whether a CA policy must target "all users" or just a set of admin roles and which roles; whether phishing resistance is judged by the built-in "Phishing-resistant MFA" authentication strength or by allowed methods; lockout threshold 5 vs 10; whether "privileged" means Entra's isPrivileged roles or a fixed list).

Also report specifically:
- How ASD defines "privileged user" / "privileged access" (does it list roles?).
- What ASD considers phishing-resistant MFA (which methods).
- Whether ISM-1649 "just-in-time" is defined, and whether time-bound active assignments are acceptable.
- Whether ISM-1403's "five failed logon attempts" applies to cloud identity smart lockout and whether risk-based lockout counts.
- For ISM-1667/1668/1669/1488/1672/1673/1654/1695: the exact text and any specific settings ASD names (e.g. ASR rule names, macro settings).

Keep the report factual and compact, with URLs for every quote. Don't speculate about Maester code.

input.description: ASD Blueprint Entra/Intune settings
input.prompt:
Research task (read-only, no code changes). I'm reviewing a Maester PR that adds Microsoft 365 checks for Australia's ASD Essential Eight and ISM controls. I need to know exactly what the ASD Blueprint for Secure Cloud (https://blueprint.asd.gov.au/) and ASD's Microsoft hardening guides prescribe, so I can tell whether ASD specifies settings that differ from CIS Microsoft 365 / CISA SCuBA, or leaves them generic.

Site map (found already): /configuration/entra-id/, /configuration/entra-id/protection/conditional-access/policies/, /configuration/entra-id/protection/conditional-access/authentication-strengths/, /configuration/entra-id/protection/authentication-methods/, /configuration/entra-id/protection/authentication-methods/password-protection/, /design/platform/identity/conditional-access/, /design/platform/identity/tenant/, /configuration/intune/endpoint-security/attack-surface-reduction/, /configuration/intune/devices/configuration-policies/ (including asd-office-hardening-all-macros-disabled and asd-office-hardening-macros-enabled-for-trusted-publishers), /design/endpoints/windows/configuration/windows-update-and-patching/, /design/platform/client/device-updates/, /security-and-governance/ (Essential Eight pages). Also look for privileged access / PIM / roles pages anywhere under /configuration/entra-id/ or /design/platform/identity/ (try identity governance, roles and administrators, privileged identity management). The blueprint is also on GitHub (search for the ASD Blueprint for Secure Cloud repository) which may be easier to read.

Also check ASD's hardening publications on cyber.gov.au: "Hardening Microsoft Windows 10 and Windows 11 workstations", "Microsoft Office macro security", "Restricting Microsoft Office macros", "Hardening Microsoft 365, Office 2021, Office 2019 and Office 2016".

For each topic, quote the specific settings verbatim (with URL) and say what they are:
1. Conditional Access: the list of policies the blueprint defines (names and what each targets/grants). Specifically: is there an "MFA for all users" policy, what users/apps it targets and exclusions; is there a separate admin policy and which roles it targets (list them); does it use the built-in "Phishing-resistant MFA" authentication strength or a custom one, and for whom (all users or admins).
2. Authentication strengths: which methods the blueprint allows.
3. Privileged access: does the blueprint require PIM, eligible-only assignments, time-bound active assignments, activation duration, approval; separate admin accounts without mailboxes/licences; cloud-only admin accounts; inactivity disabling (45 days?) or access reviews.
4. Smart lockout / password protection: the lockout threshold and duration values it sets.
5. Intune ASR: which ASR rules it sets and in what mode (block/audit/warn); specifically rules for Office apps creating child processes, Office creating executable content, Office injecting into other processes, Win32 API calls from Office macros, and any others.
6. Office macros: the settings for "block macros from the internet", "VBA macros notification", macro antivirus scanning, trusted publishers, Win32 API.
7. Internet Explorer 11: disabled or removed, and how (setting name).
8. Windows Update rings / patching: deadlines/days (quality, feature), grace periods, which Intune setting.

Return a compact report organised by those 8 topics, verbatim quotes with URLs, and a final list of every place where the blueprint names a concrete value (a number, a role list, an authentication strength, a rule mode). Say clearly when the blueprint is silent on something. Don't speculate about Maester code.

toolUseResult.prompt:
Research task (read-only, no code changes). I'm reviewing a Maester PR that adds Microsoft 365 checks for Australia's ASD Essential Eight and ISM controls. I need the authoritative ASD wording for each control so I can tell whether ASD specifies implementation details (e.g. which roles count as privileged, whether a specific authentication strength is required, what counts as "permanent", a numeric threshold, which apps/rules) or stays at the level of a generic outcome.

Controls: ISM-1504, ISM-0974, ISM-1173, ISM-1872, ISM-1649, ISM-1648, ISM-0445, ISM-1175, ISM-1403, ISM-1488, ISM-1672, ISM-1673, ISM-1654, ISM-1667, ISM-1668, ISM-1669, ISM-1695.

Sources, in order of authority:
1. The ISM itself on cyber.gov.au (current release; it's published as "Guidelines for ..." chapters, and also as OSCAL/XML/Excel downloads at https://www.cyber.gov.au/resources-business-and-government/essential-cyber-security/ism and the GitHub repo AustralianCyberSecurityCentre/ism-oscal). The OSCAL JSON on GitHub is the easiest way to get exact control text.
2. The Essential Eight Maturity Model (cyber.gov.au) and the "Essential Eight maturity model and ISM mapping" publication, including which maturity level each control sits at.
3. "Essential Eight assessment process guide" (cyber.gov.au), which tells assessors what evidence to look for and what test methods to use for each control. This is the key source for implementation specifics, e.g. how "privileged" is defined, what "phishing-resistant" means, how lockout is tested.
4. The ISM's own definitions/glossary for terms like "privileged user", "phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication", "just-in-time administration", "online services".

Third-party sites (myctrl.tools, ismcontrol.pages.dev, Microsoft Learn) are fine for finding things but quote ASD's own documents for the answer, and say when you could only find a third-party copy.

For each control return:
- the exact control text (verbatim) and the ISM release/date you read it from;
- its Essential Eight strategy and maturity level (or "not in Essential Eight");
- any ASD-specified detail that goes beyond the control text: definitions, assessment-guide test methods, thresholds, lists. Quote it verbatim with the URL/document and section;
- one line: "Specific" or "Generic", meaning whether ASD tells you how to implement/measure it in a way that would decide between two implementations (examples of what the two implementations disagree on: whether only permanent active role assignments fail vs any active assignment; whether a CA policy must target "all users" or just a set of admin roles and which roles; whether phishing resistance is judged by the built-in "Phishing-resistant MFA" authentication strength or by allowed methods; lockout threshold 5 vs 10; whether "privileged" means Entra's isPrivileged roles or a fixed list).

Also report specifically:
- How ASD defines "privileged user" / "privileged access" (does it list roles?).
- What ASD considers phishing-resistant MFA (which methods).
- Whether ISM-1649 "just-in-time" is defined, and whether time-bound active assignments are acceptable.
- Whether ISM-1403's "five failed logon attempts" applies to cloud identity smart lockout and whether risk-based lockout counts.
- For ISM-1667/1668/1669/1488/1672/1673/1654/1695: the exact text and any specific settings ASD names (e.g. ASR rule names, macro settings).

Keep the report factual and compact, with URLs for every quote. Don't speculate about Maester code.
