  # What ASD specifies for the Essential Eight and ISM M365 checks
  
  **Sources read:**
  - The Blueprint GitHub repo (github.com/ASD-Blueprint/ASD-Blueprint-for-Secure-Cloud, HEAD a6e1e5f, 18 Sep 2026). Live pages at blueprint.asd.gov.au were spot-checked and match it. URLs below are `https://blueprint.asd.gov.au/<path>/`.
  - cyber.gov.au:
    - *Hardening Microsoft Windows 11 workstations*, last reviewed 23 Jan 2026 (the Windows 10 version, 4 Sep 2025, has the same ASR and IE text).
    - *Hardening Microsoft 365, Office 2021, Office 2019 and Office 2016*, 24 Jul 2023.
    - *Restricting Microsoft Office macros*, 27 Nov 2023. The "Microsoft Office macro security" URL now redirects here.
    - *Essential Eight maturity model*, 27 Nov 2023.
  
  **Caveats that apply throughout:**
  - Every Blueprint config page carries this disclaimer: "Any implementation implied by these pages should not be considered as prescriptive as to how an organisation must scope, build, document, or assess a system."
  - The CA policies index page says: "All Conditional Access policies in the DSC are set to report only and will need to be enabled manually." The individual policy pages say "Enable policy | On".
  
  ---
  
  ## 1. Conditional Access
  
  The policy pages are under `/configuration/entra-id/protection/conditional-access/policies/`. There are 16 policies:
  
  | Policy | Users | Resources | Control |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | USR - G - Require strong auth | All users | All resources | Built-in "Phishing-resistant MFA" |
  | USR - G - Register security info with strong auth | All users | User action "Register security information" | Custom "Phishing-resistant MFA and TAP" |
  | USR - G - Risky sign-ins with strong auth | All users, sign-in risk Low + Medium | All resources | Phishing-resistant MFA |
  | USR - B - Block high-risk sign-ins | All users, sign-in risk High | All resources | Block |
  | USR - B - Block high-risk users | All users, user risk High | All resources | Block |
  | USR - B - Block users with elevated insider risk | All users, insider risk Elevated | All resources | Block |
  | USR - B - Block access via legacy auth | All users, client apps "Exchange ActiveSync clients" + "Other clients" | All resources | Block |
  | USR - B - Block access to PROTECTED information | `<PROTECTED users group>` excluded | Authentication context "PROTECTED information" | Block |
  | USR - G - Agreement to terms of use | All users | All resources | Terms |
  | USR - S - Limit user sessions | All users, excluding admin roles and `<Administrative user group>` | All resources | Sign-in frequency 12 hours |
  | ADM - S - Limit admin sessions | Admin roles + `<Administrative user group>` | All resources | Sign-in frequency 4 hours |
  | DEV - G - Compliant devices | All users | All resources | Require device to be marked as compliant |
  | DEV - B - Block access from unapproved devices | All users; platforms Android, Windows Phone, macOS, Linux | All resources | Block |
  | DEV - G - Intune enrolment with strong auth | All users | Microsoft Intune + Microsoft Intune Enrolment | Phishing-resistant MFA |
  | GST - B - Block guests | All 6 guest/external types, excluding `<Guest application user group>` | All resources | Block |
  | GST - G - Guest `<application>` access with strong auth | Guests | `<application>` | Phishing-resistant MFA |
  | LOC - B - Block access from unapproved countries | All users | All resources | Block, excluding "Allowed Countries" |
  
  **The "MFA for all users" policy.** On `.../policies/strong-authentication/`:
  - "Include | All users"
  - Exclude: "Users and groups | Checked | `<CA exclude group - USR - G - Require strong auth>`"
  - "Guest or external users | Not checked" and "Directory roles | Not checked" (under Exclude)
  - "All resources (formerly 'All cloud apps')", with "Exclude | None"
  - "Require multifactor authentication | Not checked"
  - "Require authentication strength | Phishing-resistant MFA: Checked"
  
  So the built-in strength applies to **all users**.
  
  On `/design/platform/identity/conditional-access/`:
  - "Require strong authentication for users | Enforce phishing-resistant MFA for all users"
  - "Authentication strengths for user access | Use phishing-resistant MFA | Comply with Essential Eight requirements"
  
  **Exclusions** (same design page):
  - "Use separate exclude groups for each Conditional Access policy"
  - "Use Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for exclude group membership changes"
  - "Exclude Break glass accounts from Conditional Access policy control"
  
  **There is no separate admin MFA policy.** The only ADM policy is the 4-hour session policy. On `.../policies/limit-admin-sessions/`:
  - "Directory roles | Checked | _Select applicable administrator roles_" plus `<Administrative user group>`
  - "Periodic reauthentication | 4 hours"
  - No grant control
  
  The page does not name the roles. The design page says: "Use groups as well as roles to identity administrative users".
  
  The Microsoft-managed policies are all set Off as "superseded by Blueprint policies". They include "Multifactor authentication for admins accessing Microsoft Admin Portals", "Require multifactor authentication for admins" and "Require multifactor authentication for all users".
  
  On `/design/platform/identity/authentication/`: "MFA for Administration | Configured | Administration through Microsoft 365 administration portals and other Cloud Apps should require MFA."
  
  **The only concrete admin role list is in the DSC file** (`/content/files/automation/dsc/BlueprintEntraDsc.txt`, Microsoft365DSC 1.24.717.1). Its `ADM - S - Limit admin sessions` IncludeRoles (and `USR - S` ExcludeRoles) lists 73 roles: essentially every "... Administrator" role, Global Administrator included, plus `$PrivUsers`.
  
  The DSC also disagrees with the docs in places:
  - `ADM - S - Limit admin sessions` and `DEV - G - Compliant devices` have `IncludeApplications = @("None")`, where the pages say "All resources".
  - Every DSC policy is `State = "enabledForReportingButNotEnforced"`.
  
  ## 2. Authentication strengths
  
  **The one custom strength.** On `/configuration/entra-id/protection/conditional-access/authentication-strengths/`:
  - Name: "Phishing-resistant MFA and TAP"
  - Phishing-resistant MFA: "Windows Hello For Business / Passkeys (FIDO2) / Certificate-based Authentication (Multifactor)"
  - Multifactor authentication: "Temporary Access Pass (One-time use) / Temporary Access Pass (Multi-use)"
  
  Only the Register security info policy uses it. Every other grant uses the built-in "Phishing-resistant MFA". Design page: "Authentication strengths for bootstrapping flows | Use phishing-resistant MFA plus temporary access passes (TAPs)".
  
  **Authentication methods policy** (`/configuration/entra-id/protection/authentication-methods/policies/`):
  - Enabled for "All users, excluding `<Conditional Access excluded identities>`": Passkey (FIDO2), Microsoft Authenticator, Temporary Access Pass.
  - Disabled ("No"): SMS, Hardware OATH, Third-party software OATH, Voice call, Email OTP, Certificate-based authentication. Note that CBA is disabled here although the custom strength includes it.
  - FIDO2: "Enforce attestation | Yes", "Enforce key restrictions | Yes", "Restrict specific keys | Allow", `<Organisation AAGUIDs>`.
  - Authenticator: "Allow use of Microsoft Authenticator OTP | No", "Require number matching ... | Enabled".
  - TAP: "Minimum lifetime | 1 hour", "Maximum lifetime | 8 hours", "Default lifetime | 1 hour", "One-time | No", "Length | 15 characters".
  
  **Design guidance** (`/design/platform/identity/authentication/`):
  - ML2/ML3: "FIDO2 Key / Windows Hello for Business (Pin Only) on organisational devices", with "Alternative Methods | Temporary Access Pass".
  - "Microsoft Authenticator is not phishing resistant."
  
  **Per-user MFA service settings** (`/configuration/entra-id/users/per-user-mfa/`):
  - "Do not allow users to create app passwords..."
  - "Remember multi-factor authentication on trusted device | Not checked"
  
  **Windows 11 hardening guide:** "hardware-based multi-factor authentication should be used for privileged users, remote access and any access to important or sensitive data repositories."
  
  ## 3. Privileged access
  
  **PIM design** (`/design/platform/identity/roles/`), verbatim decision table:
  - "Role activation model | Least Privilege via Privileged Identity Management"
  - "PIM role scope | All Entra roles"
  - "Approval workflow | Align approval requirements with the risk of each role's capabilities" (no fixed approval rule)
  - "Assignment type | Eligible assignment"
  - "Assignment duration | Maximum 365 days"
  - "Activation duration | Capped at 8 hours and restricted to the minimum necessary duration"
  - "Standing access exceptions | Permanent active assignment for break glass and specific service accounts"
  
  `/design/shared-services/microsoft-365/rbac/` adds "PIM | Configured" and lists the M365 roles PIM can assign.
  
  **Access reviews** (`/design/platform/identity/governance/`):
  - "Use 6-monthly access reviews for active and eligible assigned roles"
  - "Use 3-monthly access reviews for Conditional Access exclude groups"
  - "Use 6-monthly access reviews for role assigned groups"
  - "Access reviews for inactive users ... are not in implemented in the Blueprint."
  
  **Inactivity** (`/design/platform/identity/users/`): "ISM Security Controls 1404 and 1648 | Disable un-privileged and privileged user accounts after > 45 days of inactivity", done by "a custom script set to run on a scheduled basis". This conflicts with the E8 page (`/security-and-governance/essential-eight/restrict-administrative-privileges/`): "The Blueprint does not currently provide guidance for automating the disabling of accounts."
  
  **Break glass accounts** (same users page; config page `/configuration/entra-id/users/break-glass-accounts/`):
  - Two accounts, "cloud only accounts that use the `*.onmicrosoft.com` domain".
  - "Global Administrator role assigned permanently".
  - "Both Emergency access accounts will be excluded from MFA". The page's own bullet list instead says "At least one".
  - Monitored "via Defender for Cloud Apps".
  
  **Separate admin accounts:**
  - SSP template (`/security-and-governance/system-security-plan/personnel-security/`): "privileged users granted additional uniquely identifiable privileged accounts".
  - Same template: "an AppLocker blocklist is configured on workstations via Intune to prevent administrators from launching web browsers and email clients".
  - E8 page: "The Blueprint does not currently provide guidance for restricting privileged account activities." Its template text says privileged accounts "are restricted from accessing the internet, email and web services".
  
  **Silent on:**
  - Admin accounts without mailboxes or licences. `/design/shared-services/microsoft-365/licencing/` actually defines "Admin Licence Group | `rol-OrganisationName-Administrator`".
  - Cloud-only admin accounts other than break glass.
  
  **cyber.gov.au:**
  - Windows 11 guide: "separate standard and privileged accounts with different credentials ... privileged accounts used should have external web and email access blocked."
  - E8 ML2: "disabled after 12 months unless revalidated" and "disabled after 45 days of inactivity". ML3: "Just-in-time administration is used".
  
  ## 4. Smart lockout and password protection
  
  **Password protection** (`/configuration/entra-id/protection/authentication-methods/password-protection/`):
  - "Lockout threshold | 5"
  - "Lockout duration in seconds | 60"
  - "Enforce custom list | Yes"
  - "Custom banned password list | _as per organisation requirements_"
  - "Enable password protection on Windows Server Active Directory | Yes"
  - "Mode | Enforced"
  
  **Design** (`/design/platform/identity/protection/`) uses the same 5 and 60, with "Smart lockout duration automatically increases with subsequent lockouts." Password expiry: "Never" (authentication design page).
  
  **MFA account lockout** (`/configuration/entra-id/protection/risky-activities/multifactor-authentication/account-lockout/`): 3 denials, 300 minutes until the counter resets, 1440 minutes until the account is unblocked.
  
  **For contrast, the Windows guide's local/AD lockout (not Entra):** "Account lockout duration 0 / Account lockout threshold 5 invalid logon attempts / Reset account lockout counter after 15 minutes / Allow Administrator account lockout Enabled".
  
  ## 5. Intune ASR rules
  
  **Intune policy "ASD Windows Hardening Guidelines-Attack Surface Reduction"** (`/configuration/intune/endpoint-security/attack-surface-reduction/asd-windows-hardening-asr/`), assigned to All Devices. All 15 rules are set to **Block**:
  1. Adobe Reader child processes
  2. Obfuscated scripts
  3. Win32 API calls from Office macros
  4. LSASS credential stealing
  5. Prevalence/age/trusted list
  6. JS/VBS launching downloaded executables
  7. Office communication app child processes
  8. All Office apps creating child processes
  9. Untrusted/unsigned processes from USB
  10. PSExec/WMI process creation
  11. WMI event subscription persistence
  12. Office creating executable content
  13. Office injecting into other processes
  14. Advanced ransomware protection
  15. Executable content from email/webmail
  
  **Not in this policy:** vulnerable signed drivers, Webshell, copied/impersonated system tools, Safe Mode reboot.
  
  **Defender endpoint security policy page** (`/configuration/defender/endpoints/configuration-management/endpoint-security-policies/`) sets all 19 rules to Block. It adds Webshell, "[PREVIEW] Block use of copied or impersonated system tools", "Block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers (Device)" and "[PREVIEW] Block rebooting machine in Safe Mode". "Enable Controlled Folder Access" is _Not configured_.
  
  **No Audit or Warn mode appears anywhere** in the Blueprint.
  
  **cyber.gov.au:**
  - The Windows 10 and Windows 11 guides list 16 rules (the 15 above plus vulnerable signed drivers), each set to state "1" (Block).
  - The Office guide lists 6 rules, each "1": email/webmail executable content, Office child processes, executable content, code injection, Win32 API, Office communication app child processes.
  - E8 ML2: "Microsoft Office is blocked from creating child processes / ... executable content / ... injecting code into other processes".
  
  ## 6. Office macros
  
  **Blueprint design decision** (`/design/endpoints/windows/security/microsoft-office-macro-hardening/`): "Only macros digitally signed by a trusted publisher are enabled".
  
  **Intune policy "ASD Office hardening - macros enabled for trusted publishers"** (`/configuration/intune/devices/configuration-policies/asd-office-hardening-macros-enabled-for-trusted-publishers/`):
  - Per app: "Disable all except digitally signed macros", "VBA Macro Notification Settings (User) | Enabled", "Block macros from running in Office files from the Internet (User) | Enabled" (Access, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio, Word).
  - "Trust access to Visual Basic Project | Disabled", "Turn off trusted documents | Enabled", "Disable all trusted locations | Enabled", "Disable commands | Enabled, 19092".
  - Office-wide: "Macro Runtime Scan Scope (User) | Enabled, Enable for all documents", "Disable VBA for Office applications | Disabled", "Disable all Trust Bar notifications for security issues | Enabled", "Automation Security | Use application macro security level", "Allow mix of policy and user locations | Disabled".
  - Scan encrypted macros: Excel and PowerPoint say "Enabled, Scan encrypted macros (disabled)", Word says "(default)". The PowerPoint row is mislabelled "Excel Open XML workbooks".
  
  **Intune policy "ASD Office hardening - all macros disabled"** (`.../asd-office-hardening-all-macros-disabled/`):
  - "Disable all without notification"
  - "Disable VBA for Office applications | Enabled"
  - "Set the Automation Security level | Disable macros by default"
  - Outlook "Never warn, disable all"
  
  **Antivirus scanning:** the E8 page (`/security-and-governance/essential-eight/restrict-microsoft-office-macros/`) relies on Defender with AMSI. The Win32 API block is done "using Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules".
  
  **ASD macro guide (cyber.gov.au):**
  - Order of preference: "all macros are disabled / macros digitally signed by trusted publishers are enabled / macros from trusted locations are enabled / users decide ... (with additional security measures)".
  - For the trusted-publisher approach it also sets "Only trust VBA macros that use V3 signatures | Enabled", "Disable the Content page | Enabled" and MMC "Certificates | Disabled". Outlook: "Warn for signed, disable unsigned".
  - Win32 ASR rule 92E97FA1 is "(1)" for every approach except all-disabled (N/A).
  
  **Gaps in the Blueprint trusted-publisher Intune policy compared with ASD's guide:**
  - No V3-signature setting.
  - No Content page or Certificates snap-in settings.
  - No Outlook section. The design page does list Outlook "Warn for signed, disable unsigned".
  
  **E8 ML1:** "macros in files originating from the internet are blocked", "macro antivirus scanning is enabled", "macro security settings cannot be changed by users". ML2 adds "blocked from making Win32 API calls".
  
  ## 7. Internet Explorer 11
  
  **Blueprint:**
  - `/design/endpoints/windows/configuration/windows-features/`: "Internet Explorer 11 | Disabled | ... Note, this is not applicable to Windows 11."
  - It is removed by an Intune script (`/configuration/intune/devices/scripts/userapplicationhardening-removefeatures/`) running `Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName Internet-Explorer-Optional-amd64 -NoRestart` ("for Windows 10").
  - No "Disable Internet Explorer 11 as a standalone browser" policy exists anywhere in the Blueprint.
  - The Edge policy *enables* IE mode: "Configure Internet Explorer integration | Internet Explorer mode" with an Enterprise Mode Cloud Site List (`.../asd-edge-hardening/`).
  
  **ASD hardening guides:** no setting. They only say Edge "was introduced to replace Internet Explorer 11 ... should be used wherever possible."
  
  **E8 ML1–ML3:** "Internet Explorer 11 is disabled or removed."
  
  ## 8. Windows Update and patching
  
  **Blueprint** (`/design/platform/client/device-updates/`):
  - "Servicing Channel | General Availability Channel"
  - "Microsoft Product updates | Allow", "Windows Drivers | Allow"
  - "Quality Deferral period | 0 days", "Feature Deferral | 0 days"
  - "Feature Update uninstall period | 10 days"
  - "Expedite Updates Policy | Enabled for Zero Security Updates | Address extreme security risks within 48 hours"
  - Update ring settings: "Automatic Update Behaviour: `Reset to default`", "Change Notification Update Level: `Turn off all notifications including restart warnings`", "Enable Pre-release: _Not configured_".
  
  **The Blueprint is silent on:**
  - Quality and feature update deadlines.
  - Grace periods and auto-restart.
  - Any Intune update-ring configuration page.
  
  **Patching frequency** (`/design/endpoints/windows/configuration/windows-update-and-patching/`): "applied two weeks of release, or within 48 hours if an exploit exists". That matches E8's internet-facing timeframe, not its workstation one.
  
  **ASD Windows 11 guide (Group Policy):**
  - "Configure Automatic Updates | Enabled | 4 - Auto download and schedule the install | Scheduled install day: 0 - Every day"
  - "Install updates for other Microsoft products"
  - "Remove access to "Pause updates" feature | Enabled"
  - "Remove access to use all Windows Update features | Disabled"
  - "Allow Updates in OOBE | Enabled"
  - No deadlines.
  
  **E8 workstation operating systems:** "within one month of release" at ML1 and ML2. At ML3: "within 48 hours ... when ... critical ... or when working exploits exist", otherwise "within one month".
  
  ---
  
  ## Every concrete value ASD names
  
  **Conditional Access:**
  - Built-in "Phishing-resistant MFA" strength for all users, all resources, with only a per-policy exclude group.
  - Custom "Phishing-resistant MFA and TAP" (WHfB, FIDO2, CBA multifactor, TAP one-time and multi-use), used only for registering security info.
  - Admin sign-in frequency 4 hours; user sign-in frequency 12 hours.
  - Risky sign-ins: Low and Medium require phishing-resistant MFA; High is blocked. High user risk is blocked.
  - Legacy auth: block Exchange ActiveSync + Other clients.
  - Allowed device platforms: Windows and iOS only (Android, Windows Phone, macOS and Linux blocked).
  - Microsoft-managed admin and all-user MFA policies set Off.
  - 73-role admin list (DSC only).
  
  **Authentication methods:**
  - FIDO2 with attestation and an AAGUID allow list.
  - Authenticator push with number matching, OTP off.
  - TAP 1 hour minimum, 8 hours maximum, 1 hour default, length 15, not one-time.
  - SMS, voice, email OTP, hardware OATH, software OATH and CBA disabled.
  - App passwords off; remember MFA off.
  
  **PIM:**
  - All Entra roles; eligible assignment only.
  - Assignments up to 365 days; activation capped at 8 hours.
  - Approval by role risk (no fixed rule); permanent active only for break glass and service accounts.
  
  **Access reviews:** 6-monthly for roles and role-assigned groups; 3-monthly for CA exclude groups.
  
  **Inactivity:** disable after more than 45 days (ISM 1404 and 1648).
  
  **Break glass:** 2 accounts, *.onmicrosoft.com, permanent Global Administrator, excluded from MFA and CA.
  
  **Lockout:**
  - Entra smart lockout: threshold 5, duration 60 seconds; custom banned list on; on-prem Enforced.
  - MFA lockout: 3 / 300 / 1440.
  - Windows/AD lockout: 5 attempts, duration 0, reset 15 minutes.
  
  **ASR:**
  - Blueprint Intune: 15 rules, all Block.
  - Blueprint Defender: 19 rules, all Block.
  - ASD Windows guides: 16 rules = 1 (Block). ASD Office guide: 6 rules = 1.
  
  **Office macros:**
  - "Disable all except digitally signed macros"
  - Block internet macros: Enabled
  - Macro Runtime Scan Scope: all documents
  - Disable all trusted locations; turn off trusted documents
  - VBA project access: Disabled
  - Disable commands 19092
  - ASD only: V3 signatures Enabled
  
  **Internet Explorer 11:** removed by script on Windows 10 (`Internet-Explorer-Optional-amd64`); IE mode enabled in Edge.
  
  **Windows Update:**
  - GA channel; quality and feature deferral 0 days; feature uninstall 10 days.
  - Expedite within 48 hours; drivers and Microsoft products allowed.
  - ASD Group Policy: auto-install every day, Pause removed.
  
  ## Where the Blueprint is silent
  
  - A separate admin MFA or strength policy, and an admin role list outside the DSC.
  - Mailbox-less or unlicensed admins, and cloud-only admins other than break glass.
  - PIM approval specifics, MFA-on-activation values and notification values.
  - Update deadlines, grace periods and restart behaviour.
  - An "IE11 standalone browser" policy setting.
  - ASR Audit or Warn modes and per-rule exclusions (all "Not configured").
  
</agent-message>

  | USR - G - Register security info with strong auth | All users | User action "Register security information" | Custom "Phishing-resistant MFA and TAP" |
  | USR - G - Risky sign-ins with strong auth | All users, sign-in risk Low + Medium | All resources | Phishing-resistant MFA |
  | USR - B - Block high-risk sign-ins | All users, sign-in risk High | All resources | Block |
  | USR - B - Block high-risk users | All users, user risk High | All resources | Block |
  | USR - B - Block users with elevated insider risk | All users, insider risk Elevated | All resources | Block |
  | USR - B - Block access via legacy auth | All users, client apps "Exchange ActiveSync clients" + "Other clients" | All resources | Block |
  | USR - B - Block access to PROTECTED information | `<PROTECTED users group>` excluded | Authentication context "PROTECTED information" | Block |
  | USR - G - Agreement to terms of use | All users | All resources | Terms |
  | USR - S - Limit user sessions | All users, excluding admin roles and `<Administrative user group>` | All resources | Sign-in frequency 12 hours |
  | ADM - S - Limit admin sessions | Admin roles + `<Administrative user group>` | All resources | Sign-in frequency 4 hours |
  | DEV - G - Compliant devices | All users | All resources | Require device to be marked as compliant |
  | DEV - B - Block access from unapproved devices | All users; platforms Android, Windows Phone, macOS, Linux | All resources | Block |
  | DEV - G - Intune enrolment with strong auth | All users | Microsoft Intune + Microsoft Intune Enrolment | Phishing-resistant MFA |
  | GST - B - Block guests | All 6 guest/external types, excluding `<Guest application user group>` | All resources | Block |
  | GST - G - Guest `<application>` access with strong auth | Guests | `<application>` | Phishing-resistant MFA |
  | LOC - B - Block access from unapproved countries | All users | All resources | Block, excluding "Allowed Countries" |
  
  **The "MFA for all users" policy.** On `.../policies/strong-authentication/`:
  - "Include | All users"
  - Exclude: "Users and groups | Checked | `<CA exclude group - USR - G - Require strong auth>`"
  - "Guest or external users | Not checked" and "Directory roles | Not checked" (under Exclude)
  - "All resources (formerly 'All cloud apps')", with "Exclude | None"
  - "Require multifactor authentication | Not checked"
  - "Require authentication strength | Phishing-resistant MFA: Checked"
  
  So the built-in strength applies to **all users**.
  
  On `/design/platform/identity/conditional-access/`:
  - "Require strong authentication for users | Enforce phishing-resistant MFA for all users"
  - "Authentication strengths for user access | Use phishing-resistant MFA | Comply with Essential Eight requirements"
  
  **Exclusions** (same design page):
  - "Use separate exclude groups for each Conditional Access policy"
  - "Use Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for exclude group membership changes"
  - "Exclude Break glass accounts from Conditional Access policy control"
  
  **There is no separate admin MFA policy.** The only ADM policy is the 4-hour session policy. On `.../policies/limit-admin-sessions/`:
  - "Directory roles | Checked | _Select applicable administrator roles_" plus `<Administrative user group>`
  - "Periodic reauthentication | 4 hours"
  - No grant control
  
  The page does not name the roles. The design page says: "Use groups as well as roles to identity administrative users".
  
  The Microsoft-managed policies are all set Off as "superseded by Blueprint policies". They include "Multifactor authentication for admins accessing Microsoft Admin Portals", "Require multifactor authentication for admins" and "Require multifactor authentication for all users".
  
  On `/design/platform/identity/authentication/`: "MFA for Administration | Configured | Administration through Microsoft 365 administration portals and other Cloud Apps should require MFA."
  
  **The only concrete admin role list is in the DSC file** (`/content/files/automation/dsc/BlueprintEntraDsc.txt`, Microsoft365DSC 1.24.717.1). Its `ADM - S - Limit admin sessions` IncludeRoles (and `USR - S` ExcludeRoles) lists 73 roles: essentially every "... Administrator" role, Global Administrator included, plus `$PrivUsers`.
  
  The DSC also disagrees with the docs in places:
  - `ADM - S - Limit admin sessions` and `DEV - G - Compliant devices` have `IncludeApplications = @("None")`, where the pages say "All resources".
  - Every DSC policy is `State = "enabledForReportingButNotEnforced"`.
  
  ## 2. Authentication strengths
  
  **The one custom strength.** On `/configuration/entra-id/protection/conditional-access/authentication-strengths/`:
  - Name: "Phishing-resistant MFA and TAP"
  - Phishing-resistant MFA: "Windows Hello For Business / Passkeys (FIDO2) / Certificate-based Authentication (Multifactor)"
  - Multifactor authentication: "Temporary Access Pass (One-time use) / Temporary Access Pass (Multi-use)"
  
  Only the Register security info policy uses it. Every other grant uses the built-in "Phishing-resistant MFA". Design page: "Authentication strengths for bootstrapping flows | Use phishing-resistant MFA plus temporary access passes (TAPs)".
  
  **Authentication methods policy** (`/configuration/entra-id/protection/authentication-methods/policies/`):
  - Enabled for "All users, excluding `<Conditional Access excluded identities>`": Passkey (FIDO2), Microsoft Authenticator, Temporary Access Pass.
  - Disabled ("No"): SMS, Hardware OATH, Third-party software OATH, Voice call, Email OTP, Certificate-based authentication. Note that CBA is disabled here although the custom strength includes it.
  - FIDO2: "Enforce attestation | Yes", "Enforce key restrictions | Yes", "Restrict specific keys | Allow", `<Organisation AAGUIDs>`.
  - Authenticator: "Allow use of Microsoft Authenticator OTP | No", "Require number matching ... | Enabled".
  - TAP: "Minimum lifetime | 1 hour", "Maximum lifetime | 8 hours", "Default lifetime | 1 hour", "One-time | No", "Length | 15 characters".
  
  **Design guidance** (`/design/platform/identity/authentication/`):
  - ML2/ML3: "FIDO2 Key / Windows Hello for Business (Pin Only) on organisational devices", with "Alternative Methods | Temporary Access Pass".
  - "Microsoft Authenticator is not phishing resistant."
  
  **Per-user MFA service settings** (`/configuration/entra-id/users/per-user-mfa/`):
  - "Do not allow users to create app passwords..."
  - "Remember multi-factor authentication on trusted device | Not checked"
  
  **Windows 11 hardening guide:** "hardware-based multi-factor authentication should be used for privileged users, remote access and any access to important or sensitive data repositories."
  
  ## 3. Privileged access
  
  **PIM design** (`/design/platform/identity/roles/`), verbatim decision table:
  - "Role activation model | Least Privilege via Privileged Identity Management"
  - "PIM role scope | All Entra roles"
  - "Approval workflow | Align approval requirements with the risk of each role's capabilities" (no fixed approval rule)
  - "Assignment type | Eligible assignment"
  - "Assignment duration | Maximum 365 days"
  - "Activation duration | Capped at 8 hours and restricted to the minimum necessary duration"
  - "Standing access exceptions | Permanent active assignment for break glass and specific service accounts"
  
  `/design/shared-services/microsoft-365/rbac/` adds "PIM | Configured" and lists the M365 roles PIM can assign.
  
  **Access reviews** (`/design/platform/identity/governance/`):
  - "Use 6-monthly access reviews for active and eligible assigned roles"
  - "Use 3-monthly access reviews for Conditional Access exclude groups"
  - "Use 6-monthly access reviews for role assigned groups"
  - "Access reviews for inactive users ... are not in implemented in the Blueprint."
  
  **Inactivity** (`/design/platform/identity/users/`): "ISM Security Controls 1404 and 1648 | Disable un-privileged and privileged user accounts after > 45 days of inactivity", done by "a custom script set to run on a scheduled basis". This conflicts with the E8 page (`/security-and-governance/essential-eight/restrict-administrative-privileges/`): "The Blueprint does not currently provide guidance for automating the disabling of accounts."
  
  **Break glass accounts** (same users page; config page `/configuration/entra-id/users/break-glass-accounts/`):
  - Two accounts, "cloud only accounts that use the `*.onmicrosoft.com` domain".
  - "Global Administrator role assigned permanently".
  - "Both Emergency access accounts will be excluded from MFA". The page's own bullet list instead says "At least one".
  - Monitored "via Defender for Cloud Apps".
  
  **Separate admin accounts:**
  - SSP template (`/security-and-governance/system-security-plan/personnel-security/`): "privileged users granted additional uniquely identifiable privileged accounts".
  - Same template: "an AppLocker blocklist is configured on workstations via Intune to prevent administrators from launching web browsers and email clients".
  - E8 page: "The Blueprint does not currently provide guidance for restricting privileged account activities." Its template text says privileged accounts "are restricted from accessing the internet, email and web services".
  
  **Silent on:**
  - Admin accounts without mailboxes or licences. `/design/shared-services/microsoft-365/licencing/` actually defines "Admin Licence Group | `rol-OrganisationName-Administrator`".
  - Cloud-only admin accounts other than break glass.
  
  **cyber.gov.au:**
  - Windows 11 guide: "separate standard and privileged accounts with different credentials ... privileged accounts used should have external web and email access blocked."
  - E8 ML2: "disabled after 12 months unless revalidated" and "disabled after 45 days of inactivity". ML3: "Just-in-time administration is used".
  
  ## 4. Smart lockout and password protection
  
  **Password protection** (`/configuration/entra-id/protection/authentication-methods/password-protection/`):
  - "Lockout threshold | 5"
  - "Lockout duration in seconds | 60"
  - "Enforce custom list | Yes"
  - "Custom banned password list | _as per organisation requirements_"
  - "Enable password protection on Windows Server Active Directory | Yes"
  - "Mode | Enforced"
  
  **Design** (`/design/platform/identity/protection/`) uses the same 5 and 60, with "Smart lockout duration automatically increases with subsequent lockouts." Password expiry: "Never" (authentication design page).
  
  **MFA account lockout** (`/configuration/entra-id/protection/risky-activities/multifactor-authentication/account-lockout/`): 3 denials, 300 minutes until the counter resets, 1440 minutes until the account is unblocked.
  
  **For contrast, the Windows guide's local/AD lockout (not Entra):** "Account lockout duration 0 / Account lockout threshold 5 invalid logon attempts / Reset account lockout counter after 15 minutes / Allow Administrator account lockout Enabled".
  
  ## 5. Intune ASR rules
  
  **Intune policy "ASD Windows Hardening Guidelines-Attack Surface Reduction"** (`/configuration/intune/endpoint-security/attack-surface-reduction/asd-windows-hardening-asr/`), assigned to All Devices. All 15 rules are set to **Block**:
  1. Adobe Reader child processes
  2. Obfuscated scripts
  3. Win32 API calls from Office macros
  4. LSASS credential stealing
  5. Prevalence/age/trusted list
  6. JS/VBS launching downloaded executables
  7. Office communication app child processes
  8. All Office apps creating child processes
  9. Untrusted/unsigned processes from USB
  10. PSExec/WMI process creation
  11. WMI event subscription persistence
  12. Office creating executable content
  13. Office injecting into other processes
  14. Advanced ransomware protection
  15. Executable content from email/webmail
  
  **Not in this policy:** vulnerable signed drivers, Webshell, copied/impersonated system tools, Safe Mode reboot.
  
  **Defender endpoint security policy page** (`/configuration/defender/endpoints/configuration-management/endpoint-security-policies/`) sets all 19 rules to Block. It adds Webshell, "[PREVIEW] Block use of copied or impersonated system tools", "Block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers (Device)" and "[PREVIEW] Block rebooting machine in Safe Mode". "Enable Controlled Folder Access" is _Not configured_.
  
  **No Audit or Warn mode appears anywhere** in the Blueprint.
  
  **cyber.gov.au:**
  - The Windows 10 and Windows 11 guides list 16 rules (the 15 above plus vulnerable signed drivers), each set to state "1" (Block).
  - The Office guide lists 6 rules, each "1": email/webmail executable content, Office child processes, executable content, code injection, Win32 API, Office communication app child processes.
  - E8 ML2: "Microsoft Office is blocked from creating child processes / ... executable content / ... injecting code into other processes".
  
  ## 6. Office macros
  
  **Blueprint design decision** (`/design/endpoints/windows/security/microsoft-office-macro-hardening/`): "Only macros digitally signed by a trusted publisher are enabled".
  
  **Intune policy "ASD Office hardening - macros enabled for trusted publishers"** (`/configuration/intune/devices/configuration-policies/asd-office-hardening-macros-enabled-for-trusted-publishers/`):
  - Per app: "Disable all except digitally signed macros", "VBA Macro Notification Settings (User) | Enabled", "Block macros from running in Office files from the Internet (User) | Enabled" (Access, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio, Word).
  - "Trust access to Visual Basic Project | Disabled", "Turn off trusted documents | Enabled", "Disable all trusted locations | Enabled", "Disable commands | Enabled, 19092".
  - Office-wide: "Macro Runtime Scan Scope (User) | Enabled, Enable for all documents", "Disable VBA for Office applications | Disabled", "Disable all Trust Bar notifications for security issues | Enabled", "Automation Security | Use application macro security level", "Allow mix of policy and user locations | Disabled".
  - Scan encrypted macros: Excel and PowerPoint say "Enabled, Scan encrypted macros (disabled)", Word says "(default)". The PowerPoint row is mislabelled "Excel Open XML workbooks".
  
  **Intune policy "ASD Office hardening - all macros disabled"** (`.../asd-office-hardening-all-macros-disabled/`):
  - "Disable all without notification"
  - "Disable VBA for Office applications | Enabled"
  - "Set the Automation Security level | Disable macros by default"
  - Outlook "Never warn, disable all"
  
  **Antivirus scanning:** the E8 page (`/security-and-governance/essential-eight/restrict-microsoft-office-macros/`) relies on Defender with AMSI. The Win32 API block is done "using Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules".
  
  **ASD macro guide (cyber.gov.au):**
  - Order of preference: "all macros are disabled / macros digitally signed by trusted publishers are enabled / macros from trusted locations are enabled / users decide ... (with additional security measures)".
  - For the trusted-publisher approach it also sets "Only trust VBA macros that use V3 signatures | Enabled", "Disable the Content page | Enabled" and MMC "Certificates | Disabled". Outlook: "Warn for signed, disable unsigned".
  - Win32 ASR rule 92E97FA1 is "(1)" for every approach except all-disabled (N/A).
  
  **Gaps in the Blueprint trusted-publisher Intune policy compared with ASD's guide:**
  - No V3-signature setting.
  - No Content page or Certificates snap-in settings.
  - No Outlook section. The design page does list Outlook "Warn for signed, disable unsigned".
  
  **E8 ML1:** "macros in files originating from the internet are blocked", "macro antivirus scanning is enabled", "macro security settings cannot be changed by users". ML2 adds "blocked from making Win32 API calls".
  
  ## 7. Internet Explorer 11
  
  **Blueprint:**
  - `/design/endpoints/windows/configuration/windows-features/`: "Internet Explorer 11 | Disabled | ... Note, this is not applicable to Windows 11."
  - It is removed by an Intune script (`/configuration/intune/devices/scripts/userapplicationhardening-removefeatures/`) running `Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName Internet-Explorer-Optional-amd64 -NoRestart` ("for Windows 10").
  - No "Disable Internet Explorer 11 as a standalone browser" policy exists anywhere in the Blueprint.
  - The Edge policy *enables* IE mode: "Configure Internet Explorer integration | Internet Explorer mode" with an Enterprise Mode Cloud Site List (`.../asd-edge-hardening/`).
  
  **ASD hardening guides:** no setting. They only say Edge "was introduced to replace Internet Explorer 11 ... should be used wherever possible."
  
  **E8 ML1–ML3:** "Internet Explorer 11 is disabled or removed."
  
  ## 8. Windows Update and patching
  
  **Blueprint** (`/design/platform/client/device-updates/`):
  - "Servicing Channel | General Availability Channel"
  - "Microsoft Product updates | Allow", "Windows Drivers | Allow"
  - "Quality Deferral period | 0 days", "Feature Deferral | 0 days"
  - "Feature Update uninstall period | 10 days"
  - "Expedite Updates Policy | Enabled for Zero Security Updates | Address extreme security risks within 48 hours"
  - Update ring settings: "Automatic Update Behaviour: `Reset to default`", "Change Notification Update Level: `Turn off all notifications including restart warnings`", "Enable Pre-release: _Not configured_".
  
  **The Blueprint is silent on:**
  - Quality and feature update deadlines.
  - Grace periods and auto-restart.
  - Any Intune update-ring configuration page.
  
  **Patching frequency** (`/design/endpoints/windows/configuration/windows-update-and-patching/`): "applied two weeks of release, or within 48 hours if an exploit exists". That matches E8's internet-facing timeframe, not its workstation one.
  
  **ASD Windows 11 guide (Group Policy):**
  - "Configure Automatic Updates | Enabled | 4 - Auto download and schedule the install | Scheduled install day: 0 - Every day"
  - "Install updates for other Microsoft products"
  - "Remove access to "Pause updates" feature | Enabled"
  - "Remove access to use all Windows Update features | Disabled"
  - "Allow Updates in OOBE | Enabled"
  - No deadlines.
  
  **E8 workstation operating systems:** "within one month of release" at ML1 and ML2. At ML3: "within 48 hours ... when ... critical ... or when working exploits exist", otherwise "within one month".
  
  ---
  
  ## Every concrete value ASD names
  
  **Conditional Access:**
  - Built-in "Phishing-resistant MFA" strength for all users, all resources, with only a per-policy exclude group.
  - Custom "Phishing-resistant MFA and TAP" (WHfB, FIDO2, CBA multifactor, TAP one-time and multi-use), used only for registering security info.
  - Admin sign-in frequency 4 hours; user sign-in frequency 12 hours.
  - Risky sign-ins: Low and Medium require phishing-resistant MFA; High is blocked. High user risk is blocked.
  - Legacy auth: block Exchange ActiveSync + Other clients.
  - Allowed device platforms: Windows and iOS only (Android, Windows Phone, macOS and Linux blocked).
  - Microsoft-managed admin and all-user MFA policies set Off.
  - 73-role admin list (DSC only).
  
  **Authentication methods:**
  - FIDO2 with attestation and an AAGUID allow list.
  - Authenticator push with number matching, OTP off.
  - TAP 1 hour minimum, 8 hours maximum, 1 hour default, length 15, not one-time.
  - SMS, voice, email OTP, hardware OATH, software OATH and CBA disabled.
  - App passwords off; remember MFA off.
  
  **PIM:**
  - All Entra roles; eligible assignment only.
  - Assignments up to 365 days; activation capped at 8 hours.
  - Approval by role risk (no fixed rule); permanent active only for break glass and service accounts.
  
  **Access reviews:** 6-monthly for roles and role-assigned groups; 3-monthly for CA exclude groups.
  
  **Inactivity:** disable after more than 45 days (ISM 1404 and 1648).
  
  **Break glass:** 2 accounts, *.onmicrosoft.com, permanent Global Administrator, excluded from MFA and CA.
  
  **Lockout:**
  - Entra smart lockout: threshold 5, duration 60 seconds; custom banned list on; on-prem Enforced.
  - MFA lockout: 3 / 300 / 1440.
  - Windows/AD lockout: 5 attempts, duration 0, reset 15 minutes.
  
  **ASR:**
  - Blueprint Intune: 15 rules, all Block.
  - Blueprint Defender: 19 rules, all Block.
  - ASD Windows guides: 16 rules = 1 (Block). ASD Office guide: 6 rules = 1.
  
  **Office macros:**
  - "Disable all except digitally signed macros"
  - Block internet macros: Enabled
  - Macro Runtime Scan Scope: all documents
  - Disable all trusted locations; turn off trusted documents
  - VBA project access: Disabled
  - Disable commands 19092
  - ASD only: V3 signatures Enabled
  
  **Internet Explorer 11:** removed by script on Windows 10 (`Internet-Explorer-Optional-amd64`); IE mode enabled in Edge.
  
  **Windows Update:**
  - GA channel; quality and feature deferral 0 days; feature uninstall 10 days.
  - Expedite within 48 hours; drivers and Microsoft products allowed.
  - ASD Group Policy: auto-install every day, Pause removed.
  
  ## Where the Blueprint is silent
  
  - A separate admin MFA or strength policy, and an admin role list outside the DSC.
  - Mailbox-less or unlicensed admins, and cloud-only admins other than break glass.
  - PIM approval specifics, MFA-on-activation values and notification values.
  - Update deadlines, grace periods and restart behaviour.
  - An "IE11 standalone browser" policy setting.
  - ASR Audit or Warn modes and per-rule exclusions (all "Not configured").
  
</agent-message>

  - "Lockout duration in seconds | 60"
  - "Enforce custom list | Yes"
  - "Custom banned password list | _as per organisation requirements_"
  - "Enable password protection on Windows Server Active Directory | Yes"
  - "Mode | Enforced"

  6. JS/VBS launching downloaded executables

  9. Untrusted/unsigned processes from USB
  10. PSExec/WMI process creation
  11. WMI event subscription persistence

  13. Office injecting into other processes
  14. Advanced ransomware protection

It adds Webshell, "[PREVIEW] Block use of copied or impersonated system tools", "Block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers (Device)" and "[PREVIEW] Block rebooting machine in Safe Mode".   - "Install updates for other Microsoft products"
  - "Remove access to "Pause updates" feature | Enabled"
  - "Remove access to use all Windows Update features | Disabled"
  - "Allow Updates in OOBE | Enabled"

  - Allowed device platforms: Windows and iOS only (Android, Windows Phone, macOS and Linux blocked).

  - 73-role admin list (DSC only).
  
  **Authentication methods:**

  - Authenticator push with number matching, OTP off.
  - TAP 1 hour minimum, 8 hours maximum, 1 hour default, length 15, not one-time.
  - SMS, voice, email OTP, hardware OATH, software OATH and CBA disabled.
  - App passwords off; remember MFA off.

  - Assignments up to 365 days; activation capped at 8 hours.
  - Approval by role risk (no fixed rule); permanent active only for break glass and service accounts.
  
  **Access reviews:** 6-monthly for roles and role-assigned groups; 3-monthly for CA exclude groups.
  
  **Inactivity:** disable after more than 45 days (ISM 1404 and 1648).
  
  **Break glass:** 2 accounts, *.onmicrosoft.com, permanent Global Administrator, excluded from MFA and CA.
  
  **Lockout:**
  - Entra smart lockout: threshold 5, duration 60 seconds; custom banned list on; on-prem Enforced.
  - MFA lockout: 3 / 300 / 1440.
  - Windows/AD lockout: 5 attempts, duration 0, reset 15 minutes.
  
  **ASR:**
  - Blueprint Intune: 15 rules, all Block.
  - Blueprint Defender: 19 rules, all Block.
  - ASD Windows guides: 16 rules = 1 (Block). ASD Office guide: 6 rules = 1.
  
  **Office macros:**
  - "Disable all except digitally signed macros"
  - Block internet macros: Enabled
  - Macro Runtime Scan Scope: all documents
  - Disable all trusted locations; turn off trusted documents
  - VBA project access: Disabled
  - Disable commands 19092
  - ASD only: V3 signatures Enabled

  **Windows Update:**
  - GA channel; quality and feature deferral 0 days; feature uninstall 10 days.
  - Expedite within 48 hours; drivers and Microsoft products allowed.
  - ASD Group Policy: auto-install every day, Pause removed.
  
  ## Where the Blueprint is silent
  
  - A separate admin MFA or strength policy, and an admin role list outside the DSC.
  - Mailbox-less or unlicensed admins, and cloud-only admins other than break glass.
  - PIM approval specifics, MFA-on-activation values and notification values.
  - Update deadlines, grace periods and restart behaviour.
  - An "IE11 standalone browser" policy setting.
  - ASR Audit or Warn modes and per-rule exclusions (all "Not configured").

  ## 8. Windows Update and patching
  
  **Blueprint** (`/design/platform/client/device-updates/`):
  - "Servicing Channel | General Availability Channel"
  - "Microsoft Product updates | Allow", "Windows Drivers | Allow"
  - "Quality Deferral period | 0 days", "Feature Deferral | 0 days"
  - "Feature Update uninstall period | 10 days"
  - "Expedite Updates Policy | Enabled for Zero Security Updates | Address extreme security risks within 48 hours"
  - Update ring settings: "Automatic Update Behaviour: `Reset to default`", "Change Notification Update Level: `Turn off all notifications including restart warnings`", "Enable Pre-release: _Not configured_".
  
  **The Blueprint is silent on:**
  - Quality and feature update deadlines.
  - Grace periods and auto-restart.
  - Any Intune update-ring configuration page.
  
  **Patching frequency** (`/design/endpoints/windows/configuration/windows-update-and-patching/`): "applied two weeks of release, or within 48 hours if an exploit exists". That matches E8's internet-facing timeframe, not its workstation one.
  
  **ASD Windows 11 guide (Group Policy):**
  - "Configure Automatic Updates | Enabled | 4 - Auto download and schedule the install | Scheduled install day: 0 - Every day"
  - "Install updates for other Microsoft products"
  - "Remove access to "Pause updates" feature | Enabled"
  - "Remove access to use all Windows Update features | Disabled"
  - "Allow Updates in OOBE | Enabled"
  - No deadlines.
  
  **E8 workstation operating systems:** "within one month of release" at ML1 and ML2. At ML3: "within 48 hours ... when ... critical ... or when working exploits exist", otherwise "within one month".
  
  ---
  
  ## Every concrete value ASD names
  
  **Conditional Access:**
  - Built-in "Phishing-resistant MFA" strength for all users, all resources, with only a per-policy exclude group.
  - Custom "Phishing-resistant MFA and TAP" (WHfB, FIDO2, CBA multifactor, TAP one-time and multi-use), used only for registering security info.
  - Admin sign-in frequency 4 hours; user sign-in frequency 12 hours.
  - Risky sign-ins: Low and Medium require phishing-resistant MFA; High is blocked. High user risk is blocked.
  - Legacy auth: block Exchange ActiveSync + Other clients.
  - Allowed device platforms: Windows and iOS only (Android, Windows Phone, macOS and Linux blocked).
  - Microsoft-managed admin and all-user MFA policies set Off.
  - 73-role admin list (DSC only).
  
  **Authentication methods:**
  - FIDO2 with attestation and an AAGUID allow list.
  - Authenticator push with number matching, OTP off.
  - TAP 1 hour minimum, 8 hours maximum, 1 hour default, length 15, not one-time.
  - SMS, voice, email OTP, hardware OATH, software OATH and CBA disabled.
  - App passwords off; remember MFA off.
  
  **PIM:**
  - All Entra roles; eligible assignment only.
  - Assignments up to 365 days; activation capped at 8 hours.
  - Approval by role risk (no fixed rule); permanent active only for break glass and service accounts.
  
  **Access reviews:** 6-monthly for roles and role-assigned groups; 3-monthly for CA exclude groups.
  
  **Inactivity:** disable after more than 45 days (ISM 1404 and 1648).
  
  **Break glass:** 2 accounts, *.onmicrosoft.com, permanent Global Administrator, excluded from MFA and CA.
  
  **Lockout:**
  - Entra smart lockout: threshold 5, duration 60 seconds; custom banned list on; on-prem Enforced.
  - MFA lockout: 3 / 300 / 1440.
  - Windows/AD lockout: 5 attempts, duration 0, reset 15 minutes.
  
  **ASR:**
  - Blueprint Intune: 15 rules, all Block.
  - Blueprint Defender: 19 rules, all Block.
  - ASD Windows guides: 16 rules = 1 (Block). ASD Office guide: 6 rules = 1.
  
  **Office macros:**
  - "Disable all except digitally signed macros"
  - Block internet macros: Enabled
  - Macro Runtime Scan Scope: all documents
  - Disable all trusted locations; turn off trusted documents
  - VBA project access: Disabled
  - Disable commands 19092
  - ASD only: V3 signatures Enabled
  
  **Internet Explorer 11:** removed by script on Windows 10 (`Internet-Explorer-Optional-amd64`); IE mode enabled in Edge.
  
  **Windows Update:**
  - GA channel; quality and feature deferral 0 days; feature uninstall 10 days.
  - Expedite within 48 hours; drivers and Microsoft products allowed.
  - ASD Group Policy: auto-install every day, Pause removed.
  
  ## Where the Blueprint is silent
  
  - A separate admin MFA or strength policy, and an admin role list outside the DSC.
  - Mailbox-less or unlicensed admins, and cloud-only admins other than break glass.
  - PIM approval specifics, MFA-on-activation values and notification values.
  - Update deadlines, grace periods and restart behaviour.
  - An "IE11 standalone browser" policy setting.
  - ASR Audit or Warn modes and per-rule exclusions (all "Not configured").

  # What ASD specifies for the Essential Eight and ISM M365 checks
  
  **Sources read:**
  - The Blueprint GitHub repo (github.com/ASD-Blueprint/ASD-Blueprint-for-Secure-Cloud, HEAD a6e1e5f, 18 Sep 2026). Live pages at blueprint.asd.gov.au were spot-checked and match it. URLs below are `https://blueprint.asd.gov.au/<path>/`.
  - cyber.gov.au:
    - *Hardening Microsoft Windows 11 workstations*, last reviewed 23 Jan 2026 (the Windows 10 version, 4 Sep 2025, has the same ASR and IE text).
    - *Hardening Microsoft 365, Office 2021, Office 2019 and Office 2016*, 24 Jul 2023.
    - *Restricting Microsoft Office macros*, 27 Nov 2023. The "Microsoft Office macro security" URL now redirects here.
    - *Essential Eight maturity model*, 27 Nov 2023.
  
  **Caveats that apply throughout:**
  - Every Blueprint config page carries this disclaimer: "Any implementation implied by these pages should not be considered as prescriptive as to how an organisation must scope, build, document, or assess a system."
  - The CA policies index page says: "All Conditional Access policies in the DSC are set to report only and will need to be enabled manually." The individual policy pages say "Enable policy | On".
  
  ---
  
  ## 1. Conditional Access
  
  The policy pages are under `/configuration/entra-id/protection/conditional-access/policies/`. There are 16 policies:
  
  | Policy | Users | Resources | Control |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | USR - G - Require strong auth | All users | All resources | Built-in "Phishing-resistant MFA" |
  | USR - G - Register security info with strong auth | All users | User action "Register security information" | Custom "Phishing-resistant MFA and TAP" |
  | USR - G - Risky sign-ins with strong auth | All users, sign-in risk Low + Medium | All resources | Phishing-resistant MFA |
  | USR - B - Block high-risk sign-ins | All users, sign-in risk High | All resources | Block |
  | USR - B - Block high-risk users | All users, user risk High | All resources | Block |
  | USR - B - Block users with elevated insider risk | All users, insider risk Elevated | All resources | Block |
  | USR - B - Block access via legacy auth | All users, client apps "Exchange ActiveSync clients" + "Other clients" | All resources | Block |
  | USR - B - Block access to PROTECTED information | `<PROTECTED users group>` excluded | Authentication context "PROTECTED information" | Block |
  | USR - G - Agreement to terms of use | All users | All resources | Terms |
  | USR - S - Limit user sessions | All users, excluding admin roles and `<Administrative user group>` | All resources | Sign-in frequency 12 hours |
  | ADM - S - Limit admin sessions | Admin roles + `<Administrative user group>` | All resources | Sign-in frequency 4 hours |
  | DEV - G - Compliant devices | All users | All resources | Require device to be marked as compliant |
  | DEV - B - Block access from unapproved devices | All users; platforms Android, Windows Phone, macOS, Linux | All resources | Block |
  | DEV - G - Intune enrolment with strong auth | All users | Microsoft Intune + Microsoft Intune Enrolment | Phishing-resistant MFA |
  | GST - B - Block guests | All 6 guest/external types, excluding `<Guest application user group>` | All resources | Block |
  | GST - G - Guest `<application>` access with strong auth | Guests | `<application>` | Phishing-resistant MFA |
  | LOC - B - Block access from unapproved countries | All users | All resources | Block, excluding "Allowed Countries" |
  
  **The "MFA for all users" policy.** On `.../policies/strong-authentication/`:
  - "Include | All users"
  - Exclude: "Users and groups | Checked | `<CA exclude group - USR - G - Require strong auth>`"
  - "Guest or external users | Not checked" and "Directory roles | Not checked" (under Exclude)
  - "All resources (formerly 'All cloud apps')", with "Exclude | None"
  - "Require multifactor authentication | Not checked"
  - "Require authentication strength | Phishing-resistant MFA: Checked"
  
  So the built-in strength applies to **all users**.
  
  On `/design/platform/identity/conditional-access/`:
  - "Require strong authentication for users | Enforce phishing-resistant MFA for all users"
  - "Authentication strengths for user access | Use phishing-resistant MFA | Comply with Essential Eight requirements"
  
  **Exclusions** (same design page):
  - "Use separate exclude groups for each Conditional Access policy"
  - "Use Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for exclude group membership changes"
  - "Exclude Break glass accounts from Conditional Access policy control"
  
  **There is no separate admin MFA policy.** The only ADM policy is the 4-hour session policy. On `.../policies/limit-admin-sessions/`:
  - "Directory roles | Checked | _Select applicable administrator roles_" plus `<Administrative user group>`
  - "Periodic reauthentication | 4 hours"
  - No grant control
  
  The page does not name the roles. The design page says: "Use groups as well as roles to identity administrative users".
  
  The Microsoft-managed policies are all set Off as "superseded by Blueprint policies". They include "Multifactor authentication for admins accessing Microsoft Admin Portals", "Require multifactor authentication for admins" and "Require multifactor authentication for all users".
  
  On `/design/platform/identity/authentication/`: "MFA for Administration | Configured | Administration through Microsoft 365 administration portals and other Cloud Apps should require MFA."
  
  **The only concrete admin role list is in the DSC file** (`/content/files/automation/dsc/BlueprintEntraDsc.txt`, Microsoft365DSC 1.24.717.1). Its `ADM - S - Limit admin sessions` IncludeRoles (and `USR - S` ExcludeRoles) lists 73 roles: essentially every "... Administrator" role, Global Administrator included, plus `$PrivUsers`.
  
  The DSC also disagrees with the docs in places:
  - `ADM - S - Limit admin sessions` and `DEV - G - Compliant devices` have `IncludeApplications = @("None")`, where the pages say "All resources".
  - Every DSC policy is `State = "enabledForReportingButNotEnforced"`.
  
  ## 2. Authentication strengths
  
  **The one custom strength.** On `/configuration/entra-id/protection/conditional-access/authentication-strengths/`:
  - Name: "Phishing-resistant MFA and TAP"
  - Phishing-resistant MFA: "Windows Hello For Business / Passkeys (FIDO2) / Certificate-based Authentication (Multifactor)"
  - Multifactor authentication: "Temporary Access Pass (One-time use) / Temporary Access Pass (Multi-use)"
  
  Only the Register security info policy uses it. Every other grant uses the built-in "Phishing-resistant MFA". Design page: "Authentication strengths for bootstrapping flows | Use phishing-resistant MFA plus temporary access passes (TAPs)".
  
  **Authentication methods policy** (`/configuration/entra-id/protection/authentication-methods/policies/`):
  - Enabled for "All users, excluding `<Conditional Access excluded identities>`": Passkey (FIDO2), Microsoft Authenticator, Temporary Access Pass.
  - Disabled ("No"): SMS, Hardware OATH, Third-party software OATH, Voice call, Email OTP, Certificate-based authentication. Note that CBA is disabled here although the custom strength includes it.
  - FIDO2: "Enforce attestation | Yes", "Enforce key restrictions | Yes", "Restrict specific keys | Allow", `<Organisation AAGUIDs>`.
  - Authenticator: "Allow use of Microsoft Authenticator OTP | No", "Require number matching ... | Enabled".
  - TAP: "Minimum lifetime | 1 hour", "Maximum lifetime | 8 hours", "Default lifetime | 1 hour", "One-time | No", "Length | 15 characters".
  
  **Design guidance** (`/design/platform/identity/authentication/`):
  - ML2/ML3: "FIDO2 Key / Windows Hello for Business (Pin Only) on organisational devices", with "Alternative Methods | Temporary Access Pass".
  - "Microsoft Authenticator is not phishing resistant."
  
  **Per-user MFA service settings** (`/configuration/entra-id/users/per-user-mfa/`):
  - "Do not allow users to create app passwords..."
  - "Remember multi-factor authentication on trusted device | Not checked"
  
  **Windows 11 hardening guide:** "hardware-based multi-factor authentication should be used for privileged users, remote access and any access to important or sensitive data repositories."
  
  ## 3. Privileged access
  
  **PIM design** (`/design/platform/identity/roles/`), verbatim decision table:
  - "Role activation model | Least Privilege via Privileged Identity Management"
  - "PIM role scope | All Entra roles"
  - "Approval workflow | Align approval requirements with the risk of each role's capabilities" (no fixed approval rule)
  - "Assignment type | Eligible assignment"
  - "Assignment duration | Maximum 365 days"
  - "Activation duration | Capped at 8 hours and restricted to the minimum necessary duration"
  - "Standing access exceptions | Permanent active assignment for break glass and specific service accounts"
  
  `/design/shared-services/microsoft-365/rbac/` adds "PIM | Configured" and lists the M365 roles PIM can assign.
  
  **Access reviews** (`/design/platform/identity/governance/`):
  - "Use 6-monthly access reviews for active and eligible assigned roles"
  - "Use 3-monthly access reviews for Conditional Access exclude groups"
  - "Use 6-monthly access reviews for role assigned groups"
  - "Access reviews for inactive users ... are not in implemented in the Blueprint."
  
  **Inactivity** (`/design/platform/identity/users/`): "ISM Security Controls 1404 and 1648 | Disable un-privileged and privileged user accounts after > 45 days of inactivity", done by "a custom script set to run on a scheduled basis". This conflicts with the E8 page (`/security-and-governance/essential-eight/restrict-administrative-privileges/`): "The Blueprint does not currently provide guidance for automating the disabling of accounts."
  
  **Break glass accounts** (same users page; config page `/configuration/entra-id/users/break-glass-accounts/`):
  - Two accounts, "cloud only accounts that use the `*.onmicrosoft.com` domain".
  - "Global Administrator role assigned permanently".
  - "Both Emergency access accounts will be excluded from MFA". The page's own bullet list instead says "At least one".
  - Monitored "via Defender for Cloud Apps".
  
  **Separate admin accounts:**
  - SSP template (`/security-and-governance/system-security-plan/personnel-security/`): "privileged users granted additional uniquely identifiable privileged accounts".
  - Same template: "an AppLocker blocklist is configured on workstations via Intune to prevent administrators from launching web browsers and email clients".
  - E8 page: "The Blueprint does not currently provide guidance for restricting privileged account activities." Its template text says privileged accounts "are restricted from accessing the internet, email and web services".
  
  **Silent on:**
  - Admin accounts without mailboxes or licences. `/design/shared-services/microsoft-365/licencing/` actually defines "Admin Licence Group | `rol-OrganisationName-Administrator`".
  - Cloud-only admin accounts other than break glass.
  
  **cyber.gov.au:**
  - Windows 11 guide: "separate standard and privileged accounts with different credentials ... privileged accounts used should have external web and email access blocked."
  - E8 ML2: "disabled after 12 months unless revalidated" and "disabled after 45 days of inactivity". ML3: "Just-in-time administration is used".
  
  ## 4. Smart lockout and password protection
  
  **Password protection** (`/configuration/entra-id/protection/authentication-methods/password-protection/`):
  - "Lockout threshold | 5"
  - "Lockout duration in seconds | 60"
  - "Enforce custom list | Yes"
  - "Custom banned password list | _as per organisation requirements_"
  - "Enable password protection on Windows Server Active Directory | Yes"
  - "Mode | Enforced"
  
  **Design** (`/design/platform/identity/protection/`) uses the same 5 and 60, with "Smart lockout duration automatically increases with subsequent lockouts." Password expiry: "Never" (authentication design page).
  
  **MFA account lockout** (`/configuration/entra-id/protection/risky-activities/multifactor-authentication/account-lockout/`): 3 denials, 300 minutes until the counter resets, 1440 minutes until the account is unblocked.
  
  **For contrast, the Windows guide's local/AD lockout (not Entra):** "Account lockout duration 0 / Account lockout threshold 5 invalid logon attempts / Reset account lockout counter after 15 minutes / Allow Administrator account lockout Enabled".
  
  ## 5. Intune ASR rules
  
  **Intune policy "ASD Windows Hardening Guidelines-Attack Surface Reduction"** (`/configuration/intune/endpoint-security/attack-surface-reduction/asd-windows-hardening-asr/`), assigned to All Devices. All 15 rules are set to **Block**:
  1. Adobe Reader child processes
  2. Obfuscated scripts
  3. Win32 API calls from Office macros
  4. LSASS credential stealing
  5. Prevalence/age/trusted list
  6. JS/VBS launching downloaded executables
  7. Office communication app child processes
  8. All Office apps creating child processes
  9. Untrusted/unsigned processes from USB
  10. PSExec/WMI process creation
  11. WMI event subscription persistence
  12. Office creating executable content
  13. Office injecting into other processes
  14. Advanced ransomware protection
  15. Executable content from email/webmail
  
  **Not in this policy:** vulnerable signed drivers, Webshell, copied/impersonated system tools, Safe Mode reboot.
  
  **Defender endpoint security policy page** (`/configuration/defender/endpoints/configuration-management/endpoint-security-policies/`) sets all 19 rules to Block. It adds Webshell, "[PREVIEW] Block use of copied or impersonated system tools", "Block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers (Device)" and "[PREVIEW] Block rebooting machine in Safe Mode". "Enable Controlled Folder Access" is _Not configured_.
  
  **No Audit or Warn mode appears anywhere** in the Blueprint.
  
  **cyber.gov.au:**
  - The Windows 10 and Windows 11 guides list 16 rules (the 15 above plus vulnerable signed drivers), each set to state "1" (Block).
  - The Office guide lists 6 rules, each "1": email/webmail executable content, Office child processes, executable content, code injection, Win32 API, Office communication app child processes.
  - E8 ML2: "Microsoft Office is blocked from creating child processes / ... executable content / ... injecting code into other processes".
  
  ## 6. Office macros
  
  **Blueprint design decision** (`/design/endpoints/windows/security/microsoft-office-macro-hardening/`): "Only macros digitally signed by a trusted publisher are enabled".
  
  **Intune policy "ASD Office hardening - macros enabled for trusted publishers"** (`/configuration/intune/devices/configuration-policies/asd-office-hardening-macros-enabled-for-trusted-publishers/`):
  - Per app: "Disable all except digitally signed macros", "VBA Macro Notification Settings (User) | Enabled", "Block macros from running in Office files from the Internet (User) | Enabled" (Access, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio, Word).
  - "Trust access to Visual Basic Project | Disabled", "Turn off trusted documents | Enabled", "Disable all trusted locations | Enabled", "Disable commands | Enabled, 19092".
  - Office-wide: "Macro Runtime Scan Scope (User) | Enabled, Enable for all documents", "Disable VBA for Office applications | Disabled", "Disable all Trust Bar notifications for security issues | Enabled", "Automation Security | Use application macro security level", "Allow mix of policy and user locations | Disabled".
  - Scan encrypted macros: Excel and PowerPoint say "Enabled, Scan encrypted macros (disabled)", Word says "(default)". The PowerPoint row is mislabelled "Excel Open XML workbooks".
  
  **Intune policy "ASD Office hardening - all macros disabled"** (`.../asd-office-hardening-all-macros-disabled/`):
  - "Disable all without notification"
  - "Disable VBA for Office applications | Enabled"
  - "Set the Automation Security level | Disable macros by default"
  - Outlook "Never warn, disable all"
  
  **Antivirus scanning:** the E8 page (`/security-and-governance/essential-eight/restrict-microsoft-office-macros/`) relies on Defender with AMSI. The Win32 API block is done "using Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules".
  
  **ASD macro guide (cyber.gov.au):**
  - Order of preference: "all macros are disabled / macros digitally signed by trusted publishers are enabled / macros from trusted locations are enabled / users decide ... (with additional security measures)".
  - For the trusted-publisher approach it also sets "Only trust VBA macros that use V3 signatures | Enabled", "Disable the Content page | Enabled" and MMC "Certificates | Disabled". Outlook: "Warn for signed, disable unsigned".
  - Win32 ASR rule 92E97FA1 is "(1)" for every approach except all-disabled (N/A).
  
  **Gaps in the Blueprint trusted-publisher Intune policy compared with ASD's guide:**
  - No V3-signature setting.
  - No Content page or Certificates snap-in settings.
  - No Outlook section. The design page does list Outlook "Warn for signed, disable unsigned".
  
  **E8 ML1:** "macros in files originating from the internet are blocked", "macro antivirus scanning is enabled", "macro security settings cannot be changed by users". ML2 adds "blocked from making Win32 API calls".
  
  ## 7. Internet Explorer 11
  
  **Blueprint:**
  - `/design/endpoints/windows/configuration/windows-features/`: "Internet Explorer 11 | Disabled | ... Note, this is not applicable to Windows 11."
  - It is removed by an Intune script (`/configuration/intune/devices/scripts/userapplicationhardening-removefeatures/`) running `Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName Internet-Explorer-Optional-amd64 -NoRestart` ("for Windows 10").
  - No "Disable Internet Explorer 11 as a standalone browser" policy exists anywhere in the Blueprint.
  - The Edge policy *enables* IE mode: "Configure Internet Explorer integration | Internet Explorer mode" with an Enterprise Mode Cloud Site List (`.../asd-edge-hardening/`).
  
  **ASD hardening guides:** no setting. They only say Edge "was introduced to replace Internet Explorer 11 ... should be used wherever possible."
  
  **E8 ML1–ML3:** "Internet Explorer 11 is disabled or removed."
  
  ## 8. Windows Update and patching
  
  **Blueprint** (`/design/platform/client/device-updates/`):
  - "Servicing Channel | General Availability Channel"
  - "Microsoft Product updates | Allow", "Windows Drivers | Allow"
  - "Quality Deferral period | 0 days", "Feature Deferral | 0 days"
  - "Feature Update uninstall period | 10 days"
  - "Expedite Updates Policy | Enabled for Zero Security Updates | Address extreme security risks within 48 hours"
  - Update ring settings: "Automatic Update Behaviour: `Reset to default`", "Change Notification Update Level: `Turn off all notifications including restart warnings`", "Enable Pre-release: _Not configured_".

  ## Where the Blueprint is silent
  
  - A separate admin MFA or strength policy, and an admin role list outside the DSC.
