  # What ASD specifies for the Essential Eight and ISM M365 checks
  
  **Sources read:**
  - The Blueprint GitHub repo (github.com/ASD-Blueprint/ASD-Blueprint-for-Secure-Cloud, HEAD a6e1e5f, 18 Sep 2026). Live pages at blueprint.asd.gov.au were spot-checked and match it. URLs below are `https://blueprint.asd.gov.au/<path>/`.
  - cyber.gov.au:
    - *Hardening Microsoft Windows 11 workstations*, last reviewed 23 Jan 2026 (the Windows 10 version, 4 Sep 2025, has the same ASR and IE text).
    - *Hardening Microsoft 365, Office 2021, Office 2019 and Office 2016*, 24 Jul 2023.
    - *Restricting Microsoft Office macros*, 27 Nov 2023. The "Microsoft Office macro security" URL now redirects here.
    - *Essential Eight maturity model*, 27 Nov 2023.
  
  **Caveats that apply throughout:**
  - Every Blueprint config page carries this disclaimer: "Any implementation implied by these pages should not be considered as prescriptive as to how an organisation must scope, build, document, or assess a system."
  - The CA policies index page says: "All Conditional Access policies in the DSC are set to report only and will need to be enabled manually." The individual policy pages say "Enable policy | On".
  
  ---
  
  ## 1. Conditional Access
  
  The policy pages are under `/configuration/entra-id/protection/conditional-access/policies/`. There are 16 policies:
  
  | Policy | Users | Resources | Control |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | USR - G - Require strong auth | All users | All resources | Built-in "Phishing-resistant MFA" |
  | USR - G - Register security info with strong auth | All users | User action "Register security information" | Custom "Phishing-resistant MFA and TAP" |
  | USR - G - Risky sign-ins with strong auth | All users, sign-in risk Low + Medium | All resources | Phishing-resistant MFA |
  | USR - B - Block high-risk sign-ins | All users, sign-in risk High | All resources | Block |
  | USR - B - Block high-risk users | All users, user risk High | All resources | Block |
  | USR - B - Block users with elevated insider risk | All users, insider risk Elevated | All resources | Block |
  | USR - B - Block access via legacy auth | All users, client apps "Exchange ActiveSync clients" + "Other clients" | All resources | Block |
  | USR - B - Block access to PROTECTED information | `<PROTECTED users group>` excluded | Authentication context "PROTECTED information" | Block |
  | USR - G - Agreement to terms of use | All users | All resources | Terms |
  | USR - S - Limit user sessions | All users, excluding admin roles and `<Administrative user group>` | All resources | Sign-in frequency 12 hours |
  | ADM - S - Limit admin sessions | Admin roles + `<Administrative user group>` | All resources | Sign-in frequency 4 hours |
  | DEV - G - Compliant devices | All users | All resources | Require device to be marked as compliant |
  | DEV - B - Block access from unapproved devices | All users; platforms Android, Windows Phone, macOS, Linux | All resources | Block |
  | DEV - G - Intune enrolment with strong auth | All users | Microsoft Intune + Microsoft Intune Enrolment | Phishing-resistant MFA |
  | GST - B - Block guests | All 6 guest/external types, excluding `<Guest application user group>` | All resources | Block |
  | GST - G - Guest `<application>` access with strong auth | Guests | `<application>` | Phishing-resistant MFA |
  | LOC - B - Block access from unapproved countries | All users | All resources | Block, excluding "Allowed Countries" |
  
  **The "MFA for all users" policy.** On `.../policies/strong-authentication/`:
  - "Include | All users"
  - Exclude: "Users and groups | Checked | `<CA exclude group - USR - G - Require strong auth>`"
  - "Guest or external users | Not checked" and "Directory roles | Not checked" (under Exclude)
  - "All resources (formerly 'All cloud apps')", with "Exclude | None"
  - "Require multifactor authentication | Not checked"
  - "Require authentication strength | Phishing-resistant MFA: Checked"
  
  So the built-in strength applies to **all users**.
  
  On `/design/platform/identity/conditional-access/`:
  - "Require strong authentication for users | Enforce phishing-resistant MFA for all users"
  - "Authentication strengths for user access | Use phishing-resistant MFA | Comply with Essential Eight requirements"
  
  **Exclusions** (same design page):
  - "Use separate exclude groups for each Conditional Access policy"
  - "Use Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for exclude group membership changes"
  - "Exclude Break glass accounts from Conditional Access policy control"
  
  **There is no separate admin MFA policy.** The only ADM policy is the 4-hour session policy. On `.../policies/limit-admin-sessions/`:
  - "Directory roles | Checked | _Select applicable administrator roles_" plus `<Administrative user group>`
  - "Periodic reauthentication | 4 hours"
  - No grant control
  
  The page does not name the roles. The design page says: "Use groups as well as roles to identity administrative users".
  
  The Microsoft-managed policies are all set Off as "superseded by Blueprint policies". They include "Multifactor authentication for admins accessing Microsoft Admin Portals", "Require multifactor authentication for admins" and "Require multifactor authentication for all users".
  
  On `/design/platform/identity/authentication/`: "MFA for Administration | Configured | Administration through Microsoft 365 administration portals and other Cloud Apps should require MFA."
  
  **The only concrete admin role list is in the DSC file** (`/content/files/automation/dsc/BlueprintEntraDsc.txt`, Microsoft365DSC 1.24.717.1). Its `ADM - S - Limit admin sessions` IncludeRoles (and `USR - S` ExcludeRoles) lists 73 roles: essentially every "... Administrator" role, Global Administrator included, plus `$PrivUsers`.
  
  The DSC also disagrees with the docs in places:
  - `ADM - S - Limit admin sessions` and `DEV - G - Compliant devices` have `IncludeApplications = @("None")`, where the pages say "All resources".
  - Every DSC policy is `State = "enabledForReportingButNotEnforced"`.
  
  ## 2. Authentication strengths
  
  **The one custom strength.** On `/configuration/entra-id/protection/conditional-access/authentication-strengths/`:
  - Name: "Phishing-resistant MFA and TAP"
  - Phishing-resistant MFA: "Windows Hello For Business / Passkeys (FIDO2) / Certificate-based Authentication (Multifactor)"
  - Multifactor authentication: "Temporary Access Pass (One-time use) / Temporary Access Pass (Multi-use)"
  
  Only the Register security info policy uses it. Every other grant uses the built-in "Phishing-resistant MFA". Design page: "Authentication strengths for bootstrapping flows | Use phishing-resistant MFA plus temporary access passes (TAPs)".
  
  **Authentication methods policy** (`/configuration/entra-id/protection/authentication-methods/policies/`):
  - Enabled for "All users, excluding `<Conditional Access excluded identities>`": Passkey (FIDO2), Microsoft Authenticator, Temporary Access Pass.
  - Disabled ("No"): SMS, Hardware OATH, Third-party software OATH, Voice call, Email OTP, Certificate-based authentication. Note that CBA is disabled here although the custom strength includes it.
  - FIDO2: "Enforce attestation | Yes", "Enforce key restrictions | Yes", "Restrict specific keys | Allow", `<Organisation AAGUIDs>`.
  - Authenticator: "Allow use of Microsoft Authenticator OTP | No", "Require number matching ... | Enabled".
  - TAP: "Minimum lifetime | 1 hour", "Maximum lifetime | 8 hours", "Default lifetime | 1 hour", "One-time | No", "Length | 15 characters".
  
  **Design guidance** (`/design/platform/identity/authentication/`):
  - ML2/ML3: "FIDO2 Key / Windows Hello for Business (Pin Only) on organisational devices", with "Alternative Methods | Temporary Access Pass".
  - "Microsoft Authenticator is not phishing resistant."
  
  **Per-user MFA service settings** (`/configuration/entra-id/users/per-user-mfa/`):
  - "Do not allow users to create app passwords..."
  - "Remember multi-factor authentication on trusted device | Not checked"
  
  **Windows 11 hardening guide:** "hardware-based multi-factor authentication should be used for privileged users, remote access and any access to important or sensitive data repositories."
  
  ## 3. Privileged access
  
  **PIM design** (`/design/platform/identity/roles/`), verbatim decision table:
  - "Role activation model | Least Privilege via Privileged Identity Management"
  - "PIM role scope | All Entra roles"
  - "Approval workflow | Align approval requirements with the risk of each role's capabilities" (no fixed approval rule)
  - "Assignment type | Eligible assignment"
  - "Assignment duration | Maximum 365 days"
  - "Activation duration | Capped at 8 hours and restricted to the minimum necessary duration"
  - "Standing access exceptions | Permanent active assignment for break glass and specific service accounts"
  
  `/design/shared-services/microsoft-365/rbac/` adds "PIM | Configured" and lists the M365 roles PIM can assign.
  
  **Access reviews** (`/design/platform/identity/governance/`):
  - "Use 6-monthly access reviews for active and eligible assigned roles"
  - "Use 3-monthly access reviews for Conditional Access exclude groups"
  - "Use 6-monthly access reviews for role assigned groups"
  - "Access reviews for inactive users ... are not in implemented in the Blueprint."
  
  **Inactivity** (`/design/platform/identity/users/`): "ISM Security Controls 1404 and 1648 | Disable un-privileged and privileged user accounts after > 45 days of inactivity", done by "a custom script set to run on a scheduled basis". This conflicts with the E8 page (`/security-and-governance/essential-eight/restrict-administrative-privileges/`): "The Blueprint does not currently provide guidance for automating the disabling of accounts."
  
  **Break glass accounts** (same users page; config page `/configuration/entra-id/users/break-glass-accounts/`):
  - Two accounts, "cloud only accounts that use the `*.onmicrosoft.com` domain".
  - "Global Administrator role assigned permanently".
  - "Both Emergency access accounts will be excluded from MFA". The page's own bullet list instead says "At least one".
  - Monitored "via Defender for Cloud Apps".
  
  **Separate admin accounts:**
  - SSP template (`/security-and-governance/system-security-plan/personnel-security/`): "privileged users granted additional uniquely identifiable privileged accounts".
  - Same template: "an AppLocker blocklist is configured on workstations via Intune to prevent administrators from launching web browsers and email clients".
  - E8 page: "The Blueprint does not currently provide guidance for restricting privileged account activities." Its template text says privileged accounts "are restricted from accessing the internet, email and web services".
  
  **Silent on:**
  - Admin accounts without mailboxes or licences. `/design/shared-services/microsoft-365/licencing/` actually defines "Admin Licence Group | `rol-OrganisationName-Administrator`".
  - Cloud-only admin accounts other than break glass.
  
  **cyber.gov.au:**
  - Windows 11 guide: "separate standard and privileged accounts with different credentials ... privileged accounts used should have external web and email access blocked."
  - E8 ML2: "disabled after 12 months unless revalidated" and "disabled after 45 days of inactivity". ML3: "Just-in-time administration is used".
  
  ## 4. Smart lockout and password protection
  
  **Password protection** (`/configuration/entra-id/protection/authentication-methods/password-protection/`):
  - "Lockout threshold | 5"
  - "Lockout duration in seconds | 60"
  - "Enforce custom list | Yes"
  - "Custom banned password list | _as per organisation requirements_"
  - "Enable password protection on Windows Server Active Directory | Yes"
  - "Mode | Enforced"
  
  **Design** (`/design/platform/identity/protection/`) uses the same 5 and 60, with "Smart lockout duration automatically increases with subsequent lockouts." Password expiry: "Never" (authentication design page).
  
  **MFA account lockout** (`/configuration/entra-id/protection/risky-activities/multifactor-authentication/account-lockout/`): 3 denials, 300 minutes until the counter resets, 1440 minutes until the account is unblocked.
  
  **For contrast, the Windows guide's local/AD lockout (not Entra):** "Account lockout duration 0 / Account lockout threshold 5 invalid logon attempts / Reset account lockout counter after 15 minutes / Allow Administrator account lockout Enabled".
  
  ## 5. Intune ASR rules
  
  **Intune policy "ASD Windows Hardening Guidelines-Attack Surface Reduction"** (`/configuration/intune/endpoint-security/attack-surface-reduction/asd-windows-hardening-asr/`), assigned to All Devices. All 15 rules are set to **Block**:
  1. Adobe Reader child processes
  2. Obfuscated scripts
  3. Win32 API calls from Office macros
  4. LSASS credential stealing
  5. Prevalence/age/trusted list
  6. JS/VBS launching downloaded executables
  7. Office communication app child processes
  8. All Office apps creating child processes
  9. Untrusted/unsigned processes from USB
  10. PSExec/WMI process creation
  11. WMI event subscription persistence
  12. Office creating executable content
  13. Office injecting into other processes
  14. Advanced ransomware protection
  15. Executable content from email/webmail
  
  **Not in this policy:** vulnerable signed drivers, Webshell, copied/impersonated system tools, Safe Mode reboot.
  
  **Defender endpoint security policy page** (`/configuration/defender/endpoints/configuration-management/endpoint-security-policies/`) sets all 19 rules to Block. It adds Webshell, "[PREVIEW] Block use of copied or impersonated system tools", "Block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers (Device)" and "[PREVIEW] Block rebooting machine in Safe Mode". "Enable Controlled Folder Access" is _Not configured_.
  
  **No Audit or Warn mode appears anywhere** in the Blueprint.
  
  **cyber.gov.au:**
  - The Windows 10 and Windows 11 guides list 16 rules (the 15 above plus vulnerable signed drivers), each set to state "1" (Block).
  - The Office guide lists 6 rules, each "1": email/webmail executable content, Office child processes, executable content, code injection, Win32 API, Office communication app child processes.
  - E8 ML2: "Microsoft Office is blocked from creating child processes / ... executable content / ... injecting code into other processes".
  
  ## 6. Office macros
  
  **Blueprint design decision** (`/design/endpoints/windows/security/microsoft-office-macro-hardening/`): "Only macros digitally signed by a trusted publisher are enabled".
  
  **Intune policy "ASD Office hardening - macros enabled for trusted publishers"** (`/configuration/intune/devices/configuration-policies/asd-office-hardening-macros-enabled-for-trusted-publishers/`):
  - Per app: "Disable all except digitally signed macros", "VBA Macro Notification Settings (User) | Enabled", "Block macros from running in Office files from the Internet (User) | Enabled" (Access, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio, Word).
  - "Trust access to Visual Basic Project | Disabled", "Turn off trusted documents | Enabled", "Disable all trusted locations | Enabled", "Disable commands | Enabled, 19092".
  - Office-wide: "Macro Runtime Scan Scope (User) | Enabled, Enable for all documents", "Disable VBA for Office applications | Disabled", "Disable all Trust Bar notifications for security issues | Enabled", "Automation Security | Use application macro security level", "Allow mix of policy and user locations | Disabled".
  - Scan encrypted macros: Excel and PowerPoint say "Enabled, Scan encrypted macros (disabled)", Word says "(default)". The PowerPoint row is mislabelled "Excel Open XML workbooks".
  
  **Intune policy "ASD Office hardening - all macros disabled"** (`.../asd-office-hardening-all-macros-disabled/`):
  - "Disable all without notification"
  - "Disable VBA for Office applications | Enabled"
  - "Set the Automation Security level | Disable macros by default"
  - Outlook "Never warn, disable all"
  
  **Antivirus scanning:** the E8 page (`/security-and-governance/essential-eight/restrict-microsoft-office-macros/`) relies on Defender with AMSI. The Win32 API block is done "using Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules".
  
  **ASD macro guide (cyber.gov.au):**
  - Order of preference: "all macros are disabled / macros digitally signed by trusted publishers are enabled / macros from trusted locations are enabled / users decide ... (with additional security measures)".
  - For the trusted-publisher approach it also sets "Only trust VBA macros that use V3 signatures | Enabled", "Disable the Content page | Enabled" and MMC "Certificates | Disabled". Outlook: "Warn for signed, disable unsigned".
  - Win32 ASR rule 92E97FA1 is "(1)" for every approach except all-disabled (N/A).
  
  **Gaps in the Blueprint trusted-publisher Intune policy compared with ASD's guide:**
  - No V3-signature setting.
  - No Content page or Certificates snap-in settings.
  - No Outlook section. The design page does list Outlook "Warn for signed, disable unsigned".
  
  **E8 ML1:** "macros in files originating from the internet are blocked", "macro antivirus scanning is enabled", "macro security settings cannot be changed by users". ML2 adds "blocked from making Win32 API calls".
  
  ## 7. Internet Explorer 11
  
  **Blueprint:**
  - `/design/endpoints/windows/configuration/windows-features/`: "Internet Explorer 11 | Disabled | ... Note, this is not applicable to Windows 11."
  - It is removed by an Intune script (`/configuration/intune/devices/scripts/userapplicationhardening-removefeatures/`) running `Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName Internet-Explorer-Optional-amd64 -NoRestart` ("for Windows 10").
  - No "Disable Internet Explorer 11 as a standalone browser" policy exists anywhere in the Blueprint.
  - The Edge policy *enables* IE mode: "Configure Internet Explorer integration | Internet Explorer mode" with an Enterprise Mode Cloud Site List (`.../asd-edge-hardening/`).
  
  **ASD hardening guides:** no setting. They only say Edge "was introduced to replace Internet Explorer 11 ... should be used wherever possible."
  
  **E8 ML1–ML3:** "Internet Explorer 11 is disabled or removed."
  
  ## 8. Windows Update and patching
  
  **Blueprint** (`/design/platform/client/device-updates/`):
  - "Servicing Channel | General Availability Channel"
  - "Microsoft Product updates | Allow", "Windows Drivers | Allow"
  - "Quality Deferral period | 0 days", "Feature Deferral | 0 days"
  - "Feature Update uninstall period | 10 days"
  - "Expedite Updates Policy | Enabled for Zero Security Updates | Address extreme security risks within 48 hours"
  - Update ring settings: "Automatic Update Behaviour: `Reset to default`", "Change Notification Update Level: `Turn off all notifications including restart warnings`", "Enable Pre-release: _Not configured_".
  
  **The Blueprint is silent on:**
  - Quality and feature update deadlines.
  - Grace periods and auto-restart.
  - Any Intune update-ring configuration page.
  
  **Patching frequency** (`/design/endpoints/windows/configuration/windows-update-and-patching/`): "applied two weeks of release, or within 48 hours if an exploit exists". That matches E8's internet-facing timeframe, not its workstation one.
  
  **ASD Windows 11 guide (Group Policy):**
  - "Configure Automatic Updates | Enabled | 4 - Auto download and schedule the install | Scheduled install day: 0 - Every day"
  - "Install updates for other Microsoft products"
  - "Remove access to "Pause updates" feature | Enabled"
  - "Remove access to use all Windows Update features | Disabled"
  - "Allow Updates in OOBE | Enabled"
  - No deadlines.
  
  **E8 workstation operating systems:** "within one month of release" at ML1 and ML2. At ML3: "within 48 hours ... when ... critical ... or when working exploits exist", otherwise "within one month".
  
  ---
  
  ## Every concrete value ASD names
  
  **Conditional Access:**
  - Built-in "Phishing-resistant MFA" strength for all users, all resources, with only a per-policy exclude group.
  - Custom "Phishing-resistant MFA and TAP" (WHfB, FIDO2, CBA multifactor, TAP one-time and multi-use), used only for registering security info.
  - Admin sign-in frequency 4 hours; user sign-in frequency 12 hours.
  - Risky sign-ins: Low and Medium require phishing-resistant MFA; High is blocked. High user risk is blocked.
  - Legacy auth: block Exchange ActiveSync + Other clients.
  - Allowed device platforms: Windows and iOS only (Android, Windows Phone, macOS and Linux blocked).
  - Microsoft-managed admin and all-user MFA policies set Off.
  - 73-role admin list (DSC only).
  
  **Authentication methods:**
  - FIDO2 with attestation and an AAGUID allow list.
  - Authenticator push with number matching, OTP off.
  - TAP 1 hour minimum, 8 hours maximum, 1 hour default, length 15, not one-time.
  - SMS, voice, email OTP, hardware OATH, software OATH and CBA disabled.
  - App passwords off; remember MFA off.
  
  **PIM:**
  - All Entra roles; eligible assignment only.
  - Assignments up to 365 days; activation capped at 8 hours.
  - Approval by role risk (no fixed rule); permanent active only for break glass and service accounts.
  
  **Access reviews:** 6-monthly for roles and role-assigned groups; 3-monthly for CA exclude groups.
  
  **Inactivity:** disable after more than 45 days (ISM 1404 and 1648).
  
  **Break glass:** 2 accounts, *.onmicrosoft.com, permanent Global Administrator, excluded from MFA and CA.

---
name: map-benchmarks-to-existing-tests
description: New benchmark suites should map requirements onto existing tests instead of re-implementing the same check
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When a contributed benchmark suite (e.g. ASD Essential Eight/ISM, PR 2552) re-implements a setting that a CIS, CISA, MT or EIDSCA test already reads, the owner prefers adding the benchmark's requirement to the existing test's `Control` over a new test or variant. A separate test is justified only where the benchmark's own sources name a concrete different value (e.g. ISM 45 days, lockout 5 vs CIS 10); even then, share the data-reading helper.

**Why:** keeps checks generic, avoids two tests disagreeing on one setting, and keeps suite-named helpers (`Get-MtAsd*`) out of reusable code.

**How to apply:** when reviewing a benchmark PR, check the benchmark's primary sources (control text, assessment guide, reference build) for specifics before accepting a duplicate; recommend mapping where it is generic. Note that Maester has no framework selector yet, so mapped tests don't run under `-Suite <benchmark>`. Related: [[maester-3-design]].

content.text:
You were right about the ISM. The controls say what to achieve, not how. Where ASD does get specific (in its assessment guide and its reference build, the ASD Blueprint for Secure Cloud), it agrees with either CIS or CISA in every overlapping case, so those controls can map to an existing test. The only places ASD names its own value are the 45-day inactivity limit and the lockout threshold of 5.

## Checks that overlap existing tests

| ASD control | What ASD says | Where it lands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **ISM-1504** MFA for online services | All human users, any MFA except biometrics at ML1. No Conditional Access design. | **Map to CIS 5.2.2.2.** It's the strictest of the existing checks: it also rejects policies narrowed by platform or location. |
| **ISM-1872** Phishing-resistant MFA | All users, privileged and unprivileged. The examples given are "a security key, smart card or passkey". The Blueprint's only sign-in policy is the built-in Phishing-resistant MFA strength for All users and All resources. | **Map to CISA.MS.AAD.3.1**, which matches the Blueprint exactly. The ASD helper does one thing better: it matches the built-in strength by ID, where CISA matches the display name. Fix that in CISA 3.1 instead of keeping a second test. |
| **ISM-1649** Just-in-time admin | The assessment guide says access is granted "immediately before that access is required and for only as long as it is required". The Blueprint makes every Entra role eligible-only, with permanent active assignments only for break-glass and specific service accounts. | **Map to CIS 5.3.1**, which fails any standing active assignment. The PR's check (and CISA 7.4) only fails permanent ones, so it would pass a 6-month active assignment that the Blueprint doesn't allow. |
| **ISM-1173 / ISM-0974** MFA for users of systems | ASD assesses these by watching someone sign in **to a workstation**. | **Don't map them to a Conditional Access test.** Admin MFA in online services is already covered by 1504 and 1872, which apply to all users. The Blueprint has no separate admin MFA policy. |
| **ISM-0445 / ISM-1175** Dedicated admin accounts | The control text is generic. ASD's test for 1175 is an admin account that has an email address or mailbox. | MT.1028 only covers permanent control-plane assignments, so an eligible Global Administrator with a mailbox passes it. **Keep the check, but as a general MT test** (privileged users should not have a mailbox), mapped to ISM-1175. |
| **ISM-1648** Inactive privileged access | **45 days.** | **Keep it in the ASD suite.** MT.1029 relies on the PIM alert, whose day count the tenant sets (1–365). Use `Get-MtRoleMember` instead of `Get-MtAsdPrivilegedUser`. |
| **ISM-1403** Lockout threshold | **5 or fewer.** The Blueprint sets 5 attempts with a 60-second lockout. CIS and EIDSCA pass at 10. | **Keep it, sharing a helper with CIS 5.2.3.8.** One helper in `internal/services/entra` returns the threshold; each test compares it against its own number. |

## The Intune checks

All 8 are new, and ASD is specific about each one. Four have bugs against ASD's own assessment guide:

- **ISM-1667** checks one ASR rule. The guide requires two, and the PR is missing *Block Office communication application from creating child processes*.
- **ISM-1668** has the same problem: it is missing *Block executable content from email client and webmail*.
- **ISM-1654** passes only when the "Disable IE11 as a standalone browser" setting is configured. The Blueprint removes IE11 with a script instead, and says IE11 doesn't apply to Windows 11. A tenant built to ASD's own Blueprint would fail it.
- **ISM-1672** passes scanning for low-trust documents only. ASD's macro guide and the Blueprint both set "Enable for all documents"; the assessment guide calls that setting "Ideal".

The ASR helper correctly requires Block, as ASD does. It should still move to `internal/services/intune` under a general name, so MT.1178 can use it later.

## The open decision

Maester has no way to select tests by framework. With mapping, `-Suite asd` would run only the ASD-specific tests (ISM-1648, ISM-1403 and the 8 Intune checks). The mapped controls would carry `essential-eight:ISM-xxxx` in their results but wouldn't run in an ASD-only run. To make mapping complete we'd want a `-Framework essential-eight` selector. I'd build that as its own PR rather than inside #2552.

I saved a memory that benchmark suites should map onto existing tests unless ASD (or the benchmark) names a different value.

Sources:
- [ISM, September 2026](https://www.cyber.gov.au/ism/2026-09) and the [ISM OSCAL catalogue](https://github.com/AustralianCyberSecurityCentre/ism-oscal)
- [Essential Eight assessment process guide](https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/essential-eight/essential-eight-assessment-process-guide)
- [Essential Eight maturity model and ISM mapping](https://www.cyber.gov.au/publication/essential-eight-maturity-model-and-ism-mapping)
- [ASD Blueprint: Require strong auth policy](https://blueprint.asd.gov.au/configuration/entra-id/protection/conditional-access/policies/strong-authentication/), [roles and PIM design](https://blueprint.asd.gov.au/design/platform/identity/roles/), [password protection](https://blueprint.asd.gov.au/configuration/entra-id/protection/authentication-methods/password-protection/)
- [Restricting Microsoft Office macros](https://www.cyber.gov.au/publication/restricting-microsoft-office-macros)
- [Hardening Microsoft 365, Office 2021, 2019 and 2016](https://www.cyber.gov.au/publication/hardening-microsoft-365-office-2021-office-2019-and-office-2016)
- [CISA SCuBA Entra baseline](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/blob/main/PowerShell/ScubaGear/baselines/aad.md)
- [PIM security alerts](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-how-to-configure-security-alerts)

content.content:
internal/                         Not exported
    engine/                         Discovery, selection, planning and execution of tests
    session/                        Module state, configuration, versions, progress and telemetry
    connect/                        Connection checks and consent help
    report/                         Result conversion, Markdown reports, affected objects
    app/                            Helpers for the Maester Entra app
    packs/                          Pack manifests, the lock file and store, the loader gate and connectors
    services/<service>/             Reusable data access for one service (the GitHub client, Graph caching, ...)
    checks/<suite>/<service>/       Helpers used by the checks of one suite
    generated/eidsca/  orca/        Generated; regenerate, never edit
    utility/                        Small helpers with no domain (query strings, object properties, prompts)
  assets/  lib/  tools/             Data files, the compiled engine, developer tools
  tests/                            Unit tests of the module itself
  because that is what an author knows when adding a check and what an admin knows when looking for one. Themes
  that cut across products, such as AI, are the `Area` attribute of a test: Copilot Studio agent checks live in
  `maester/copilot-studio/`, an Entra agent identity check lives in `maester/entra/`, and both declare
  `Area = 'ai'`, so `Invoke-Maester -Area ai` runs them together. A theme folder such as `ai/` would end up
  holding checks for Copilot, Copilot Studio, Foundry, Entra Agent ID and Purview, each with its own API, portal
  and permissions.
- **Data access is shared, check logic is not.** Code that reads a service (`services/`) is reused by many checks and
  by custom tests. Code that only one suite's checks need stays in `checks/<suite>/`.

### Making an internal helper public

Custom tests are loaded into their own private module, so they can call only the commands Maester exports. When
users need one of the internal helpers in their own tests, promote it instead of copying it:

1. Move the file from `powershell/internal/services/<service>/` to `powershell/public/services/<service>/` with
   `git mv`, so its history follows it.
2. Add the function to `FunctionsToExport` in `powershell/Maester.psd1`.
3. Give it complete comment-based help: synopsis, description, every parameter, at least one example and a
   `.LINK` to `https://maester.dev/docs/commands/<Name>`. The command reference page is generated from it.
4. Review the name and parameters before you merge. Once a command is exported it is public API: renaming it,
   removing a parameter or changing what it returns is a breaking change for users' tests.

`Manifest.Tests.ps1` fails if a file in `public/` is not exported or an internal function is, and `Help.Tests.ps1`
fails if an exported command's help is incomplete, so a half-finished promotion does not pass CI. Helpers that
belong to one suite's checks (`internal/checks/`) are not candidates: move the reusable part into
`services/<service>/` first.

## Maester PowerShell module dev guide

lastPrompt: how would we refactor these? Should we create new tests for ASD but they are just a shim that call into the other tests? that way if they diverge from cis or CISA we just have to update the thin layer…

content.text:
Yes, use shims. I'd have each one call the CIS or CISA test function directly, rather than adding a shared layer underneath both. That's simpler, and Maester already does it: CISA.MS.AAD.3.2 calls `Test-MtCisaPhishResistant`. All built-in tests load into the Maester module, so any of them can call another.

**Why shims beat mapping alone.** A result row has a single `Benchmark`, built from the first `Control` it can resolve. If we only added `essential-eight:ISM-1504` to CIS 5.2.2.2, that row would still show CIS's benchmark details, and the Essential Eight maturity level and strategy would never appear on any row. With a shim, every ASD requirement gets its own row carrying its maturity level, and `-Suite asd` works without a new `-Framework` selector. The cost is a second row for the same setting in a full run. Maester already accepts that: MT.1007, CIS 5.2.2.2 and CISA 3.2 read the same policy today. Graph responses are cached, so a shim adds no extra calls.

**A shim looks like this:**

```powershell
function Test-MtAsdSmartLockoutThreshold {
    <# help, including the ASD wording and why it calls the CIS check #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'ASD.ISM-1403',
        Title = 'User accounts are protected by lockout mechanisms aligned to a maximum of five failed logon attempts.',
        # Product, Feature, Area, ResourceType, Severity, UserImpact, ImplementationCost, Mitre, Service
        # and License as in CIS.M365.5.2.3.8
        Control = ('ism:ISM-1403', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-7'),
        Author = 'jusso-dev'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # The most failed sign-ins allowed before an account is locked. ASD sets five; CIS allows ten.
        [ValidateRange(1, 50)]
        [int] $MaximumLockoutThreshold = 5
    )

    return Test-MtCisSmartLockoutThreshold -MaximumLockoutThreshold $MaximumLockoutThreshold
}
```

None of the CIS or CISA tests we'd call mention their benchmark in their result text, so the ASD rows read correctly.

**What each ASD check becomes**

| ASD check | Becomes | Logic |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ISM-1504 | Shim | `Test-MtCisMfaForEveryUser` (CIS 5.2.2.2) |
| ISM-1872 | Shim | `Test-MtCisaPhishResistant` (CISA 3.1). First fix CISA 3.1 to match the built-in strength by ID, not display name. |
| ISM-1649 | Shim | `Test-MtCisPrivilegedRolesActivatedNotAssigned` (CIS 5.3.1). Remove the `essential-eight:ISM-1649` the PR adds to CIS 5.3.1, so each requirement is claimed in one place. |
| ISM-1403 | Shim with ASD's value | `Test-MtCisSmartLockoutThreshold -MaximumLockoutThreshold 5` |
| ISM-1648 | Own test | ASD's 45 days. Uses `Get-MtRoleMember` instead of `Get-MtAsdPrivilegedUser`. |
| ISM-0445 | Own test, renamed ISM-1175 | ASD tests 1175 as "admin account with a mailbox". MT.1028 only covers permanent control-plane assignments, so it's too narrow to call. |
| ISM-1173 | Dropped | ASD assesses it at workstation sign-in, not Conditional Access. |
| 8 Intune checks | Own tests | Fix ISM-1667, 1668, 1654 and 1672 as described earlier. Move the ASR helper to `internal/services/intune` under a general name. |

`Get-MtAsdMfaPolicy` and `Get-MtAsdPrivilegedUser` are deleted, so no ASD-named helper is left.

**Two guardrails would keep the shims thin:**

1. **A pairing unit test.** It lists each shim with the test it calls, and fails if the called function is gone or any attribute differs: Product, Feature, Area, ResourceType, Severity, UserImpact, ImplementationCost, Mitre, Service or License. The rubric already says the same check in two suites gets the same values; this makes drift a test failure instead of something the review bot has to catch. The list also shows anyone changing CIS 5.2.2.2 that an ASD test depends on it.
2. **A sentence in the contributing guide.** It currently says "Data access is shared, check logic is not." That needs an exception: a benchmark test may call another suite's test when both benchmarks ask for the same thing.

**What happens when the two diverge:**

- **ASD changes its guidance:** replace the shim's one line with ASD-specific logic and remove its row from the pairing test.
- **CIS changes its test for a new benchmark version:** the ASD row follows without anyone noticing. The pairing test makes that dependency visible, but it can't judge whether the new CIS rule still fits ASD. So whoever reviews a CIS update needs to check the shims listed against it.

content.content:
﻿Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate users to the organisation's online services (ISM-1504, Essential Eight Maturity Level One; ISM-0974 for unprivileged users at Maturity Level Two).

A password alone is defeated by phishing, password spray and credential stuffing. Requiring a second factor for every user on every cloud app is the first Essential Eight requirement for multi-factor authentication, and the baseline the phishing-resistant requirements of Maturity Level Two build on. This check looks for an enabled Conditional Access policy that targets all users and all cloud apps and grants access only with multi-factor authentication or an authentication strength that satisfies it.

#### Remediation action

1. In **Microsoft Entra admin center**, go to **Protection** > **[Conditional Access](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies)** and create a policy.
2. **Users**: include **All users**; exclude only your emergency access accounts.
3. **Target resources**: **All resources (formerly 'All cloud apps')**.
4. **Grant**: **Require multifactor authentication**, or **Require authentication strength** with at least **Multifactor authentication**.
5. Enable the policy in **Report-only** first, then **On**.

#### Related links

* [Essential Eight Maturity Model](https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/essential-eight/essential-eight-maturity-model)
* [ISM Guidelines for system access: Multi-factor authentication](https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/ism/cyber-security-guidelines/guidelines-system-access)
* [Common Conditional Access policy: Require MFA for all users](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-all-users-mfa-strength)

<!--- Results --->
%TestResult%

--- CIS 5.2.2.2 md
﻿An enabled Conditional Access policy requires multifactor authentication for all users, in all cloud apps.

Passwords are the most common way into Microsoft 365 accounts: they are phished, reused, guessed and sprayed. Requiring a second factor for every user at sign-in blocks most of these attacks even when the password is known.

The policy must target all users and all resources, require MFA or an authentication strength, and be enabled. Policies that apply only at a certain risk level, or that are in report-only mode, do not satisfy the test. Excluding emergency access accounts is expected.

User and group exclusions are not evaluated by this test. Application exclusions are also not evaluated when the policy targets all apps; verify exclusions are documented and reviewed annually. A condition that narrows the policy is reported unless the check is about that condition.

#### Remediation action

1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > [**Policies**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies) and select **New policy**.
3. Under **Users**, include **All users**. Exclude your emergency access accounts.
4. Under **Target resources**, select **All resources (formerly All cloud apps)**.
5. Under **Grant**, select **Grant access** and **Require multifactor authentication** (or **Require authentication strength**).
6. Set **Enable policy** to **On** (use **Report-only** first to measure the impact) and select **Create**.

#### Related links

* [Microsoft Entra admin center - Conditional Access policies](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies)
* [Require multifactor authentication for all users with Conditional Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/howto-conditional-access-policy-all-users-mfa)
* [Plan a Conditional Access deployment](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/plan-conditional-access)
* [CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark v7.0.0 - 5.2.2.2](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/microsoft_365)

<!--- Results --->
%TestResult%

content.content:
﻿Just-in-time administration is used for the administration of systems and their resources (ISM-1649, Essential Eight Maturity Level Three; supports ISM-1508).

A permanently assigned administrator role is a standing target: whoever holds the account holds the tenant, around the clock. With Privileged Identity Management, administrators are eligible for a role and activate it for a few hours when they need it, with MFA, justification and an audit trail. This check reads the active assignments of every directory role that Microsoft Entra marks as privileged and fails on each one that is permanent, that is, has no end date and was not made by an activation. Emergency access accounts named in the Maester configuration (`EmergencyAccessAccounts`) are left out.

#### Remediation action

1. In **Microsoft Entra admin center**, go to **Identity governance** > **[Privileged Identity Management](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_PIMCommon/CommonMenuBlade/~/quickStart)** > **Microsoft Entra roles** > **Assignments**.
2. For each permanent **Active** assignment listed below, choose **Remove**, then add the user again under **Eligible assignments**.
3. In **Settings** for each role, require **Microsoft Entra ID multifactor authentication** or a phishing-resistant authentication context on activation, set a maximum activation duration and require justification.
4. Keep your emergency access accounts permanently assigned, and list them in `maester-config.json` so Maester leaves them out.

#### Related links

* [Essential Eight Maturity Model](https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/essential-eight/essential-eight-maturity-model)
* [Assign Microsoft Entra roles in Privileged Identity Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-how-to-add-role-to-user)
* [Manage emergency access accounts in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/security-emergency-access)

<!--- Results --->
%TestResult%
--- 1403 md
﻿User accounts, except for break glass accounts, are protected by fixed or risk-based lockout mechanisms aligned to a maximum of five failed logon attempts (ISM-1403, Guidelines for system access).

Online password guessing is cheap: an attacker who can try ten passwords per account before a lockout gets ten chances at every account in the tenant. Microsoft Entra smart lockout counts failed sign-ins per account, locks the account for the lockout duration when the threshold is reached, and keeps counting familiar and unfamiliar locations separately so that a user at their usual desk is not locked out by an attacker elsewhere. This check reads the tenant's Password Rule Settings and passes when the lockout threshold is set explicitly to 5 or fewer (the `MaximumFailedAttempts` parameter). The Microsoft default of 10 fails. Break glass accounts are covered by smart lockout as well; keep their passwords long and random rather than excluding them.

1. In **Microsoft Entra admin center**, go to **Protection** > **[Authentication methods](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_IAM/AuthenticationMethodsMenuBlade/~/PasswordProtection)** > **Password protection**.
2. Set **Lockout threshold** to **5** and **Lockout duration in seconds** to at least **60**.
3. Click **Save**.

﻿Multi-factor authentication used for authenticating users of online services is phishing-resistant (ISM-1872, Essential Eight Maturity Level Two).

Push notifications, one-time codes and SMS are relayed by adversary-in-the-middle phishing kits in real time. Passkeys (FIDO2), Windows Hello for Business and certificate-based authentication bind the sign-in to the site, so a proxied page gets nothing it can replay. This check looks for an enabled Conditional Access policy that targets all users and all cloud apps and grants access only with the built-in **Phishing-resistant MFA** authentication strength, or a custom strength limited to those methods.

#### Remediation action

1. Register phishing-resistant methods for your users: enable **Passkey (FIDO2)** and **Certificate-based authentication** under **Protection** > **[Authentication methods](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_IAM/AuthenticationMethodsMenuBlade/~/AdminAuthMethods)**, and deploy Windows Hello for Business to managed devices.
2. 3. Roll it out by group, starting with administrators, before you target all users.

cd /Users/merill/github/maester-pr2552 && APG='https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/essential-eight/essential-eight-assessment-process-guide' && cat > tests/asd/entra/Test.ASD.ISM-1504.md <<EOF
Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate human users to their organisation's online services that process, store or communicate their organisation's sensitive data (ISM-1504, Essential Eight Maturity Level One).

A password alone is defeated by phishing, password spray and credential stuffing. Requiring a second factor for every user on every resource is the first Essential Eight requirement for multi-factor authentication, and the baseline the phishing-resistant requirement of Maturity Level Two builds on.

ASD defines which factors count, not how the policy is built, so this test runs the same check as [CIS.M365.5.2.2.2](https://maester.dev/docs/tests/CIS.M365.5.2.2.2). It looks for an enabled Conditional Access policy that targets all users and all resources and requires multi-factor authentication or an authentication strength. Policies that apply only at a certain risk level, exclude applications or are narrowed by a condition such as a platform or location do not count. Excluding emergency access accounts is expected.

#### Remediation action

1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > [**Policies**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies) and select **New policy**.
3. Under **Users**, include **All users**. Exclude your emergency access accounts.
4. Under **Target resources**, select **All resources (formerly All cloud apps)**.
5. Under **Grant**, select **Grant access** and **Require multifactor authentication** (or **Require authentication strength**).
6. Set **Enable policy** to **On** (use **Report-only** first to measure the impact) and select **Create**.

#### Related links

* [Essential Eight Maturity Model](https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/essential-eight/essential-eight-maturity-model)
* [Essential Eight assessment process guide]($APG)
* [Require multifactor authentication for all users with Conditional Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/howto-conditional-access-policy-all-users-mfa)

<!--- Results --->
%TestResult%
EOF
cat > tests/asd/entra/Test.ASD.ISM-1872.md <<EOF
Multi-factor authentication used for authenticating human users of online services is phishing-resistant (ISM-1872, Essential Eight Maturity Level Two).

Push notifications, one-time codes and SMS are relayed by adversary-in-the-middle phishing kits in real time. Passkeys (FIDO2), Windows Hello for Business and certificate-based authentication bind the sign-in to the site, so a proxied page gets nothing it can replay.

ASD's assessment guide applies this requirement to unprivileged and privileged users alike, and the ASD Blueprint for Secure Cloud meets it with one Conditional Access policy for all users and all resources that requires the **Phishing-resistant MFA** authentication strength. This test runs the same check as [CISA.MS.AAD.3.1](https://maester.dev/docs/tests/CISA.MS.AAD.3.1): an enabled policy that targets all users and all resources and requires the built-in **Phishing-resistant MFA** strength, or a custom strength limited to Windows Hello for Business, passkeys (FIDO2) and certificate-based multifactor authentication.

#### Remediation action

1. Register phishing-resistant methods for your users: enable **Passkey (FIDO2)** and **Certificate-based authentication** under **Entra ID** > **[Authentication methods](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_IAM/AuthenticationMethodsMenuBlade/~/AdminAuthMethods)**, and deploy Windows Hello for Business to managed devices.
2. In **Entra ID** > **[Conditional Access](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies)**, create a policy with **Users** > **All users** (exclude your emergency access accounts), **Target resources** > **All resources**, and **Grant** > **Require authentication strength** > **Phishing-resistant MFA**.
3. Roll it out by group, starting with administrators, before you target all users.

#### Related links

* [Phishing-resistant passwordless authentication deployment](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-plan-prerequisites-phishing-resistant-passwordless-authentication)

<!--- Results --->
%TestResult%
EOF
cat > tests/asd/entra/Test.ASD.ISM-1649.md <<EOF
Just-in-time administration is used for the administration of systems and their resources (ISM-1649, Essential Eight Maturity Level Three).

A standing administrator role is a target around the clock: whoever holds the account holds the tenant. With Privileged Identity Management, administrators are eligible for a role and activate it for a few hours when they need it, with MFA, a justification and an audit trail.

ASD's assessment guide describes just-in-time administration as granting privileged users access "immediately before that access is required and for only as long as it is required", and the ASD Blueprint for Secure Cloud makes every Microsoft Entra role an eligible assignment, with permanent active assignments only for break glass accounts. This test runs the same check as [CIS.M365.5.3.1](https://maester.dev/docs/tests/CIS.M365.5.3.1): every active assignment of a user or group to a role that Microsoft Entra marks as privileged must have been made by an activation. A time-bound active assignment fails as well, because it is standing access for its whole duration. A permanent Global Administrator assignment of an emergency access account named in the Maester configuration (\`EmergencyAccessAccounts\`) is allowed.

#### Remediation action

1. In the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com), go to **ID Governance** > **[Privileged Identity Management](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_PIMCommon/CommonMenuBlade/~/quickStart)** > **Microsoft Entra roles** > **Assignments**.
2. For each **Active** assignment listed below, choose **Remove**, then add the user or group again under **Eligible assignments**.
3. In **Settings** for each role, require multifactor authentication on activation, set a maximum activation duration and require a justification.
4. Keep your emergency access accounts permanently assigned, and list them in \`maester-config.json\` so Maester leaves them out.

#### Related links

* [Essential Eight Maturity Model](https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/essential-eight/essential-eight-maturity-model)
* [Essential Eight assessment process guide]($APG)
* [ASD Blueprint for Secure Cloud: Roles](https://blueprint.asd.gov.au/design/platform/identity/roles/)
* [Assign Microsoft Entra roles in Privileged Identity Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-how-to-add-role-to-user)

<!--- Results --->
%TestResult%
EOF
cat > tests/asd/entra/Test.ASD.ISM-1403.md <<'EOF'
User accounts, except for break glass accounts, are protected by fixed or risk-based lockout mechanisms aligned to a maximum of five failed logon attempts, with either indefinite or automated lockout durations (ISM-1403, Guidelines for system access).

Online password guessing is cheap: an attacker who can try ten passwords per account before a lockout gets ten chances at every account in the tenant. Microsoft Entra smart lockout counts failed sign-ins per account, locks the account for the lockout duration when the threshold is reached, and counts familiar and unfamiliar locations separately so that a user at their usual desk is not locked out by an attacker elsewhere.

This test runs the same check as [CIS.M365.5.2.3.8](https://maester.dev/docs/tests/CIS.M365.5.2.3.8) with ASD's maximum: the lockout threshold must be 5 or fewer (the `MaximumLockoutThreshold` parameter), where CIS allows 10. The Microsoft default of 10 fails. The ASD Blueprint for Secure Cloud sets a threshold of 5 and a lockout duration of 60 seconds.

#### Remediation action

1. In the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com), go to **Entra ID** > **[Authentication methods](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_IAM/AuthenticationMethodsMenuBlade/~/PasswordProtection)** > **Password protection**.
2. Set **Lockout threshold** to **5** and **Lockout duration in seconds** to at least **60**.
3. Select **Save**.

#### Related links

* [ISM Guidelines for system access: User account lockouts](https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/ism/cyber-security-guidelines/guidelines-system-access)
* [ASD Blueprint for Secure Cloud: Password protection](https://blueprint.asd.gov.au/configuration/entra-id/protection/authentication-methods/password-protection/)
* [Protect user accounts from attacks with Microsoft Entra smart lockout](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/howto-password-smart-lockout)

<!--- Results --->
%TestResult%
EOF

content.content:
1	Phishing-resistant MFA SHALL be enforced for all users.
2	
3	Rationale: Weaker forms of MFA do not protect against sophisticated phishing attacks. By enforcing methods resistant to phishing, those risks are minimized.
4	
5	#### Remediation action:
6

function Test-MtCisaPhishResistant {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks if a Conditional Access policy using Phishing-Resistant Authentication Strengths is enabled

    .DESCRIPTION
    Phishing-resistant MFA SHALL be enforced for all users

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtCisaPhishResistant

    Returns true if at least one policy is set to use the built-in phishing resistant authentication strengths

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Test-MtCisaPhishResistant
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'CISA.MS.AAD.3.1',
        Title = 'Phishing-resistant MFA SHALL be enforced for all users.',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'conditional-access',
        Area = 'authentication',
        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
        Severity = 'High',
        UserImpact = 'High',
        ImplementationCost = 'High',
        Mitre = 'T1566.002',
        Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1',
        Service = 'Graph',
        License = 'AAD_PREMIUM',
        Author = 'soulemike'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    $result = Get-MtConditionalAccessPolicy | Where-Object { $_.state -eq "enabled" }

    $policies = $result | Where-Object {`
        $_.conditions.applications.includeApplications -contains "All" -and `
        $_.conditions.users.includeUsers -contains "All" -and `
        $_.grantControls.authenticationStrength.displayName -eq "Phishing-resistant MFA" }

    $testResult = ($policies|Measure-Object).Count -ge 1

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. Your tenant has one or more policies that require Phishing Resistant Authentication Strengths :`n`n%TestResult%"
    } else {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Your tenant does not have any Conditional Access policies that require Phishing Resistant Authentication Strengths."
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown -GraphObjectType ConditionalAccess -GraphObjects $policies

    return $testResult
}

﻿function Test-MtCisaPhishResistant {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks if a Conditional Access policy using Phishing-Resistant Authentication Strengths is enabled

    .DESCRIPTION
    Phishing-resistant MFA SHALL be enforced for all users

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtCisaPhishResistant

    Returns true if at least one policy is set to use the built-in phishing resistant authentication strengths

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Test-MtCisaPhishResistant
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'CISA.MS.AAD.3.1',
        Title = 'Phishing-resistant MFA SHALL be enforced for all users.',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'conditional-access',
        Area = 'authentication',
        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
        Severity = 'High',
        UserImpact = 'High',
        ImplementationCost = 'High',
        Mitre = 'T1566.002',
        Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1',
        Service = 'Graph',
        License = 'AAD_PREMIUM',
        Author = 'soulemike'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    # The built-in Phishing-resistant MFA strength, and the methods a custom strength may be limited to, as ScubaGear checks them.
    $phishingResistantStrengthId = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000004'
    $phishingResistantMethods = @('windowsHelloForBusiness', 'fido2', 'x509CertificateMultiFactor')

    $result = Get-MtConditionalAccessPolicy | Where-Object { $_.state -eq "enabled" }

    $policies = $result | Where-Object {`
        $_.conditions.applications.includeApplications -contains "All" -and `
        $_.conditions.users.includeUsers -contains "All" -and `
        $_.grantControls.authenticationStrength -and (
            $_.grantControls.authenticationStrength.id -eq $phishingResistantStrengthId -or (
                @($_.grantControls.authenticationStrength.allowedCombinations).Count -gt 0 -and
                @($_.grantControls.authenticationStrength.allowedCombinations | Where-Object { $_ -notin $phishingResistantMethods }).Count -eq 0
            )
        ) }

    $testResult = ($policies|Measure-Object).Count -ge 1

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. Your tenant has one or more policies that require Phishing Resistant Authentication Strengths :`n`n%TestResult%"
    } else {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Your tenant does not have any Conditional Access policies that require Phishing Resistant Authentication Strengths."
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown -GraphObjectType ConditionalAccess -GraphObjects $policies

    return $testResult
}

It 'Gives the rows of the ASD suite their maturity level and strategy, and the ISM control as Control, without a tenant' {
        $rows = @((Get-Run 'Asd').Tests | Where-Object Suite -EQ 'ASD')
        $rows.Count | Should -Be 15
        @($rows | Where-Object { $_.Benchmark.Framework -cnotin 'essential-eight', 'ism' -or -not $_.Benchmark.Requirement } | ForEach-Object Id) | Should -BeNullOrEmpty
        $essentialEight = @($rows | Where-Object { $_.Benchmark.Framework -ceq 'essential-eight' })
        $essentialEight.Count | Should -Be 14
        @($essentialEight | Where-Object { $_.Benchmark.Level -cnotin 'ML1', 'ML2', 'ML3' -or -not $_.Benchmark.Strategy } | ForEach-Object Id) | Should -BeNullOrEmpty
        # The framework file relates each Essential Eight requirement to the ISM control of the same ID.
        @($essentialEight | Where-Object { $_.Control -cnotcontains "ism:$($_.Benchmark.Requirement)" } | ForEach-Object Id) | Should -BeNullOrEmpty
        $row = $rows | Where-Object Id -EQ 'ASD.ISM-1504'
        $row.Benchmark.Level | Should -BeExactly 'ML1'
        $row.Benchmark.Strategy | Should -BeExactly 'Multi-factor authentication'
        @($row.Control)[0] | Should -BeExactly 'essential-eight:ISM-1504'
        # Related references follow the test's own values: the ISM controls of ISM-1504 and ISM-0974, in that order.
        @($row.Control)[-2..-1] | Should -Be @('ism:ISM-1504', 'ism:ISM-0974')
        $ism = $rows | Where-Object Id -EQ 'ASD.ISM-1403'
        $ism.Benchmark.Framework | Should -BeExactly 'ism'
        $ism.Benchmark.Section | Should -BeExactly 'User account lockouts'

    <#
    .Synopsis

    .Description
    Returns all the members of the specific group ID.

    .Example
    Get-MtGroupMember

    #>
  [CmdletBinding()]
  param(
    # ID for the Entra group to return members for.
    [Parameter(Position = 0, mandatory = $true)]
    [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]
    [guid]$GroupId,
    # Include indirect members through nested groups.
    [switch]$Recursive
  )

  # Validate GroupId is not empty GUID
  if ($GroupId -eq [guid]::Empty) {
    Write-Error "GroupId cannot be an empty GUID."
    return $null
  }

  try {
    $group = Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri "groups/$GroupId/" -ApiVersion v1.0
    if (-not $group) {
      Write-Verbose "Group ($GroupId) was not found in the tenant and will be skipped. This may be an external partner group assigned via GDAP, or the group may have been deleted."
      return $null
    }
  } catch {
    # Check status code via Response.StatusCode (Invoke-MgGraphRequest pattern used in this repo),
    # including enum, string ('NotFound'), and integer (404) forms; then via the typed StatusCode
    # property (.NET 5+/PS7); then fall back to message matching for older runtimes.
    $responseStatusCode = $_.Exception.Response.StatusCode
    $exceptionStatusCode = $_.Exception.StatusCode
    $is404 = ($responseStatusCode -eq [System.Net.HttpStatusCode]::NotFound) -or
             ($responseStatusCode -eq 'NotFound') -or
             ($responseStatusCode -eq 404) -or
             ($exceptionStatusCode -eq [System.Net.HttpStatusCode]::NotFound) -or
             ($_.Exception.Message -match 'NotFound|404')
    if ($is404) {
      Write-Verbose "Group ($GroupId) was not found in the tenant and will be skipped. This may be an external partner group assigned via GDAP, or the group may have been deleted. Details: $($_.Exception.Message)"
    } else {
      Write-Warning "Error obtaining group ($GroupId) from Microsoft Graph. Confirm the group exists in your tenant. Details: $($_.Exception.Message)"
    }
    return $null
  }

  Write-Verbose -Message "Getting group members for group: $($group.displayName) ($GroupId)"

  try {
    $members = Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri "groups/$GroupId/members" -ApiVersion v1.0

﻿function Get-MtAsdPrivilegedUser {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns the users that hold a privileged directory role, with the names of their roles, for the ASD checks.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Shared by the Essential Eight Restrict administrative privileges checks. A role is privileged when Microsoft
    Entra marks its definition isPrivileged. Active and eligible assignments count. The emergency access
    accounts named in the Maester configuration (EmergencyAccessAccounts) are left out, and so is every
    principal that is not a user.

    Returns a hashtable from user object ID to the sorted, unique display names of the user's privileged
    roles. The hashtable is empty when nobody holds a privileged role.

    .EXAMPLE
    $privilegedUsers = Get-MtAsdPrivilegedUser
    $privilegedUsers.Keys

    Returns the object IDs of the users that hold a privileged directory role.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([hashtable])]
    param()

content.content:
.DESCRIPTION
    ISM-1648 (Essential Eight, Restrict administrative privileges, Maturity Level Two) asks that privileged
    access to systems and their resources is disabled after 45 days of inactivity.

    The check lists the users with an active or eligible assignment to a directory role that Microsoft Entra
    marks as privileged, directly or through a role-assignable group, and reads the last sign-in of each. A user fails when the account is enabled and the
    most recent interactive or non-interactive sign-in is older than the number of days given (45 by
    default), or when the account has never signed in and was created before that. The emergency access
    accounts named in the Maester configuration (EmergencyAccessAccounts) are left out, because they are
    meant to stay unused.

    MT.1029 reports the same accounts through the Privileged Identity Management stale accounts alert, whose
    number of days each tenant sets. ASD names 45 days, so this check reads the sign-ins itself.

    .EXAMPLE
--- md
﻿Privileged access to systems and their resources is disabled after 45 days of inactivity (ISM-1648, Essential Eight Maturity Level Two).

An administrator account nobody uses is an account nobody watches. Its password ages, its owner may have moved on, and a sign-in on it is unlikely to be questioned. This check lists the users with an active or eligible assignment to a directory role that Microsoft Entra marks as privileged and reads the last sign-in of each. An enabled account fails when its most recent interactive or non-interactive sign-in is older than 45 days (the `InactiveDays` parameter), or when it has never signed in and was created before that. Emergency access accounts named in the Maester configuration (`EmergencyAccessAccounts`) are left out, because they are meant to stay unused.

#### Remediation action

1. In **Microsoft Entra admin center**, open **[Users](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_UsersAndTenants/UserManagementMenuBlade/~/AllUsers)** and check each account listed below with its owner.
2. Remove the privileged role in **Roles & administrators**, or disable the account under **Edit properties** > **Account enabled**.

15:    (EmergencyAccessAccounts) are left out, because they are meant to stay unused.
﻿Privileged users are assigned a dedicated privileged user account to be used solely for duties requiring privileged access (ISM-0445, Essential Eight Maturity Level One), and privileged user accounts are prevented from accessing the internet, email and web services (ISM-1175).

When the same account reads email, browses the web and administers the tenant, every phishing message and every malicious link reaches an administrator. A separate, unlicensed account for privileged duties keeps the role away from the inbox. This check lists the users with an active or eligible assignment to a directory role that Microsoft Entra marks as privileged and fails for each one that has an enabled Exchange Online service plan that provides a mailbox (Plan 1, Plan 2, Kiosk or Essentials; the `MailboxServicePlanId` parameter). The Exchange Foundation plan that comes with Entra ID, Intune and Defender licences creates no mailbox and does not count. Emergency access accounts named in the Maester configuration (`EmergencyAccessAccounts`) are left out.

#### Remediation action

1. For each administrator listed below, create a cloud-only account for privileged work, for example `adm-firstname.lastname@yourtenant.onmicrosoft.com`, and do not assign it a licence that includes Exchange Online.
2. In **Microsoft Entra admin center**, open **[Roles & administrators](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_IAM/RolesManagementMenuBlade/~/AllRoles)** (or Privileged Identity Management) and move the role from the everyday account to the new one.
3. Where an administrator must receive mail for a role, forward it to the everyday account rather than keeping a mailbox on the privileged one.

#### Related links

* [Essential Eight Maturity Model](https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/essential-eight/essential-eight-maturity-model)
* [ISM Guidelines for system access: Privileged access to systems](https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/ism/cyber-security-guidelines/guidelines-system-access)
* [Securing privileged access: separate user accounts for administrators](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/security-planning#ensure-separate-user-accounts-and-mail-forwarding-for-global-administrator-accounts)

content.content:
# ASD Essential Eight and ISM

Checks that verify a Microsoft 365 tenant against the Australian Signals Directorate (ASD)
[Essential Eight Maturity Model](https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/essential-eight/essential-eight-maturity-model)
and the controls of the [Information Security Manual](https://www.cyber.gov.au/ism) (ISM) that it is built from.

## Layout

- `suite.json` declares the suite (`ASD`) and its two frameworks, `essential-eight` and `ism`.
- `frameworks/essential-eight.json` and `frameworks/ism.json` are the catalogues of the two frameworks. They are
  generated from the ISM OSCAL release by `build/asd/Update-AsdFramework.ps1`; do not edit them by hand.
- `<service>/Test.ASD.<ISM control>.ps1` and `.md` are the checks, one folder per product (`entra/`, `intune/`).

## IDs and mapping

ASD publishes the maturity model with a
[mapping of every requirement to one ISM control](https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/essential-eight/essential-eight-maturity-model-ism-mapping)
(October 2024 edition), and the ISM OSCAL release ships that mapping as Essential Eight baseline profiles, so a
check is named after the control it implements: `ASD.ISM-1504` implements ISM-1504. Its attribute names the
requirement in the Essential Eight framework first, `Control = 'essential-eight:ISM-1504'`, and the framework file
relates that requirement to `ism:ISM-1504`, which Maester adds to the result. A check for a control that the
maturity model does not use names the ISM directly, `Control = 'ism:ISM-0421'`.

A test in another suite that checks what one of these controls asks for may name the same requirement in its
`Control`, after the requirement it is written for.

The `Benchmark` of a result carries the facts of the requirement: the maturity level that first requires it
(`Level`: `ML1`, `ML2` or `ML3`) and the mitigation strategy or strategies (`Strategy`) from the Essential Eight framework, or the
guideline, section and classification applicability from the ISM.

A passing check is evidence for the control it names. It is not an assessment: an Essential Eight assessment also
covers endpoints, servers and processes that a tenant check cannot see.

﻿function Test-MtAsdAsrRule {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that one Microsoft Defender attack surface reduction rule is set to Block by an assigned Intune policy.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Shared by the Essential Eight user application hardening and Microsoft Office macro checks. Reads the
    attack surface reduction rules of every Windows configuration policy (endpoint security and settings
    catalog share the setting definition IDs), takes the strongest mode any assigned policy sets for the rule,
    and passes when it is Block. Audit, Warn and Off are reported and fail: the ISM asks for the behaviour to be
    blocked, not logged.

    Writes the result detail and returns the result of the check.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtAsdAsrRule -RuleSuffix 'blockallofficeapplicationsfromcreatingchildprocesses' -RuleName 'Block all Office applications from creating child processes'
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # The end of the rule's setting definition ID after device_vendor_msft_policy_config_defender_attacksurfacereductionrules_.
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]
        [string] $RuleSuffix,

        # The name of the rule, as the Intune admin center shows it.
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]
        [string] $RuleName
    )

    $definitionId = "device_vendor_msft_policy_config_defender_attacksurfacereductionrules_$RuleSuffix"
﻿function Test-MtAsdOfficeChildProcessesBlocked {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that an assigned Intune policy sets the attack surface reduction rule "Block all Office applications from creating child processes" to Block.

    .DESCRIPTION
    ISM-1667 (Essential Eight, User application hardening, Maturity Level Two) asks that Microsoft Office is blocked from creating child processes.

    Attack surface reduction rules are read from every Intune Windows configuration policy (Endpoint security
    and settings catalog share the setting definition IDs). The check passes when an assigned policy sets the
    rule to Block; Audit and Warn only report the behaviour and do not satisfy the control.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtAsdOfficeChildProcessesBlocked

    Returns true when an assigned policy sets the rule to Block.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/ASD.ISM-1667
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'ASD.ISM-1667',
        Title = 'Microsoft Office is blocked from creating child processes.',
        Product = 'intune',
        RelatedProduct = 'defender',
        Feature = 'endpoint-security',
        Area = 'devices',
        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
        Severity = 'High',
        UserImpact = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre = ('T1204.002', 'T1566.001'),
        Control = ('essential-eight:ISM-1667', 'nist-800-53-r5:CM-7'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        License = 'INTUNE_A',
        Author = 'jusso-dev'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    return Test-MtAsdAsrRule -RuleSuffix 'blockallofficeapplicationsfromcreatingchildprocesses' -RuleName 'Block all Office applications from creating child processes'
}
﻿Microsoft Office is blocked from creating child processes (ISM-1667, Essential Eight Maturity Level Two, User application hardening).

A malicious document rarely does its damage inside Word or Excel: it launches PowerShell, cmd.exe or a downloaded executable. Blocking Office from starting child processes cuts that chain whatever the macro, exploit or DDE payload tried. This check reads the attack surface reduction rules of every Intune Windows configuration policy (Endpoint security and settings catalog policies share the same setting definitions) and passes when an assigned policy sets **Block all Office applications from creating child processes** to **Block**. Audit and Warn only report the behaviour and do not satisfy the control.

#### Remediation action

1. In **Microsoft Intune admin center**, go to **Endpoint security** > **[Attack surface reduction](https://intune.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_Intune_Workflows/SecurityManagementMenu/~/asr)** and open your attack surface reduction rules policy, or create one for **Windows** with the profile **Attack Surface Reduction Rules**.
2. Set **Block all Office applications from creating child processes** to **Block**. Pilot the rule in **Audit** first if Office add-ins or line-of-business macros are in use.
3. Assign the policy to all workstations.

#### Related links

* [Essential Eight Maturity Model](https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/essential-eight/essential-eight-maturity-model)
* [Attack surface reduction rules reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference)
* [ISM Guidelines for system hardening](https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/ism/cyber-security-guidelines/guidelines-system-hardening)

﻿function Get-MtIntuneConfigurationPolicySetting {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns every setting of the Intune Windows configuration policies, one row per setting instance.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Reads the settings catalog, endpoint security and other policies of the configurationPolicies API for the
    Windows platform, with their assignments, and flattens the settings of each policy. A choice setting, a
    group collection and a simple setting each become a row; the children of a choice or a group follow it with
    the parent's setting definition ID in ParentDefinitionId, so a check can look a setting up by definition ID
    wherever it sits.

    Each row has PolicyId, PolicyName, TemplateFamily, IsAssigned, SettingDefinitionId, Value (the choice
    value or simple value, or $null for a group) and ParentDefinitionId.

    .EXAMPLE
    Get-MtIntuneConfigurationPolicySetting | Where-Object SettingDefinitionId -like '*blockmacroexecutionfrominternet'

    Returns the Office macro settings of every Windows policy.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject[]])]
    param(
        # Only the policies of these template families, for example endpointSecurityAttackSurfaceReduction. Every Windows policy when omitted.
        [string[]] $TemplateFamily
    )

    $policies = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri "deviceManagement/configurationPolicies?`$filter=platforms has 'windows10'&`$expand=assignments" -ApiVersion beta)
    if ($TemplateFamily) { $policies = @($policies | Where-Object { $_.templateReference.templateFamily -in $TemplateFamily }) }
    Write-Verbose "Reading the settings of $($policies.Count) Intune Windows configuration policies"

﻿Microsoft Office is blocked from creating executable content (ISM-1668, Essential Eight Maturity Level Two, User application hardening).

A macro that writes an executable, script or DLL to disk is staging malware for a later step. Blocking Office from creating executable content stops the drop even when the macro itself was allowed to run. This check reads the attack surface reduction rules of every Intune Windows configuration policy (Endpoint security and settings catalog policies share the same setting definitions) and passes when an assigned policy sets **Block Office applications from creating executable content** to **Block**. Audit and Warn only report the behaviour and do not satisfy the control.

#### Remediation action

1. In **Microsoft Intune admin center**, go to **Endpoint security** > **[Attack surface reduction](https://intune.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_Intune_Workflows/SecurityManagementMenu/~/asr)** and open your attack surface reduction rules policy, or create one for **Windows** with the profile **Attack Surface Reduction Rules**.
2. Set **Block Office applications from creating executable content** to **Block**. Pilot the rule in **Audit** first if Office add-ins or line-of-business macros are in use.
3. Assign the policy to all workstations.
