﻿function Test-MtAsdOfficeMacroAntivirusScanning {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that an assigned Intune policy enables antivirus scanning of Microsoft Office macros at runtime.

    .DESCRIPTION
    ISM-1672 (Essential Eight, Restrict Microsoft Office macros, Maturity Level One) asks that Microsoft Office
    macro antivirus scanning is enabled.

    The check reads the Intune settings catalog policies for Windows and looks for the Office setting
    "Macro Runtime Scan Scope" set to Enabled with the scope "Enable for low trust documents" or
    "Enable for all documents", in a policy that is assigned. The scan hands macro behaviour to the
    Antimalware Scan Interface (AMSI), where Microsoft Defender Antivirus or another registered antivirus
    inspects it.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtAsdOfficeMacroAntivirusScanning

    Returns true when an assigned policy enables macro runtime scanning.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/ASD.ISM-1672
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'ASD.ISM-1672',
        Title = 'Microsoft Office macro antivirus scanning is enabled.',
        Product = 'intune',
        Feature = 'device-configuration',
        Area = 'devices',
        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
    $effective = @($report | Where-Object { $_.Assigned -and $_.Scans })
    $testResult = $effective.Count -gt 0

    if (@($report).Count -eq 0) {
        $testResultMarkdown = 'No Intune Windows policy configures the Office setting **Macro Runtime Scan Scope**. Enable it for all documents in a settings catalog policy that is assigned to your users.'
    } else {
        $table = "| Policy | Macro runtime scan | Assigned |`n| --- | --- | --- |`n"
        foreach ($r in $report) { $table += "| $($r.Policy) | $($r.Scope) | $(if ($r.Assigned) { 'Yes' } else { 'No' }) |`n" }
        if ($testResult) {
            $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. An assigned Intune policy enables antivirus scanning of Office macros at runtime.`n`n$table"
        } else {
            $testResultMarkdown = "The Office setting **Macro Runtime Scan Scope** is configured, but no assigned policy enables it for low trust or all documents.`n`n$table"
        }
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}
﻿Microsoft Office macro antivirus scanning is enabled (ISM-1672, Essential Eight Maturity Level One).

A macro that is allowed to run can still be malicious. With macro runtime scanning, Office hands the behaviour of a running macro to the Antimalware Scan Interface (AMSI), where Microsoft Defender Antivirus or another registered antivirus inspects it and stops it. This check reads the Intune settings catalog policies for Windows and looks for **Macro Runtime Scan Scope** set to **Enabled** with the scope **Enable for low trust documents** or **Enable for all documents**, in an assigned policy. ASD recommends scanning all documents.

#### Remediation action

1. In **Microsoft Intune admin center**, go to **Devices** > **[Configuration](https://intune.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_Intune_DeviceSettings/DevicesMenu/~/configuration)** > **Create** > **New policy** > **Windows 10 and later** > **Settings catalog**.
2. Add, under **Microsoft Office 2016** > **Security Settings**, the setting **Macro Runtime Scan Scope**, set it to **Enabled** and choose **Enable for all documents**.

﻿function Test-MtAsdInternetExplorerDisabled {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that an assigned Intune policy disables Internet Explorer 11 as a standalone browser.

    .DESCRIPTION
    ISM-1654 (Essential Eight, User application hardening, Maturity Level One) asks that Internet Explorer 11
    is disabled or removed.

    The check reads the Intune settings catalog policies for Windows and looks for the Internet Explorer
    setting "Disable Internet Explorer 11 as a standalone browser" set to Enabled in a policy that is assigned.
    Devices where Internet Explorer is removed as a Windows feature, or that run a Windows release without it,
    satisfy the control without this setting; the check does not see them.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtAsdInternetExplorerDisabled

    Returns true when an assigned policy disables Internet Explorer 11.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/ASD.ISM-1654
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'ASD.ISM-1654',
        Title = 'Internet Explorer 11 is disabled or removed.',
        Product = 'intune',
        Feature = 'device-configuration',
        Area = 'devices',
        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
        Severity = 'Low',
﻿Internet Explorer 11 is disabled or removed (ISM-1654, Essential Eight Maturity Level One).

Internet Explorer 11 is out of support and keeps the legacy rendering engine and ActiveX reachable from the desktop. This check reads the Intune settings catalog policies for Windows and looks for **Disable Internet Explorer 11 as a standalone browser** set to **Enabled** in an assigned policy. Devices where Internet Explorer is removed as a Windows optional feature, or that run a Windows release that no longer carries it, satisfy the control without this setting; the check does not see them.

#### Remediation action

1. In **Microsoft Intune admin center**, go to **Devices** > **[Configuration](https://intune.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_Intune_DeviceSettings/DevicesMenu/~/configuration)** > **Create** > **New policy** > **Windows 10 and later** > **Settings catalog**.
2. Add, under **Administrative Templates** > **Windows Components** > **Internet Explorer**, the setting **Disable Internet Explorer 11 as a standalone browser** and set it to **Enabled**.
3. Assign the policy to all devices.

content.content:
## Settings shared by many tests

Read tenant-wide settings from `GlobalSettings` in the config with `Get-MtSetting`:

```powershell
$accounts = Get-MtSetting -Name EmergencyAccessAccounts
$siteUrl  = Get-MtSetting -Name 'Contoso.SiteUrl' -Default 'https://contoso.sharepoint.com'
```

When the config does not set the value, `Get-MtSetting` returns Maester's default for the settings it knows,
else `-Default`. Use a `Namespace.Key` name for your own settings. Prefer a test parameter when the value
belongs to one test.

## What a custom test can call

Each custom test file is loaded into its own private module. It can call every command Maester exports,
including `Invoke-MtGraphRequest`, `Add-MtTestResultDetail`, `Get-MtSetting`, `Get-MtTenantContext`,
`Test-MtConnection`, `Get-MtLicenseInformation`, `Get-MtUser`, `Get-MtConditionalAccessPolicy` and
`Invoke-MtTest`. It cannot call Maester's private functions, and it cannot replace a Maester command.

Functions defined in the same file are visible to the test. Functions in another test file are not. To share
code between files, put it in a helper `.ps1` (one that is not named `Test.*.ps1`) and dot-source it from
inside the test function: `. "$PSScriptRoot/Contoso.Helpers.ps1"`. `$PSScriptRoot` is the test file's folder.

To reuse a built-in check, run it through the engine instead of calling its function:

```powershell
$row = Invoke-MtTest -Id MT.1005
$row.Result   # Passed, Failed, Skipped, ...
```

The built-in check functions are no longer exported in 3.0, and they no longer contain their own connection
checks, so calling one directly is not supported.

## A suite manifest for your folder
--- skill workflow
### Framework requirements and NIST controls (`Control`)

Fill in `Control` on every new check. Do not leave it out because it is optional: decide, and leave it empty
only when nothing applies. It is the only way a check is mapped to a framework. Work through these in order:

1. **The requirement the check is written for.** A CIS check lists `cis-m365:<id>` or `cis-github:<id>`, a
   CISA check lists `cisa-scuba:<id>` and an ASD check `essential-eight:<ISM id>` (or `ism:<ISM id>`), first. If the requirement is not in the suite's framework file yet, add it
   there with its facts (level and profiles, or criticality) in the same pull request.
2. **A CIS, CISA or ASD requirement that asks for the same setting.** A Maester check that verifies what
   `cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1` asks for lists it. Look the requirement up in `tests/cis/frameworks/*.json`,
   `tests/cisa/frameworks/cisa-scuba.json` and `tests/asd/frameworks/*.json`, or in the lookup of the [test builder](https://maester.dev/test-builder).
   `Get-MtTest -Suite CISA | Format-Table Id, Title, Control` shows what the existing checks map to.
3. **NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls**, written `nist-800-53-r5:<control>`, chosen with the NIST part of the
   rubric's [Control section](../../../website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md#control) from the pinned list
   `powershell/assets/MaesterNistControls.json`. At most three, best fit first, and only when a passing result is
   direct evidence for the control. Skip this step when step 1 or 2 gave a `cisa-scuba` reference: CISA publishes
   the NIST mapping of its policies and the result gets it from the framework file.

The first value that names a requirement in a framework file becomes the `Benchmark` of the result, so the order
matters. An inventory count, or a health, licensing or tidiness check, usually lists nothing.

### Where the keys come from
## Step-by-Step Workflow: Creating a New Check

1. **Reserve an ID.** Check [issue #697](https://github.com/maester365/maester/issues/697) and comment to reserve
   the next `MT.xxxx` (the maester-issue-manager agent can do this). `Get-MtTest MT.12*` shows which IDs exist.
2. **Scaffold** with `New-MtTest -Id <ID> -Title '...' -Service <service> -Product <product key>
   -Path ./tests/<suite>/<service>`.
3. **Fill in the attribute**: `License`, `Author`, flags as needed.
4. **Write the function**: read with `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` or the helpers, decide, `Add-MtTestResultDetail`,
   return a boolean. Add parameters for tunable values.
5. **Write the guide, the `.md`**, in full: a one-line summary, why the setting matters, numbered remediation
   steps with a direct link to the admin portal page, related links (Microsoft Learn, and the benchmark when the
   check maps to one), and the results footer. Replace every placeholder that `New-MtTest` wrote; a check with
   scaffold text in its guide is not finished. Verify product facts and links with Microsoft Learn.
6. **Choose the attribute values** with the rubric: `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType`, `Severity`, `UserImpact`,
   `ImplementationCost`, `Mitre`, `Control`, and `RelatedProduct` when one applies. See
   [Choosing the attribute values](#choosing-the-attribute-values) and
   [Framework requirements and NIST controls](#framework-requirements-and-nist-controls-control). The
   [test builder](https://maester.dev/test-builder) shows the allowed values and the rubric for each attribute
   and writes the attribute; use it to check a value you are unsure of.
7. **Validate offline**: `Import-Module ./powershell/Maester.psd1 -Force; Get-MtTest <ID>` must show
   `IsValid = True` and no `Errors`. Name the ID and leave out `-Path`: `Get-MtTest -Path <file>` applies the
   rules of a custom test, so it does not report a missing attribute or a key that is not in the taxonomy.
8. **Run against a tenant**: `Connect-Maester; Invoke-MtTest -Path <file>` (or `Invoke-MtTest -Id <ID>`). Try
   `-Parameter @{...}` for each parameter. Check the row's `Result`, `ReasonCode`, `ResultDetail.TestResult`.
9. **Run the unit tests**: `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1`. `powershell/tests/general/NativeTestLint.Tests.ps1`
   and `powershell/tests/general/NativeTestAttributes.Tests.ps1` check every built-in test.

## Converting a User's Pester-format Test
## Validation Checklist

### Test logic
- [ ] Returns exactly one `$true`/`$false`; no stray pipeline output.
- [ ] No `Test-MtConnection` guard, no `Get-MtLicenseInformation` check; `Service` and `License` declared instead.
- [ ] No blanket `try { } catch { Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Error ... }`.
- [ ] `-SkippedBecause NotApplicable` (not `$null`) when the check does not apply.
- [ ] Data retrieval uses `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` or Maester helpers.
- [ ] No hard-coded GUIDs, tenant IDs or names; tunables are described parameters.
- [ ] No writes to `$script:`, `$global:`, `$env:` or `$__MtSession`.
- [ ] `Platform = 'Windows'` if it uses Windows-only commands.

### Attribute and files
- [ ] `Test.<Id>.ps1` and `Test.<Id>.md` in the right suite folder; ID unique and not reused.
## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Why it matters | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Adding a `Test-MtConnection` guard or licence check | Duplicates the engine's gate; lint fails | Declare `Service` / `License` |
| Wrapping the body in `try`/`catch` that reports `-SkippedBecause Error` | Lint fails; the engine already does it | Remove it; catch only specific conditions |
| Returning `$null` for "not applicable" | Reported as `Skipped`/`NoResult` | `Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause NotApplicable` |
| Uncaptured output (`$list.Add(...)`) | `Error`/`InvalidReturn` | `$null = $list.Add(...)` |
| Variables or `@()` in the attribute | `InvalidMetadata` | Constants and `('a', 'b')` lists only |
| `Category` or `Preview` in the attribute | `InvalidMetadata`; both were removed in 3.0 | `Product` and `Feature`; `Lifecycle = 'Preview'` |
| A `Tag` such as `'CA'`, `'Entra'` or `'Maester'` on a built-in check | Unit tests fail; tags are not the taxonomy | Use the attribute that says it; see [Tags](#tags) |
| A product alias (`'Entra ID'`) or a key that is not in the taxonomy | Unit tests fail | Use the key from `powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`, or add the key in the same pull request |
| Copying `Severity`, `Area` or `Mitre` from a similar check | The value may not fit this check, and the attribute review fails a value that does not fit | Choose each value with the rubric |
| Validating a built-in check with `Get-MtTest -Path` only | It applies the rules of a custom test and reports no missing attribute | `Get-MtTest <ID>` |
| File name does not match `Id` | `InvalidMetadata` | Rename to `Test.<Id>.ps1` |
| Missing `[CmdletBinding()]` | `InvalidMetadata` | Add it before `param()` |
| Hard-coded thresholds or object IDs | Users cannot tune the check | Make them described parameters |
| Multi-line `#` comment above a parameter | Only the last line is read as its description | One-line comment or `.PARAMETER` |
| `Invoke-MgGraphRequest` / `Get-Mg*` | Bypasses caching | `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` |
| Using `-Severity` or `-TestTitle` on `Add-MtTestResultDetail` | Ignored for single-result checks | Set them in the attribute |
| Editing generated EIDSCA/ORCA files or `website/docs/tests/` | Overwritten | Change the generator or the test files |
| Adding the function to `FunctionsToExport` | Check functions are internal in 3.0 | Don't |
| Missing `%TestResult%` in `-Result` with `-GraphObjects` | The object table is not inserted | Include the placeholder |

## Reference Examples

- [ ] No `Test-MtConnection` guard, no `Get-MtLicenseInformation` check; `Service` and `License` declared instead.
- [ ] No blanket `try { } catch { Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Error ... }`.
- [ ] `-SkippedBecause NotApplicable` (not `$null`) when the check does not apply.
- [ ] Data retrieval uses `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` or Maester helpers.
- [ ] No hard-coded GUIDs, tenant IDs or names; tunables are described parameters.
- [ ] No writes to `$script:`, `$global:`, `$env:` or `$__MtSession`.
- [ ] `Platform = 'Windows'` if it uses Windows-only commands.

### Attribute and files
- [ ] `Test.<Id>.ps1` and `Test.<Id>.md` in the right suite folder; ID unique and not reused.
## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Why it matters | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Adding a `Test-MtConnection` guard or licence check | Duplicates the engine's gate; lint fails | Declare `Service` / `License` |
| Wrapping the body in `try`/`catch` that reports `-SkippedBecause Error` | Lint fails; the engine already does it | Remove it; catch only specific conditions |
| Returning `$null` for "not applicable" | Reported as `Skipped`/`NoResult` | `Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause NotApplicable` |
| Uncaptured output (`$list.Add(...)`) | `Error`/`InvalidReturn` | `$null = $list.Add(...)` |
| Variables or `@()` in the attribute | `InvalidMetadata` | Constants and `('a', 'b')` lists only |
| `Category` or `Preview` in the attribute | `InvalidMetadata`; both were removed in 3.0 | `Product` and `Feature`; `Lifecycle = 'Preview'` |
| A `Tag` such as `'CA'`, `'Entra'` or `'Maester'` on a built-in check | Unit tests fail; tags are not the taxonomy | Use the attribute that says it; see [Tags](#tags) |
| A product alias (`'Entra ID'`) or a key that is not in the taxonomy | Unit tests fail | Use the key from `powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`, or add the key in the same pull request |
| Copying `Severity`, `Area` or `Mitre` from a similar check | The value may not fit this check, and the attribute review fails a value that does not fit | Choose each value with the rubric |
| Validating a built-in check with `Get-MtTest -Path` only | It applies the rules of a custom test and reports no missing attribute | `Get-MtTest <ID>` |
| File name does not match `Id` | `InvalidMetadata` | Rename to `Test.<Id>.ps1` |
| Missing `[CmdletBinding()]` | `InvalidMetadata` | Add it before `param()` |
| Hard-coded thresholds or object IDs | Users cannot tune the check | Make them described parameters |
| Multi-line `#` comment above a parameter | Only the last line is read as its description | One-line comment or `.PARAMETER` |
| `Invoke-MgGraphRequest` / `Get-Mg*` | Bypasses caching | `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` |
| Using `-Severity` or `-TestTitle` on `Add-MtTestResultDetail` | Ignored for single-result checks | Set them in the attribute |
| Editing generated EIDSCA/ORCA files or `website/docs/tests/` | Overwritten | Change the generator or the test files |
| Adding the function to `FunctionsToExport` | Check functions are internal in 3.0 | Don't |
| Missing `%TestResult%` in `-Result` with `-GraphObjects` | The object table is not inserted | Include the placeholder |

You are a Maester test expert focused on creating and maintaining high-quality security checks for Microsoft 365 tenants.

## Canonical skill

Read and follow the [Maester Test Expert skill](../skills/maester-test-expert/SKILL.md). It is the **single source of truth** for Maester check authoring conventions, the `[MaesterTest]` attributes, the native test format, the validation checklist and remediation guidance.

If anything in this agent file conflicts with the skill, the skill wins.

## Priorities

1. Implement complete checks: a native test (`Test.<ID>.ps1` with its `[MaesterTest]` attribute) and its `Test.<ID>.md`. Website test pages are generated; do not write them by hand.
2. Choose each classification, priority and ATT&CK attribute with the [attribute rubric](../../website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md), using keys from `powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`. When you review a check, check its attributes against the rubric as a separate step, as "Reviewing a test's attributes" in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) describes, and fail the review if a value does not fit.
3. Fill in `Control` on every new check: the CIS or CISA requirement it implements or shares a setting with, and the NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls it supports, as the skill's "Framework requirements and NIST controls" section describes. Leave it empty only when nothing applies.
4. Write the guide (`Test.<ID>.md`) in full: summary, why it matters, numbered remediation steps with admin portal links, related links. Leave no scaffold placeholder.
5. Follow Maester conventions for skip behavior and result formatting, as the skill describes.
6. Use Microsoft Learn MCP tools for Microsoft-specific facts and code samples.
7. Coordinate MT ID reservation through the `maester-issue-manager` agent on [issue #697](https://github.com/maester365/maester/issues/697) when implementing new MT checks. Create or update other tracking issues only when the user asks.

## Guardrails

- Use least-privilege changes and avoid unrelated edits.
- Prefer actionable remediation guidance and clear pass/fail output.
- Do not edit auto-generated EIDSCA/ORCA files directly; change the generators under `build/eidsca/` and `build/orca/` instead.

input.command:
cd /Users/merill/github/maester-pr2552 && python3 -I - <<'PY'
p = 'website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx'
s = open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()
section = r'''## Tests that another suite already has

Benchmarks overlap. CIS, CISA SCuBA and ASD all ask for multifactor authentication for every user, and Maester
has its own test for it as well. Before you write a test for a benchmark requirement, look for a test that
already reads the same setting, then decide from the benchmark's own sources whether it asks for anything that
test does not check.

1. **Find the tests that read the setting.** `Get-MtTest -Product entra -Feature conditional-access | Format-Table
   Id, Title` lists the candidates; searching `tests/` for the Graph endpoint or the setting name finds the rest.
   Look in every suite, not only the one you are writing for.
2. **Read what the benchmark asks, in its own sources.** The one-line text of a requirement is usually generic.
   The detail that decides between two implementations is in the benchmark's audit or assessment guidance and in
   any reference configuration it publishes: the audit and remediation sections of a CIS benchmark, the SCuBA
   baseline and ScubaGear for CISA, and for ASD the ISM, the Essential Eight assessment process guide and the ASD
   Blueprint for Secure Cloud. Note every concrete value they name: a number of days, a threshold, a list of
   roles, an authentication strength, a rule that must be set to Block.
3. **Choose what to write:**

| What the benchmark asks | What you write |
| --- | --- |
| What an existing test checks | A shim: a test with its own ID, title, `Control` and guide whose body returns the result of the existing test |
| The same check with a different value, which the existing test takes as a parameter | A shim that passes the value, with the benchmark's value as the default of its own parameter |
| Something no test checks, or a rule no parameter covers | A test of its own. Read the data with the helpers in `powershell/internal/services/<service>/`, and move a helper there when another suite has the code you need; don't copy another test's logic |

A shim for ASD's lockout requirement, which asks for what CIS 5.2.3.8 checks with a lower maximum:

```powershell
function Test-MtAsdSmartLockoutThreshold {
    <# ...help that says what ASD asks and which test this runs... #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'ASD.ISM-1403',
        Title = 'User accounts are protected by lockout mechanisms aligned to a maximum of five failed logon attempts.',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'password-protection',
        Area = 'authentication',
        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
        Severity = 'Medium',
        UserImpact = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre = ('T1110.001', 'T1110.003'),
        Control = ('ism:ISM-1403', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-7'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        Author = 'jusso-dev'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # The most failed sign-ins allowed before an account is locked. ASD sets five; CIS allows ten.
        [ValidateRange(1, 50)]
        [int] $MaximumLockoutThreshold = 5
    )

    return Test-MtCisSmartLockoutThreshold -MaximumLockoutThreshold $MaximumLockoutThreshold
}
```

A shim:

- declares the same values as the test it calls for `Product`, `RelatedProduct`, `Feature`, `Area`,
  `ResourceType`, `Severity`, `UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost`, `Mitre`, `Service`, `License`, `Permission`,
  `TenantType`, `Cloud`, `Platform`, `Lifecycle`, `LongRunning` and `Exclusive`. Its own are `Id`, `Title`,
  `Control`, `Author`, `Contributor` and its parameters.
- names the requirement it implements first in `Control`, and that requirement is not added to the `Control` of
  the test it calls, so a run reports it once.
- calls a test that is not a shim itself, and passes only parameters that test declares.
- says in its guide what the benchmark asks and links the test it runs by its ID.

`powershell/tests/general/TestShims.Tests.ps1` finds every built-in test whose body is a single `return` of
another built-in test's function and fails when one of these is not true. The result text comes from the test
that is called, so write that test's messages without naming its benchmark.

content.content:
# AGENTS.md

Maester is a PowerShell framework for monitoring Microsoft 365 security
configuration, with its own test engine. Pester is used only for the module's unit tests
and to run users' Pester-format custom tests. Requires PowerShell 7.4+. Monorepo: `powershell/` (module source),
`tests/` (security checks shipped to users), `src/Maester.Engine/` (C# engine core,
built DLL committed in `powershell/lib/`), `build/`, `website/` (Docusaurus,
maester.dev), `report/` (React app that builds the HTML report template).

## Two unrelated test trees — don't mix them

- `tests/` — Maester **security checks** that ship to end-user tenants, run via
  `Invoke-Maester`. Each check is a native test: `tests/<suite>/[<service>/]Test.<ID>.ps1`
  (one function with a `[MaesterTest(...)]` attribute) plus `Test.<ID>.md`. No
  `*.Tests.ps1` wrappers, no connection/licence guards, no outer try/catch: declare
  `Service`/`License` and the engine handles them. Scaffold with `New-MtTest`,
  validate with `Get-MtTest <ID>` (`Get-MtTest -Path` applies the rules of a custom test
  and does not report a missing attribute), run with `Invoke-MtTest -Path`; `Convert-MtTest`
  converts users' Pester-format tests. New MT.xxxx checks go here; follow
  `.github/skills/maester-test-expert/SKILL.md` and `website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx`,
  and choose the attribute values with `website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md`
  (see "Reviewing a test's attributes" below).
- `powershell/tests/` — **unit tests for the module itself**.

## Commands

- Unit tests: `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1` — run before pushing. These enforce
  naming, exports, help, and PSScriptAnalyzer conventions; fix what they flag.
- Build module: `./build/Build-MaesterModule.ps1`; validate: `./build/Test-MaesterModuleOutput.ps1`
- Website: `cd website && npm ci && npm start` · Report: `cd report && npm ci && npm run build`
When you write, change or review a test, check its attributes against the rubric as a separate
step, after the code review and before you approve or hand off:

1. Read the test's `.ps1` and `.md` and state in one sentence what it checks and what the fix is.
2. For each attribute that is new or changed, decide whether the declared value fits the rubric. A
   value fails only when the rubric clearly gives a different one; say which value and which rule.
3. Fail the review if any value does not fit. Do not approve with a note to fix it later.

Three things enforce this, in order:

- `powershell/tests/general/NativeTestAttributes.Tests.ps1` fails on anything mechanical: a missing
  attribute, a key that is not in the taxonomy, a retired ATT&CK technique, a taxonomy tag on a
  built-in test.
- The `attribute-review` workflow (`.github/workflows/attribute-review.yaml`) runs a reviewer model
  against the rubric on every pull request that adds a test or changes one of these attributes, and
  fails the check with the value it expected and the reason. It calls the Claude API with the
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` secret; without the secret it reports that the review was skipped. To run
  the same review locally before pushing, set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and run
  `./build/review/Invoke-MtAttributeReview.ps1 -BaseRef origin/main -OutputPath ./TestResults`
  (`TestResults/` is ignored by git; without `-OutputPath` the report is written to the current
  folder).
- The person or agent reviewing the pull request applies the same rubric and is the last word. A
  maintainer who disagrees with the workflow can apply the `attribute-review-override` label and
  should say why in the pull request.

## Labelling pull requests, issues and discussions

content.content:
## When to Use This Skill

- Creating a new Maester security check
- Editing or refactoring an existing check
- Adding or correcting a check's attributes: product, feature, area, resource type, severity, user impact,
  implementation cost, ATT&CK techniques, service or licence declarations
- Writing or updating a check's `.md` (description, remediation, result template)
- Reviewing a check for correctness, attributes that fit the rubric, or documentation completeness
- Debugging a failing, erroring or skipped check
- Writing or converting a user's custom test (`custom/` folder)

**Do NOT use this skill for:**

- Editing EIDSCA tests by hand -- `tests/eidsca/Test.EIDSCA.*` are generated by `build/eidsca/Update-EidscaTests.ps1`
  from templates in `build/eidsca/templates/`. Change the generator or its data.
- Editing ORCA tests by hand -- `tests/orca/Test.ORCA.*` (header "Generated by ./build/orca/Update-OrcaTests.ps1")
  and `powershell/internal/generated/orca/check-ORCA*.ps1` are generated. Change the generator.
- Editing `website/docs/tests/` -- test pages are generated from the test files by
  `website/scripts/generate-test-docs.mjs`.
- Unit tests of the module itself (`powershell/tests/`).

## Prerequisites
### Attribute and files
- [ ] `Test.<Id>.ps1` and `Test.<Id>.md` in the right suite folder; ID unique and not reused.
- [ ] `Id`, `Title`, `Product`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType`, `Severity`, `Mitre`, `Service`, `Author` set;
      values constant.

input.content:
---
name: map-benchmarks-to-existing-tests
description: Benchmark tests that duplicate another suite's check must be shims; review every new test for duplicates against the benchmark's own sources
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When a benchmark suite (CIS, CISA, ASD, ...) needs a check that another suite's test already does, the new test is a **shim**: own Id, Title, Control, guide; body is `return <other test's function>` (with a parameter when the benchmark names a different value, e.g. ASD lockout 5 vs CIS 10). A check of its own only when the benchmark's own sources (audit/assessment guidance, reference configuration such as ASD Blueprint) ask for something different. Generic helpers never carry a suite name (`Get-MtAsd*`); they go in `internal/services/<service>/`. Decided 2026-10-29 on PR 2552; written into AGENTS.md ("Reviewing a test for duplicates"), the writing-tests guide ("Tests that another suite already has"), the maester-test-expert skill/agents, and enforced by `powershell/tests/general/TestShims.Tests.ps1`.

**Why:** the owner caught that my first review of PR 2552 would have accepted the ASD tests as written, duplicating CIS/CISA logic. Shims keep one implementation while each benchmark keeps its own row (with its Benchmark facts such as E8 maturity level). Mapping a Control onto another suite's test alone loses that, and Maester has no framework selector.

**How to apply:** in every test review or authoring task, search all suites for the same setting first, read the benchmark's primary sources, and fail a review that re-implements an existing check without a reason from those sources. Related: [[maester-3-design]].

A proposal for a new benchmark gets no suite label until that suite exists; mention it in the
report so a maintainer can add one to `.github/labels.json`.

`suite: cis`, `suite: cisa`, `suite: eidsca`, `suite: orca`: the PR adds or changes checks in
`tests/<suite>/**` or changes that suite's generator under `build/<suite>/**`, or the item is
about that benchmark's mapping, content or permissions. A one-line attribute alignment in
another suite's check does not add that suite. The MT checks under `tests/maester/**` and the AD
checks under `tests/ad/**` have no suite label; `product:` already covers them.

input.content:
Thanks @jusso-dev. The framework files and the suite plumbing are well done. I've pushed a refactor to your branch. The main change: where ASD asks for what another suite already checks, the ASD test now runs that suite's test instead of carrying its own copy.

**What ASD's sources say.** I checked each control against the ISM (September 2026), the [Essential Eight assessment process guide](https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/essential-eight/essential-eight-assessment-process-guide) and the [ASD Blueprint for Secure Cloud](https://blueprint.asd.gov.au/). The ISM text is generic, and where ASD does get specific, it matches an existing test:

- **ISM-1504** asks for MFA for all human users of online services and names the factors, not the policy design. That is CIS.M365.5.2.2.2.
- **ISM-1872** applies to privileged and unprivileged users alike. The Blueprint meets it with one policy for all users and all resources that requires the built-in Phishing-resistant MFA strength. That is CISA.MS.AAD.3.1.
- **ISM-1649**: the assessment guide describes just-in-time as access granted "immediately before that access is required and for only as long as it is required". The Blueprint makes every Entra role eligible-only, with permanent active assignments only for break glass accounts. That is CIS.M365.5.3.1. The earlier check failed only permanent assignments, so a six-month active assignment passed.
- **ISM-1403** is CIS.M365.5.2.3.8 with a maximum of 5 instead of 10. The Blueprint also sets 5.

**Shims.** Those four tests are now shims. Each has its own ID, title, `Control` and guide, and its body returns the other test's result, e.g. `return Test-MtCisMfaForEveryUser` or `return Test-MtCisSmartLockoutThreshold -MaximumLockoutThreshold $MaximumLockoutThreshold`. Each ASD requirement keeps its own row, with its maturity level, and there's one implementation per setting. `powershell/tests/general/TestShims.Tests.ps1` finds every shim and fails when:

- its attributes differ from the test it calls;
- it calls a test that doesn't exist, or that is itself a shim;
- it passes a parameter that test doesn't declare;
- its requirement is also on that test's `Control`;
- its guide doesn't name that test.

The rule is now written down for future tests, under [Tests that another suite already has](https://maester.dev/docs/next/writing-tests#tests-that-another-suite-already-has), in `contributing.md`, in `AGENTS.md` ("Reviewing a test for duplicates") and in the maester-test-expert skill and agents.

**Removed and renamed**

- **ASD.ISM-1173 is removed.** ASD assesses ISM-1173 and ISM-0974 by watching a sign-in to a workstation, not to an online service. MFA for admins in online services is covered by ISM-1504 and ISM-1872, which apply to all users.
- **ASD.ISM-0445 is now ASD.ISM-1175.** The assessment guide tests ISM-1175 by listing the privileged accounts that have an email address, which is what this check does. ISM-0445 stays as its second `Control`.
- **CIS.M365.5.3.1 and 5.3.3 are back to `main`.** The ISM-1649 requirement now lives on the shim. CIS 5.3.3 requires weekly or monthly access reviews where ISM-1647 allows 12 months, so a CIS failure doesn't mean ISM-1647 fails.
- **`Get-MtAsdMfaPolicy` is removed.** It repeated MT.1006 and MT.1007.
- **`Get-MtAsdPrivilegedUser` is now `Get-MtPrivilegedRoleUser`**, in `internal/services/entra`. It also counts members of role-assignable groups, so an admin who holds a role through a group is no longer missed. It reads the privileged roles with the same beta `$filter=isPrivileged eq true` call as CIS 5.3.1, because `$select=isPrivileged` on v1.0 returns 400 (MT.1209 notes this). ISM-1648 and the mailbox check would have errored on that call.
- **ASR:** reading the rules moved to `Get-MtIntuneAsrRule` in `internal/services/intune`, so MT.1178 can use it later. `Test-MtAsdAsrRule` now takes several rules.

**Fixes from ASD's assessment guide**

- **ISM-1667** also needs *Block Office communication application from creating child processes* (`26190899-…`). The guide lists both rules.
- **ISM-1668** also needs *Block executable content from email client and webmail* (`BE9BA2D9-…`).
- **ISM-1672** now needs Macro Runtime Scan Scope set to all documents. ASD's [macro guide](https://www.cyber.gov.au/publication/restricting-microsoft-office-macros) and the Blueprint both set that. The low-trust scope scans only files with the Mark of the Web, whose macros ISM-1488 already blocks.
- **ISM-1654:** the Blueprint removes IE11 with a platform script, which Maester can't read, so a Blueprint tenant fails this check. The result and the guide now say so, and explain how to turn the test off with a reason.
- **ISM-1648:** Severity and ImplementationCost are now Medium, as the attribute review asked.
- **CISA.MS.AAD.3.1** now matches the built-in strength by ID, and accepts a custom strength limited to Windows Hello for Business, FIDO2 and certificate-based MFA, as ScubaGear does. Before, any custom strength named "Phishing-resistant MFA" passed, whatever methods it allowed.

**Also:**

- Merged `main` and reverted the generated `Invoke-Maester.mdx`.
- Regenerated the test builder and golden data.
- Updated the titles to the September 2026 ISM wording ("human users").
- Added `AsdChecks.Tests.ps1`, which mocks Graph and covers the changed logic.
- Added a `suite: asd` label.

Two things for you:

1. **A tenant run.** The three Graph behaviours you flagged still need one: `signInActivity` inside the `$batch` (ISM-1648), `$expand=assignments` on `configurationPolicies`, and the `isof()` filter on `deviceConfigurations` (ISM-1695). Could you run `Invoke-Maester -Suite asd` against a tenant and post the results?
2. **The PR description.** It still lists 15 checks with ISM-1173 and ISM-0445. It's now 14, and ISM-0445 is ISM-1175.

The refactor and the new guidance are done locally on the #2552 branch. Nothing is committed or pushed yet. The full unit test run is still going, and I'll commit and push once it passes.

**The ASD tests**
- **Four are now shims** that return another suite's result:
  - ISM-1504 runs CIS 5.2.2.2.
  - ISM-1872 runs CISA 3.1.
  - ISM-1649 runs CIS 5.3.1.
  - ISM-1403 runs CIS 5.2.3.8 with a maximum of 5.
- **Dropped or renamed:** ISM-1173 is gone. ISM-0445 is now ISM-1175. CIS 5.3.1 and 5.3.3 are back to `main`, since the shims now carry the ASD requirements.
- **Helpers:** `Get-MtAsdMfaPolicy` is gone. `Get-MtAsdPrivilegedUser` is now the general `Get-MtPrivilegedRoleUser` in `internal/services/entra`, and it also counts admins who get their role through a group. Reading the ASR rules moved to `services/intune`.
- **A real bug I found along the way:** the old privileged-user helper selected `isPrivileged` on Graph v1.0, which Graph rejects with a 400. ISM-1648 and the mailbox check would have errored on their first tenant run.
- **Intune fixes against ASD's assessment guide:**
  - ISM-1667 and ISM-1668 now require both rules each.
  - ISM-1672 now requires macro scanning for all documents.
  - ISM-1654: the result now explains that removing Internet Explorer, as ASD's Blueprint does, also meets the control.
- **CISA 3.1** now matches the built-in phishing-resistant strength by ID. Before, a custom strength *named* "Phishing-resistant MFA" passed even if it allowed push notifications.

**The guidance for writing and reviewing tests with agents**
- **`AGENTS.md`** has a new "Reviewing a test for duplicates" step, before the attribute review. It tells an agent to:
  - search every suite for a test that reads the same setting;
  - read the benchmark's own sources (assessment guidance, reference build), not only the requirement's one-line text;
  - write a shim when the benchmark asks for the same thing;
  - fail the review when a test re-implements a check without a reason from those sources, or when a general helper is named after a suite.

  Every coding agent in the repo reads this file.
- **The same rule, with an example,** is in the writing-tests guide ("Tests that another suite already has"), the contributing guide, the attribute rubric, and the test-expert skill and agents. The `.claude` copies are regenerated from those sources.
- **A new unit test, `TestShims.Tests.ps1`,** finds every shim automatically. It fails if a shim's attributes differ from the test it calls, if it calls a missing test or another shim, or if the requirement it implements is also listed on the test it calls. I checked that it catches a changed Severity and a duplicated requirement.

I also added a `suite: asd` label and `AsdChecks.Tests.ps1`, which exercises the changed logic with mocked Graph data. All 14 ASD tests validate with `Get-MtTest`, and nothing has run against a tenant.

The PR comment for jusso-dev is drafted in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-merill-github-maester/cad13d5b-f6a5-465e-ab70-f69ded04259c/scratchpad/comment-2552.md`. It asks them for a tenant run and an updated PR description. I'll show it to you before posting.

refactor(asd): run the CIS and CISA checks ASD asks for, and add the shim rule

Where ASD's sources (the ISM, the Essential Eight assessment process guide and
the ASD Blueprint for Secure Cloud) ask for what another suite already checks,
the ASD test is now a shim that returns that test's result:

- ISM-1504 runs CIS.M365.5.2.2.2
- ISM-1872 runs CISA.MS.AAD.3.1
- ISM-1649 runs CIS.M365.5.3.1 (a time-bound active assignment is standing access)
- ISM-1403 runs CIS.M365.5.2.3.8 with a maximum of 5

ISM-1173 is removed: ASD assesses it at workstation sign-in. ISM-0445 becomes
ISM-1175, which ASD tests by listing privileged accounts with an email address.
CIS.M365.5.3.1 and 5.3.3 are back to main.

Get-MtAsdMfaPolicy is removed. Get-MtAsdPrivilegedUser becomes
Get-MtPrivilegedRoleUser in internal/services/entra; it counts members of
role-assignable groups and reads privileged roles with the beta isPrivileged
filter, since $select=isPrivileged on v1.0 returns 400. Reading ASR rules moves
to Get-MtIntuneAsrRule in internal/services/intune.

Fixes from the assessment guide: ISM-1667 and ISM-1668 need both of their ASR
rules, ISM-1672 needs macro scanning for all documents, ISM-1654 explains IE11
removal, ISM-1648 Severity and ImplementationCost are Medium. CISA.MS.AAD.3.1
matches the built-in strength by ID and accepts a phishing-resistant custom
strength, as ScubaGear does.

The shim rule is written into the writing-tests guide, contributing.md,
AGENTS.md (Reviewing a test for duplicates), the attribute rubric and the
maester-test-expert skill and agents. TestShims.Tests.ps1 checks every shim
against the test it calls. Adds a suite: asd label, AsdChecks.Tests.ps1, and
regenerates the test builder and golden data.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
